purpose: Zero-byte placeholder that reserves the .commandcode/taste/taste.md path in the repository so the Command Code CLI's per-repository 'taste' notes location exists and is tracked by git; it currently carries no guidance content at all (0 bytes, and its sha256 is the canonical empty-file hash e3b0c442...b7852b855).
platform_assumptions: Lives under a dot-directory (.commandcode) that is a Unix-style hidden folder; the Command Code CLI ('cmd', listed in README.md as a provider using headless print mode) owns .commandcode/ in the working tree.
feature_notes: File is completely empty: 0 bytes, 0 lines, no markdown heading, no front matter, no text.

Because .gitignore in this same bundle does not exclude .commandcode/, this empty file is committed deliberately to keep the directory present in checkouts (git does not track empty directories otherwise).

The Command Code provider is described in README.md as command `cmd`, 'headless print mode (NDJSON events), one run per turn, with a session mod for approvals'; this taste directory belongs to that CLI's own on-disk convention, not to Droppy Code's Swift sources.
unresolved_questions: Nothing in this bundle documents what the Command Code CLI writes into taste.md or when; the file is empty so its schema and format cannot be determined from it. Cannot tell from this file alone whether it is read at runtime by the app or only by the external `cmd` binary.

purpose: Git ignore list for the Droppy Code Xcode project: excludes macOS Finder metadata, Xcode build and per-user state artifacts, an Xcode explicit-modules compiler-cache mishap directory, the generated website app captures, Cloudflare wrangler state and Python bytecode caches.
platform_assumptions: `.DS_Store` is a macOS Finder artifact.
`DerivedData/`, `xcuserdata/` and `*.xcuserstate` are Xcode-specific build and per-user UI state.

The inline comment says an Xcode explicit-modules build once wrote its compiler cache into DroppyCode.xcodeproj/-Xcc, so the `-Xcc/` pattern guards against a clang flag being taken as a directory name.
`build.noindex/` is the Spotlight-skipped release folder README.md names ('The disk image lands in build.noindex/, a folder Spotlight skips').
feature_notes: Exact 13 lines in order: `.DS_Store`, `build/`, `DerivedData/`, `xcuserdata/`, `*.xcuserstate`, `build.noindex/`, the comment `# An Xcode explicit-modules build once wrote its compiler cache into DroppyCode.xcodeproj/-Xcc.`, `-Xcc/`, a blank line, the comment `# The site's app captures are generated by scripts/website_captures.py and served from R2.`, `website/assets/app/`, `.wrangler/`, `__pycache__/`.
Names the generator script by path: scripts/website_captures.py produces website/assets/app/ captures which are served from Cloudflare R2, hence ignored here.

Notably does NOT ignore `.commandcode/`, `DroppyCode.xcodeproj/`, `.build/`, `Package.resolved` or `node_modules/`; the project is generated by xcodegen from project.yml per README.md yet the .xcodeproj is not ignored.
322 bytes over 13 lines, CRLF line terminators.
unresolved_questions: Whether DroppyCode.xcodeproj is committed or merely un-ignored cannot be confirmed from this file; README.md says `xcodegen generate` produces it, which would normally suggest ignoring it, so the absence of that rule is unexplained by this bundle.

purpose: The repository's working agreement for coding agents, titled '# AGENTS.md - DroppyCode agent workflow': mandatory git-worktree isolation, the four-layer source dependency rule, what a Hydra 'head' may and may not do, a hard ban on unprompted relaunches, the glab squash-merge policy, and the release-credits requirement.
calls_into: DroppyCode/App/HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift (cited as the example of splitting a Core file that needs the provider registry into an extension one layer up)
side_effects: Prescribes `git fetch origin --prune`, `git worktree add -b <branch> ~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug> origin/main`, `git worktree remove --force ~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>` and `git worktree prune`.
Prescribes `xcodebuild -project DroppyCode.xcodeproj -scheme DroppyCode -configuration Debug build` as the only verification step.
Prescribes `glab mr create --squash-before-merge` and `glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch`.
Prescribes `python3 scripts/release_credits.py`, whose --check mode gates scripts/publish_release.sh.
platform_assumptions: Hardcoded macOS home path `/Users/jordyspruit/Desktop/DroppyCode` as the owner's checkout that must never be edited directly.
Worktree root `~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>` under the Unix home directory.
`xcodebuild` plus an Xcode project and scheme, i.e. a macOS-only toolchain.
`glab` (GitLab CLI) against a GitLab-hosted project, and `python3` on PATH.
ui_elements: States the app's About cards ignore the `### Thanks` heading, so adding Thanks changes nothing on Settings > About.
feature_notes: Exact worktree path template: `~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>`, branch created with `git worktree add -b <branch> ... origin/main` (or the agreed base branch).

Four-layer rule verbatim: DroppyCode/Core (models, pure support) reaches into nothing else; DroppyCode/Services (Git, Store, Providers) and DroppyCode/UI (Chrome, Common, Markdown, Theme, Sound) reach only into Core; DroppyCode/App (entry, model, runtime, windows, captures and every feature view) reaches into everything. New code goes in the lowest layer whose dependencies it has.
'There is no test target and no test scripts; the build is the check' - the upstream has no unit tests for the port to mirror.

Hydra head rule: 'A head never builds or otherwise verifies: no xcodebuild, no scripts/quick_run.sh, no check command.' It edits the files the lead briefed it on and reports, nothing more; the lead runs the one build that proves the change, in the checkout, after the heads report.

Relaunch ban is absolute: NEVER run scripts/quick_run.sh or otherwise quit/relaunch Droppy Code unless asked in that moment; building inside the worktree is fine, installing to /Applications and relaunching is not; 'Finish', 'merge', 'done' or 'test it' do not imply relaunch.

History facts stated: 4,292 commits on GitLab, mostly tiny Hydra head commits plus one merge commit per MR; the GitLab project's `merge_method` is `merge` and `squash_option` is `default_off`; every team merge MUST land as exactly one commit on main.
History rewriting (`rebase -i`, `filter-branch`, `filter-repo`, force-push to main) is forbidden; squash applies to new merges only. Never merge locally into main and never push straight to main.
Thanks bullet format is exact: `- Name (@gitlab-handle): what they did (!MR).`, placed after Refinements in every `## [x.y.z]` entry that ships outside work.
An outside merge request that lands between releases is added to `## [Unreleased]`'s Thanks right away rather than at release time.
unresolved_questions: scripts/quick_run.sh, scripts/release_credits.py and scripts/publish_release.sh are referenced but not in this bundle, so their exact flags beyond `--check` are unknown.
That quick_run.sh installs the built app to /Applications is implied by the relaunch rule's prose rather than confirmed by the script itself.

purpose: AppDelegate is the NSApplicationDelegate/UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate for the macOS app: it runs the launch prologue in applicationDidFinishLaunching (as of B3: reconfigure the shared URLCache to memory-only, wire the Markdown hydra-delegation-card renderer, register itself as the notification-centre delegate, take its AppModel handle from WindowManager.shared, short-circuit into a capture run if one was requested, show the main window, open the last thread, gate the welcome tour, kick off async bootstrap and background update checks, and handle a post-install relaunch), and it owns the remaining AppKit lifecycle hooks: bringing the main window back on Dock reopen, deferring Quit up to 4 minutes while a Hydra team merge is in flight, running the exactly-three-step termination cleanup (save, flush the token ledger, stop every MCP server), and routing notification presentation/response to the right chat thread or to Settings > About. It is the single seam where AppKit's OS-level app lifecycle meets the rest of the app's state (AppModel, WindowManager, MCPHub, TokenLedger, UpdateChecker/AppUpdater), so every change to it is a change to when and in what order those systems start up and shut down.

feature_notes: NEW (B3): the first two executable statements of applicationDidFinishLaunching (preceded by a 3-line explanatory comment) reconfigure the process-wide URLCache to memory-only: `URLCache.shared = URLCache(memoryCapacity: 8 * 1024 * 1024, diskCapacity: 0)`. The comment states this stops the shared cache from writing a SQLite commit for every cached response (API calls, the MCP proxy's streams, link titles), which the source describes as 'a third of the app's disk writes while a team ran.' This is significant beyond this file: porting/engineering_decisions.md ED-118 (item O-33, F.HTTP's URLCache.shared cache policy) explicitly records the cache size cut-off as PARKED ('no size cut-off') and cache persistence as unresolved ('memory only until the owner answers the persistence question'). This B3 source change is new, concrete SOURCE FACT evidence that answers exactly that parked question with a specific number (8 MiB memory, 0 disk) - it does not by itself amend ED-118, but the port's F.HTTP cache in src/Marrow.Core/Port/Http.cs should be revisited against it.

NEW (B3): the next statement, `MarkdownDelegationCard.render = { AnyView(HydraDelegationBlock(json: $0, sent: $1)) }`, wires the App-layer HydraDelegationBlock view into the UI-layer MarkdownView's renderer for 'hydra'/'hydra-leaving' fenced code blocks (DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:324-333, :507-509). This is dependency injection done specifically to respect the source's own layering rule (Core depends on nothing in the app; UI depends only on Core; App depends on everything) since MarkdownView (UI) cannot import HydraDelegationBlock (App) directly. Before this line runs, any such code block would render as a plain CodeBlock. Both MarkdownDelegationCard (as a hook point) and HydraDelegationBlock already have C# counterparts (src/Marrow.UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.cs, src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/TimelineRows.cs); only the AppDelegate-side wiring statement itself is still unported, because src/Marrow.App/AppDelegate.cs does not exist yet (unit App.AppDelegate is status TODO in porting/deps/units.json).

purpose: This AppModel extension is the Hydra auto-merge coordinator: when "Merge when the team is done" (settings.hydraAutoMerge) is on, it lands a finished lead's job and its heads' files as a commit built from a scratch-index snapshot, on a stable per-chat hydra/<slug>-<6 chars of the lead id> branch (or on the checkout's current non-default branch), pushes it (force-pushed when it is the chat's own branch), opens a merge request through glab/gh/tea and merges it, then brings the checkout up to date without ever changing branch. It also decides which files are the job's (turn touched paths, head landings and head/lead tool edits, plus a checkout sweep since the first turn's checkpoint, minus other chats' reserved or blocking claims unless this job edited the file itself), splits the job per sidebar project, serialises merges app-wide (a job that finishes while another merges now waits in a 400 ms poll instead of being skipped), retries self-clearing failures quietly a minute later, and reports outcomes as HydraMergeRecord entries plus Hydra notes in the lead's timeline. At B3 the whole 'held' mechanism (a job waiting on another chat's files) is gone.

On the chat's own branch it fetches origin and, when origin/<target> moved past HEAD, builds the tree on the remote with captureTree(paths:onto:from:); nil (overlapping changes) fails non-retryably with 'Hydra did not merge: `<target>` changed the same lines.'; the rebased tree's three-way results (merged) are later written into the checkout by syncDefaultBranch. alreadyOnMain now compares with the parent's tree (remote or HEAD). The diff and commit parent are the parent, the commit message is reused when the patch is unchanged, and a HEAD that moved after commitWork restarts the loop instead of failing; after three tries 'Hydra did not merge: the checkout kept moving.' (retryable).

The session is left to restart itself: the runtime launches the next turn with the pair's head definitions on its own.

hydraLead model resolution: the pair's orchestratorModel looked up in the provider's catalogue; with no lead model and a provider switch, that provider's default model; otherwise the chat's own model checked against the provider. The returned id falls back to option?.id ?? pair.orchestratorModel ?? (switchesProvider ? nil : thread.model).

hydraLead effort: the pair's orchestratorEffort wins whenever option?.efforts.contains(chosen) ?? true, so an unknown model does not block it; otherwise the remembered preference's effort only when the option's efforts contain it, else nil.
hydraLead fastMode = (option?.supportsFast ?? false) && preference.fastMode.

updateHydraPair only acts when settings actually changed (pair != before); it moves every chat with hydraIsOn leading with that pair onto the new lead model/effort/fastMode and re-remembers them, skipping chats already matching. A pair whose provider changed unpins those chats (hydraPairID = nil) instead of switching their provider, because a chat does not change provider under a conversation.

removeHydraPair unpins every thread pointing at the pair, clears settings.lastHydraPairID when it matched, and clears the pair from every Project.hydraPairID so the project's new chats fall back to the remembered pair.
setHydraPair(_:forProject:) only affects new chats in that project; open chats are untouched, and nil removes the rule.
leaveHydraPair clears the thread's hydraPairID and settings.lastHydraPairID but leaves Hydra itself as Settings has it, with heads back on the chat's own model and effort.

purpose: The @MainActor @Observable AppModel is the app's single library object: it owns the projects and threads arrays (the source of truth persisted to library.json), mirrors them into per-item ObservedValue cells (projectCells, threadCells, childCells, selectionCells) so a sidebar row, chat header or panel re-renders only when its own item changes, and keeps a ThreadIndex of positions for O(1) lookup. It runs the launch bootstrap (document prefetch, keychain, login environment, Hydra copy sweep and merge resume, the 300 s merge-sweep loop, provider refresh and catalog loads, and from B3 the background CLI self-update task, then the orphaned-attachment sweep), every thread and project mutation (new/forward/move/rename/archive/settle/reopen/delete, helpers and Hydra-head panels, worktree creation, project scripts), idle-runtime release after 600 s, attention handling (notifications, dock badge, unread marks), text-engine selection, and library persistence, which in B3 is a throttled save (400 ms minimum wait, at most one write per 4 s) plus a synchronous quit-time write. The file also holds ProjectFile, which reads project scripts from droppy-code.json and maps their icon names to SF Symbols.

feature_notes: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE 1, library save throttle (B3 111, 1298-1318): scheduleSave no longer cancels and restarts a 400 ms debounce. B3: 'guard persistenceEnabled, saveTask == nil else { return }' - while a save is pending, further calls do nothing (the pending save picks up every change because saveLibrary reads projects and threads when it fires). The wait is 'max(.milliseconds(400), .seconds(4) - sinceLast)' where sinceLast = ContinuousClock.now - lastLibrarySave, or 60 s when no save has happened yet in this process. The task sleeps, returns if cancelled or self is gone, sets saveTask = nil, then calls saveLibrary(). saveLibrary() now stamps 'lastLibrarySave = .now' after its persistenceEnabled guard, so the direct saves (settle 815, reopen 834, delete 965) also push the next scheduled save out to 4 s after them. Observable result: the first save after a change goes out 400 ms later, library.json is written at most once per 4 s, and a steady stream of changes is still saved (every ~4 s) instead of never. The doc comment (1298-1303) cites the reason: a busy team rewrote the file on every status change, 'over two gigabytes in an hour and a quarter (September 22)'. saveBeforeQuit is unchanged: it still cancels saveTask, nils it and latches persistence off.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE 2, CLI self-update at launch (B3 275-282): after the zai catalog load and before the capture guard and orphan-attachment sweep, bootstrap starts 'Task { [providers] in for provider in [ProviderKind.claude, .codex] where providers.status(provider).isInstalled { await providers.updateCLIIfDue(provider) } }'. The task is not awaited, not stored and never cancelled; claude is handled before codex, each installed check made when the loop reaches it. The comment states the reason: the CLIs run headless never update themselves and a model newer than the installed CLI fails outright; 'Their own updaters run here, in the background, at most every twelve hours; a newer version reloads its catalog.' The 12-hour gate, the capture-run guard, the user binary-path exemption, the 'update' child process and the catalog reload all live in ProviderRegistry.updateCLIIfDue (ProviderRegistry.swift:497, read here only at 470-560 for context and owned by another bundle).

NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, capture guard rename: the four guards 'WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled' became 'CaptureRun.isEnabled' (bootstrap 285, threadNeedsAttention 1168, requestNotificationPermission 1250, notify 1258). purpose: Holds Droppy Code's per-Mac preference model: the @MainActor @Observable final class AppSettings. It owns every user-defaults key (private enum Key, :117-180), and each stored property writes itself back in its own didSet with no save step. init() (:707-790) reads every key with its shipped default from `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`. It also defines the settings-facing enums TextGenerationChoice, ThreadFinishAction, SidebarMode and ActivityThreadStyle with their user-visible titles and detail strings, and the ModelPin and ModelPreference value types. It is the single owner of the four provider API keys (DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai, Command Code). They are read from the Keychain lazily and once, off the main thread through Task.detached, with an isReadingKeychain guard so the fill never writes back. Edits go to the Keychain, and a plaintext defaults copy is kept only when the Keychain refuses the key. In B3 the key code goes straight through APIKeychain by ProviderKind, via the new helpers storedKey(for:fallback:) and storeAPIKeyChange(_:from:provider:fallbackKey:), instead of the four per-provider *Keychain wrappers. Finally, it serves as the ProviderSettings the provider registry reads (binary paths, enabled providers, last model and effort, API keys with login-environment fallback), and as the store for Hydra pairs, the composer's model list (15-entry cap) and per-model preferences.

feature_notes: B2 to B3 (churn 42: 10 hunks, +23/-19 lines, 947 to 951 lines): no user-visible or persisted behaviour of AppSettings changed. Every hunk is a refactor that follows two upstream reorganisations elsewhere.

Hunks 1, 9 and 10 (:184, :708, :869): `WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard` became `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`. At B2, WebsiteCaptures.defaults was only a nonisolated read-through to CaptureRun.defaults, and B3 deleted those read-through properties from App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift, so the resolved suite is the same. The capture suite is still 'iordv.droppycode.website-captures' (CaptureRun.swift:40), and the branch is still the user-unreachable capture short circuit that porting/dead_code.md entry 44 lists; that entry still quotes the B2 text and line 183.

Hunks 2 to 5 (the four API-key didSets, now :367-400): each three-line body (guard, <Provider>Keychain.setAPIKey, storeAPIKeyFallback) became one call to the new private storeAPIKeyChange(_:from:provider:fallbackKey:) (:481-487). That helper holds the same guard `!isReadingKeychain, value != oldValue`, calls `APIKeychain.setKey(value, for: provider)` and then `storeAPIKeyFallback(kept ? "" : value, forKey: fallbackKey)`. The provider-to-fallback-key pairing is unchanged (.deepseek/deepseekAPIKey, .meta/metaAPIKey, .zai/zaiAPIKey, .commandcode/commandcodeAPIKey).

Hunks 6 and 7 (readKeys :434-441 plus the new storedKey(for:fallback:) :443-445): the reads now go through `APIKeychain.key(for: provider, fallback: "")` instead of DeepSeekKeychain/MetaKeychain/ZaiKeychain/CommandCodeKeychain.apiKey(fallback: ""). Those four Swift files were deleted in B3, and their account strings moved verbatim into APIKeychain.account(for:) (APIKeychain.swift:26-34), so the same four Keychain items are read and written.

The one real storage-semantics change is outside this file: APIKeychain.set at B3 tries SecItemUpdate first and adds only on errSecItemNotFound (APIKeychain.swift:50-57), where B2 did SecItemDelete then SecItemAdd. AppSettings only sees the Bool it returns and treats it as before. Records whose text says 'delete then add' (PR-PROVAPI-003, PR-PROVREG-088, PR-SETTINGS-272) must be reclassified by the APIKeychain.swift bundle.

purpose: Implements the in-app self-update installer and the observable progress model the About page's version pill renders as a slider. UpdateInstallProgress is a forward-only progress state machine with milestone dots at 0.55, 0.70, 0.86 and 0.96, creep animation for phases without byte progress, haptics at milestones and a post-relaunch celebration sweep. AppUpdater downloads the release .dmg with a delegate-based Downloader, mounts it with hdiutil, copies the .app out with ditto, verifies the Developer ID code signature against team NARHG44L48 and the bundle identifier, checks the version and Gatekeeper, then writes and launches a /bin/sh installer script that waits for the app to quit, swaps bundles with rollback, clears quarantine and reopens the app, while a UserDefaults marker lets the relaunched build finish the progress story.

Creates a staging dir <temp>/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>/ with POSIX permissions 0o700, mounts the image at <staging>/image, copies the .app to <staging>/<running bundle name>, then detaches the image with -force and deletes the .dmg. The detach and delete happen only inside the do/catch after a successful attach (lines 315-327, on success and on "The disk image holds no app." / ditto throw). If `hdiutil attach` fails, line 310 throws "The downloaded disk image could not be opened. \(attach.failureMessage)" before that block, so the downloaded <temp>/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>.dmg and the 0o700 staging dir both stay on disk.

Staging dir leak: nothing in the app ever removes <temp>/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>/ (only the installer script's `rm -rf "$STAGING"` does). Every failure before the script runs leaves it, with the staged .app when the copy happened: attach failure (310), "The disk image holds no app." (318), "The update could not be copied." (329), any verifySignature throw (331), "The downloaded app is version ... not ..." (335), "Gatekeeper did not accept the downloaded app." (339), "Droppy Code cannot replace itself in <parent>..." (378), and a throw from writing the script or process.run().

Writes <staging>/install.sh and <staging>/install.log (`staged.deletingLastPathComponent().appending(path: "install.log")`, line 382), launches /bin/sh install.sh <pid> <staged app> <installed app path> with stdin null and stdout/stderr to the log. Because the log is inside STAGING and every exit path of the script runs `rm -rf "$STAGING"` (the "The app did not quit" timeout at 424, the move-aside failure at 429, the move-into-place failure at 436, and success at 441), the log that receives those messages never survives; there is no persistent install log.

Animation constants: creep tick every 125 ms, each tick advances by (ceiling - fraction) * rate, stops when remaining <= 0.0005; preparing creep toward 0.05 at rate 0.05; unknown-size download creep toward 0.50 at rate 0.012; verifying creep toward 0.68 (verifyEnd - 0.02) at rate 0.12; staging creep toward 0.82 at rate 0.10; begin() sets fraction 0.004; failure reset after 600 ms; handoff terminate delay 350 ms.
feature_notes: begin(): cancels failure reset, phase .preparing, fraction 0.004 (set directly), Haptics .generic, creep toward 0.05 at 0.05.

noteDownloadProgress: .preparing moves to .downloading; any phase other than .downloading returns. downloadFraction <= 0 starts creep toward 0.50 at 0.012 (creep continues if already running since startCreep only updates ceiling/rate when a task exists). Otherwise stops creep and applies 0.05 + (0.55 - 0.05) * min(fraction, 1).

beginVerification / beginStaging / noteHandoff / fail are guarded by isInstallRunning. beginVerification: phase .verifying, apply 0.55, creep to 0.68 at 0.12. beginStaging: phase .staging, apply 0.70, creep to 0.82 at 0.10. noteHandoff: phase .handoff, apply 0.86. fail(): phase .failed, Haptics .levelChange, after 600 ms resets to idle (fraction 0) if still .failed and not cancelled.

apply(): clamps to 0...1, ignores values not greater than the current fraction (forward only), and for every dot crossed (previous < dot && new >= dot) fires Haptics .levelChange for handoffEnd (0.86) and .alignment for the others, unless firesHaptics is false.

Celebration: armCelebration sets hasPendingCelebration; consumePendingCelebration returns false if not armed, else clears it, stops creep, cancels failure reset, phase .celebrating, fraction set directly to 0.86, returns true; finishCelebrationSweep applies 1 without haptics when celebrating; completeCelebration resets to idle when celebrating. Consequence: installDot (0.96, doc "Crossed by the post-relaunch sweep to 100%.") is only ever crossed by finishCelebrationSweep's `apply(1, firesHaptics: false)` (the install path stops at handoffEnd 0.86, and consumePendingCelebration sets 0.86 directly), so installDot never fires a haptic. The only milestone haptics are .alignment at 0.55 and 0.70 and .levelChange at 0.86, during the install.

Note: the order in install() is progress.beginVerification() after download, then stage() (which mounts, copies, verifies signature, version and Gatekeeper), then progress.beginStaging(), then handOff; so the 'verifying' phase covers mount/copy/verify and 'staging' covers handoff preparation.
install(_:): no-op if an install is running or AppInfo.isDevelopment. Errors from any step call progress.fail() and show the 'Update Failed' alert.

handOff: requires the installed app's parent directory to be writable. Arguments to the script: script path, current PID, staged app path, destination (Bundle.main.bundleURL) path. Marker set after process.run(); two tasks: after 25 s, if phase still .handoff, remove the marker and fail(); after 350 ms, NSApp.terminate(nil). Race: the app gives up after `handoffTimeout: TimeInterval = 25` (removes "appUpdater_pendingRelaunchVersion" and fail()) while the script keeps waiting ~60 s (240 x `sleep 0.25`). If the app quits between 25 s and ~60 s the swap and `open "$DEST"` still happen, but the marker is gone, so consumeRelaunchMarker returns false and no celebration plays. Reachable: AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateLater while `model.isAnyHydraMergeRunning`, polling every 250 ms up to a 4 * 60 s deadline (AppDelegate.swift:38-47). If the quit comes after ~60 s the script has already given up and deleted the staged update.

Installer script: trap '' HUP; waits while kill -0 PID succeeds, sleeping 0.25 s, giving up once i > 240 (~60 s) with echo "The app did not quit", rm -rf STAGING, exit 1; BACKUP = <dest dir>/.<dest basename>.previous; rm -rf BACKUP; `if [ -e "$DEST" ]; then mv "$DEST" "$BACKUP" || { echo "Could not move the installed app aside"; rm -rf "$STAGING"; exit 1; } fi` (a missing DEST is NOT an error: the script goes straight on; the failure fires only when that mv fails); `if mv "$NEW" "$DEST"; then rm -rf "$BACKUP"; else echo "Could not move the update into place"; [ -e "$BACKUP" ] && mv "$BACKUP" "$DEST"; rm -rf "$STAGING"; exit 1; fi`; xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine DEST 2>/dev/null; open DEST; rm -rf STAGING. No `set -e`, so xattr or open failures do not stop the final cleanup.

Downloader: URLSessionConfiguration.ephemeral, timeoutIntervalForRequest 30, timeoutIntervalForResource 1800, waitsForConnectivity false, delegateQueue nil; session.finishTasksAndInvalidate() deferred. Progress callback: totalBytesExpectedToWrite <= 0 reports 0, else written/expected. didFinishDownloadingTo moves the temp file synchronously (removing any existing destination first) after checking a 2xx HTTP status. didCompleteWithError only finishes on error; finish() resumes the continuation at most once (it is cleared inside the lock and resumed outside it).
consumeRelaunchMarker drops a stale marker silently, so About then offers the update again.

B1->B2: Added `import Synchronization`. In Downloader the separate `private var continuation`, `private var destination` and `private let lock = NSLock()` were replaced by `private struct State { var continuation: CheckedContinuation<URL, Error>?; var destination: URL? }` held in `private let state = Mutex(State())`, with a new doc comment ('The continuation and the destination share one mutex; the delegate callbacks arrive on URLSession's own queue. The continuation is resumed outside `withLock`.'). download() now sets destination via state.withLock (previously an unlocked assignment) and stores the continuation via state.withLock; finish() takes and clears the continuation via state.withLock; didFinishDownloadingTo reads destination via state.withLock. Behaviour, strings and constants are otherwise unchanged (diff stat 16 insertions, 9 deletions).

feature_notes: isReady = settings.isEnabled(provider) && registry.status(provider).isInstalled. Note this uses status().isInstalled, unlike AppModel.hydraPickerPairs which uses countsAsInstalled, so an unprobed provider is not ready here.
provider(for:) takes the first of a side's providers that is ready and, when the side names models, actually lists one of them (side.models.isEmpty short-circuits that check).
missingProvider ignores whether the model is listed: it reports the first side whose providers are all unready, returning that side's first provider.

resolve builds HydraPair(provider: leadProvider), sets orchestratorModel to the resolved lead model's id and orchestratorEffort from recipe.lead.effort against that model (or the registry default model when the named one was not found), sets workerProvider only when the heads' provider differs from the lead's, sets workerModel/workerEffort the same way for the heads side, and copies recipe.maxHeads.

model(named:) treats each entry of names as a family fragment matched case-insensitively against a ModelOption's name or id; among the matches the highest first version number in the name wins, with ties broken by the later position in registry.models(for:) (options.firstIndex(where:)! > options.firstIndex(where:)!), so a new release moves a recipe up on its own.
The fragments are tried in order and the first fragment with any match returns immediately, so later fragments are pure fallbacks.
version(of:) reads the first [0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)? match in a catalogue name, so 'Gemini 3.8 Flash' gives 3.8; a name with no digits scores -1 in the comparison and loses to any numbered name.
unresolved_questions: The effort(_:for:) helper used for both sides is declared in the companion HydraCookbook file, so how a recipe's effort word maps onto a model's scale is not visible here.
HydraPairRecipe.Side's exact field types (especially the type of `effort`) and the full built-in recipe list are defined elsewhere.
Whether options.firstIndex(where:)! could ever trap is not determinable here; it indexes back into the same `options` array the matches came from, which appears safe but is not proven in this file.

purpose: Defines the @MainActor @Observable class AutoContinue, the runtime service that resumes a chat automatically once its provider's usage-limit window resets: it records limit hits during a turn (noteLimit), decides at turn end whether to start a wait (turnFinished), sleeps until the reset time plus a 60 second margin, posts notices and notifications, then enqueues and immediately sends a fixed continue prompt. It also implements user-driven cancel and hand-off into a new chat.

purpose: A stateless namespace enum that renders the plain-text hand-off prompt placed into a new chat's composer when a chat stopped on its provider's usage limit: it restates the request being answered, up to 40 bullet lines of what the stopped turn had already said and run, and up to 20 changed file paths, then asks the new model to take the work over.

Request block header (exact): "The request it was answering:" followed by a blank line and the request text
Fallback request text (exact): "(the request was not recorded)"
Work block header (exact): "What it had already done in that turn:" followed by a blank line and the bullet lines
Files block header (exact): "Files it had changed:" followed by a blank line and "- " prefixed paths
Closing block (exact): "Take it over from here and finish it, asking me about anything unclear."

Tool bullet prefix (exact, trailing space included): "- It ran: "
Changed-files suffix on a tool bullet (exact): " (changed <suffix>)"
Overflow phrase inside a tool bullet (exact): " and <n> more" where n = seen.count - 5

Blocks are joined with "

"; bullet lines and path lines are joined with "
"; edit paths inside a tool bullet are joined with ", "
feature_notes: The turn scanned is the last one: turn = entries whose turnID == runtime.turns.last?.id; when there is no last turn it falls back to the whole entries list
The request is found by scanning runtime.entries.reversed() (the whole transcript, not just the last turn) for the most recent .user entry and flattening its text
At most 40 bullet lines are produced: the loop breaks once lines.count reaches 40 (guard lines.count < 40 else { break })
Assistant text longer than 400 characters is truncated to String(flat.prefix(400)) and suffixed with the single character U+2026 horizontal ellipsis
Assistant entries whose flattened text is empty are skipped entirely (continue), and do not consume one of the 40 line slots
A tool bullet lists at most 5 distinct changed paths (seen.prefix(5) joined by ", "); beyond that it appends " and N more" where N = seen.count - 5
Distinct paths per tool call are collected in first-seen order with a linear !seen.contains(edit.path) check
The global Files-it-had-changed list collects distinct edit paths across the turn's tool calls and stops at exactly 20, checked both inside the inner edit loop and again after each entry
The work block and the files block are omitted entirely when their lists are empty; the opening, request and closing blocks are always present
Entry contents other than .user, .assistant and .tool are ignored (default: break in the switch)
flatten collapses all whitespace and newlines: components(separatedBy: .whitespacesAndNewlines), drop empty pieces, join with a single space, so multi-line messages become one line

Whether call.title is already user-facing prose (it is embedded verbatim after "- It ran: ") or a raw tool identifier cannot be determined from this file
The request scan ignores turn boundaries, so it picks the newest user message anywhere in the transcript; whether that can ever differ from the last turn's request is not determinable here

purpose: ThreadRuntime.swift is the per-chat live engine: the @MainActor @Observable final class ThreadRuntime owns one thread's timeline entries and turn records, its provider session (warm-up, SessionSignature-driven relaunch, resume or start-over, epoch-guarded event handling through handle(_:)), the follow-up queue with drag bundling, revert and resend over git checkpoints with optional file restore, the diff caches and change stats, command-tree snapshots that recover shell edits, delta flush pacing (StreamLoad), persistence (scheduleSave, saveNow, snapshotForPersistence) and the whole Hydra lead/head machinery (streamed delegation-block parsing, HydraDelegationBudget, batches, the waiting queue, report turns, native heads, merge-state flags). The file also declares TimelineEntry, ReplyQuote (excerpt, peel), DraftCommand, ComposerDraft (outgoingText), PromptEdit, RuntimePhase, the private TimelineItem.Content.appendStreamed extension and the rehearsal extension used by website captures and native-head timelines. At B3 (1.7.0) it gains a recovery path for a CLI that is too old for the chosen model (finishTurnUpdatingCLI and resendAfterCLIUpdate run the CLI's own updater and send the failed message again, once per CLI version), two observable merge-queue flags, and a running-turn save interval that grows with the thread file's last written size. It also loses the uncalled hydraLiveInfo helper.

feature_notes: B3 adds a way to recover from a CLI that is too old for the model (SOURCE FACT, :2255-2293). finishTurnUpdatingCLI is consulted first on three failure paths: the startTurn catch (:1378, status .failed), .turnCompleted with an error (:2209, the event's own status) and .exited with an error while a turn runs (:2226, status .failed). It takes the error only when a turnID exists, the thread's provider passes ProviderRegistry.updatesOwnCLI (Claude or Codex only), and ProviderRegistry.needsNewerCLI matches. The match is case-insensitive and fires on any of 'or newer is required', 'requires a newer version', 'claude update', 'codex update', 'upgrade codex' or 'update codex'. When it takes the error, the raw error is NOT posted. An .info notice 'This model needs a newer <name>. Updating it, then sending your message again.' is appended inside the turn, and a Task awaits finishTurn(status:turnID:) and then resendAfterCLIUpdate. The caller neither posts the error nor ends the turn itself: it returns or breaks.

resendAfterCLIUpdate (:2272-2293): awaits app.providers.updateCLIIfDue(provider, force: true). It then reads installedCLIVersion. When that is nil, or equals cliResendVersions[provider] (the version this runtime already resent at), it appends the error notice '<error>

Droppy Code could not bring <name> up to date. Run `claude update`|`codex update` in Terminal, then send the message again.' and stops. Otherwise it records the version, releases the session with stop: true so the next send launches the new binary, and checks that the runtime is idle and that the turn still exists with a user item that is not from Hydra. If any check fails, it appends '<error>

<name> is up to date now (<version>). Send the message again.'. If they pass, it calls resend(turnID, text:, attachments:, restoreFiles: false), which reverts the failed turn (the info notice goes with it) and sends the same text and attachments. A throw appends '<name> is up to date now (<version>), but the message could not be sent again: <localizedDescription> Send it again.'. These three notices land after finishTurn has cleared currentTurnID and closingTurnID, so they are filed with no turn.

Consequence read from the source (not executed): the first attempt resends even if the updater did not change the version, because cliResendVersions starts empty. A second 'too old' failure at the same version then gets the 'could not bring up to date' notice. The limit is one resend per CLI version per runtime, and it is not persisted. On Codex, revert(to:) throws 'The selected message has no Codex turn ID, so its history cannot be safely reverted.' when the failed turn has no providerTurnID and the thread already has a providerSessionID (:1866-1868). That surfaces through the third notice.

Handler ordering changed. In .turnCompleted (:2206-2211) the turn id is captured before the error notice, then the CLI check runs, then 'if let error { appendNotice(.error, error) }', then finishTurn. In .exited (:2212-2229) the error notice now comes after the turn-id capture and the CLI check. The session is still released without stopping, approvals and questions are still cleared, and native heads are still stopped before the check. The fallback '<name> stopped unexpectedly.' for a nil error is unchanged.

Two new observed runtime flags (:313-317): isHydraMergeQueued ('This chat's finished work is waiting for another chat's merge to finish, and goes right after it') and hasHydraMergeRetryPending ('A quiet retry of a merge that failed in a way that clears by itself is scheduled'). This file only declares them. AppModel+HydraMerge.swift sets and reads them: :81 and :89-90 for the in-process merge queue, :415-420 for the 60-second retry. No B3 view reads them (git grep HEAD). holdsOnlyPersistedState (:3679-3686) does not include them.

scheduleSave while a turn runs (:3634-3647) no longer waits a fixed 5 s. The delay is seconds = min(20, max(5, bytes / 250_000)), with bytes = DiskWriter.shared.lastWrittenSize(of: Storage.threadURL(threadID)) ?? 0. That gives 5 s up to 1,250,000 bytes, then a linear rise to the 20 s cap at 5,000,000 bytes. The comment says 'five seconds up to a megabyte', which is approximate: the arithmetic keeps 5 s to 1.25 MB. The idle 800 ms debounce is unchanged. saveNow's comment still speaks of 'the five-second bound on what a crash costs' (:3654), which B3 made stale for large threads.

isPresented true: if the coordinator is not already shown, coordinator.show(detail().presentedChrome()). isPresented false: coordinator.close(). The observer is `.onChange(of: isPresented) { _, shown in ... }` (line 67, and line 101 in BadgePopoverModifier) without `initial: true`, so a badge that mounts with isPresented already true does not open its popover until the flag changes.

If a popover is still shown it is closed at once (unreachable from the two callers, see side_effects). The content gets .environment(\.closePopover, { [weak self] in self?.close() }) so rows or sheets inside can close it. Size is NSHostingView(rootView: content).fittingSize, replaced by 460 x 320 if either side is <= 0, then popover.setFixedContent(content, size: size). shownIn = anchor.view.window; shownRect = anchor.view.convert(anchor.rect, to: nil). purpose: Parses a Hydra merge note's plain-text body into a HydraMergeNote (file, addition and deletion counts, target and source branch, status notes and the list of heads that landed) and renders it as HydraMergePopover, a 380 pt card titled 'Merged' with the forge favicon, three stat tiles, up to eight head faces with hover cards, a branch-to-target chip row, info notes, and Copy link / Open merge-or-pull-request buttons. The parse returns nil unless the body contains the files line, in which case the caller keeps its generic popover.

feature_notes: parse algorithm: split body on "\n"; trim each line; an empty line ends the Heads section and is skipped; the exact line "Heads" starts the Heads section; inside it, lines starting "- " are matched whole against the head regex (non-matching '- ' lines are silently dropped) and always skipped as notes; a non-'- ' line ends the section and falls through to normal handling.
Head parse: name = group 1, index = Int(group 2) ?? 0, task = group 3; files = group 5 split on ", " only when group 4 is non-nil and group 5 non-empty, else [] (the 'no files' alternative).

Files line (line 60): `if let found = line.wholeMatch(of: #/(\d+) files? \(\+(\d+) −(\d+)\) landed on `([^`]+)` from `([^`]+)`\./#), match == nil {`. The `match == nil` test is part of the if condition, so only the first matching files line sets files, additions, deletions, target (group 4), branch (group 5); a second matching files line fails the if, falls through to the "is up to date." check and then `notes.append(line.replacingOccurrences(of: "`", with: ""))`, becoming an info note with its backticks removed. For the first match, if any of the three numbers fails Int() the line is skipped with `else { continue }` (not treated as a note). Format: "<n> file(s) (+<a> −<d>) landed on `<target>` from `<branch>`."
Lines ending "is up to date." are dropped; every other line (including a second files line) becomes a note with all backticks removed.
No files line -> parse returns nil.
Copy link: ignored while didCopyLink is true; sets didCopyLink true with .snappy(duration: 0.22), then after Task.sleep 1.4 s sets it false with the same animation.
Favicon: FaviconCache.cached(host:) first; otherwise awaits FaviconCache.image(for: host). host is note.link.url.host ?? "".
Hover popover binding: shown when hoveredHead == head; dismissing clears hoveredHead only if it is still that head. onHover(false) clears only when hoveredHead equals the head.
The doc comment above headCard reads 'One number tile: the count large, what it counts small beneath it.' which actually describes stat(); a misplaced comment in source.

B1->B2: the two static NSRegularExpression properties (private static let filesPattern and static let headPattern, the latter internal) were removed and replaced with inline Swift Regex literals matched via line.wholeMatch(of:); the old patterns were anchored with ^ and $ and the new ones rely on wholeMatch, with the same capture groups and the same U+2014 dash / U+2212 minus characters. The group() helper that mapped NSRange to Substring and the NSNotFound check for group 4 were replaced by typed optional captures (found.output.4 != nil, found.output.5 ?? ""). rawLine.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) became rawLine.trimmed. Fonts moved from fixed sizes to text styles: "Merged" 15 semibold -> .title3 semibold; host line 11 -> .subheadline; heads-landed count 11 -> .subheadline; arrow.right 9 semibold -> .caption2 semibold; info.circle and note text 12 -> .callout; copied checkmark 11 semibold -> .subheadline semibold; head card name 13 semibold -> .body semibold, task 12 -> .callout, empty text 11 -> .subheadline, file paths 11 monospaced -> .subheadline monospaced; stat value 17 semibold monospacedDigit -> .title2 semibold monospacedDigit, stat label 10 medium -> .footnote medium; chip 11 monospaced -> .subheadline monospaced. Fixed symbol sizes 18 (merge icon) and 20 (seal) unchanged. File went from 298 to 286 lines. HydraMergeNote.headPattern is no longer an accessible symbol, so any external reference to it would have been removed in B2.

Digit matching: neither regex applies `.asciiOnlyDigits()`, and Swift Regex `\d` matches any Unicode decimal digit by default, while `Int(Substring)` parses only ASCII digits and fails past Int.max. So a files line with non-ASCII digits or an oversized number matches and is then dropped by `else { continue }` (lines 61-62), not turned into a note; a head line with such an index gets `index: Int(found.output.2) ?? 0` (line 48). A port whose `\d` is ASCII-only (for example JavaScript) would fail the match and turn such a files line into a note instead; match Unicode Nd digits (\p{Nd} with the u flag) to keep parity.

Card order (lines 100-216): header, stats row, heads row (only when heads non-empty, line 135), branch row (line 162), notes, buttons. The comment at lines 133-134 ("The branch chip spans whatever the arrow and the target leave, so the row runs the card's full width...") sits above `if !note.heads.isEmpty {`, not above the branch row it describes: a second misplaced comment besides the headCard one.
unresolved_questions: Who produces the merge note body (the generator of the '<n> files (+a −d) landed on ...' line, the 'Heads' section and the 'is up to date.' line) is in other files and must be matched byte-for-byte including U+2014 and U+2212. The callers of parse are DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/TimelineRows.swift:296 `HydraMergeNote.parse(details, link: request)` and :1113 `HydraMergeNote.parse(outcome.details, link: request)`, both only after `MergeRequestLink(url: link)` succeeds.
Resolved: in B1 `headPattern` appears only in HydraMergePopover.swift (B1 line 31 declaration, line 51 use), so its removal in B2 breaks no external caller.

feature_notes: B2->B3 has one functional change: HydraStatusText.elapsed(_:) now builds its ' in <duration>' clause with `Duration.seconds(seconds).formatted(.units(allowed: [.seconds, .minutes], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down)))` instead of the retired `seconds < 60 ? " in Ns" : " in Mm Ss"` string interpolation. Because this allowed-unit set omits .hours (unlike the sibling RelativeTime.duration, which includes hours and is already an established source fact elsewhere in this spec/port as 'Ns'/'Mm Ss'/'Hh Mm'), the narrow-width formatter restricted to seconds+minutes very likely still renders exactly 'Ns' below a minute and 'Mm Ss' at or above with no hour rollover for any duration -- i.e. the same string shape the retired code already produced. The already-built C# port (src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/HydraPanel.cs:801-808 Elapsed()) still implements the retired manual formula and, on that reading, would already match B3's new output by coincidence; this needs positive confirmation rather than being assumed. Two doc-comment edits in this file (the file-level intro at :5-11 and the HydraLiveInfo comment now at :475-477) are wording-only and touch no code path; PR-HYDRA-179's source_evidence quotes the old, longer comment prose verbatim, which is now stale text describing the same, unchanged HydraLiveInfo.shown function.
unresolved_questions: Verify the exact `Duration.formatted(.units(allowed: [.seconds, .minutes], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down)))` output against the compiled B3 app before closing PR-HYDRA-180; this report infers 'Ns'/'Mm Ss' by analogy with the sibling RelativeTime.duration precedent rather than an independent runtime check of this exact call.

purpose: Draws a Hydra head's progress as a single 28pt-tall Canvas of 3pt staves, one stave per tool call or assistant reply in timeline order, whose height encodes how much the step changed (lookup 0.45, command 0.65, edit 0.85, reply 1.0) and whose colour is the head's persona tint at varying opacity; a count line ('3 edits · 2 commands · 5 reads') sits under it and hovering a stave shows a 260pt glass card naming that step. The file also holds the compact 'Show what heads are doing' off-mode panel (HydraHeadProgress) that centres the head's task title over the bar, the breathing/sweeping task title (HydraWorkingTitle), the per-second elapsed-time label (HydraElapsedTime), the hover card surface modifier and a global SweepBudget that caps the highlight sweep animation to 3 running bars at once for performance.

Two sleeping tasks: .task(id: isRunning ? -1 : events.count) sets isSettled=false, and when not running sleeps rise+0.1 = 0.55 s then sets isSettled=true; .task(id: events.count) (skipped if events empty or reduce motion) sets isRising=true, sleeps 0.55 s, sets isRising=false. Capacity = max(1, floor((width + 3) / 6)); when there are more events than capacity only the latest `capacity` staves are drawn (oldest slide off the left).

Rise animation (lines 380-388): factor starts at 1; when rising (not reduce-motion) `let age = date.timeIntervalSince(stave.arrivedAt)` where date is the TimelineView context date and arrivedAt is `entry.item.date` (the timeline entry's own timestamp, lines 326/332), not the moment the stave first appeared on screen; if age < 0.45, `let t = max(0, age / rise)` and factor = 1 - pow(1 - t, 3) (ease-out cubic). So a bar opened on old history draws every stave at full height with no rise, and an entry dated in the future (negative age) gets t = 0 and factor 0.

Sweep highlight: band width max(24, filledWidth/3) where filledWidth = staves.count*6 - 3; cycle length 2.6 + 3.4 = 6.0 s computed from timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate; during the first 2.6 s the band x = -band + phase*(filledWidth+band); linear gradient white opacity 0 -> 0.55 -> 0, clipped to the filled staves path only.

Clock: TimelineView .animation minimumInterval 1/24 s, paused when !needsClock or ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling; needsClock = !reduceMotion && !isSettled && (sweeps || isRising); sweeps = isRunning && !reduceMotion && SweepBudget.shared.sweeps(id).

Zero-height skip (lines 389-390): `let height = bottom * stave.height * factor; guard height > 0 else { continue }`. A stave at factor 0 (age exactly 0 or negative) is not added to `filled`, `byKind`, `ending` or `hoveredPath` for that frame, so the sweep highlight (clipped to `filled`), the failed/stopped ending colour and the hover white 0.4 fill all skip it; its slot is also not drawn as an empty slot (slots start at staves.count). The hover card overlay is independent of the canvas and still shows.

Elapsed time: inside HydraProgressBar `let elapsed = RelativeTime.duration((isRunning ? Date.now : finishedAt ?? .now).timeIntervalSince(startedAt))` (line 130) is used only in the accessibility label (line 208); the bar draws no elapsed text. The visible elapsed time is HydraElapsedTime, which the doc comment (lines 7-8) places in the strip's pill: 'how long the head has been at it sits in the strip's pill (see `HydraElapsedTime`)'. A port must not put an elapsed label under the bar.
feature_notes: Stave classification: ToolCall.kind .edit -> edit; .command -> edit if call.edits is non-empty else command; any other kind -> edit if call.edits non-empty else lookup. Assistant entries -> reply. All other entry kinds are skipped. Counts count edit/command/lookup only (reply not counted).
An MCP tool gets its MCPCatalogEntry glyph and no symbol; non-MCP tools get ToolPresentation.symbol(for: call.kind).

StaveCache hit requires equal capacity and, row-by-row, the same TimelineEntry object identity and, for tool rows, same ToolCall.status and ToolCall.title; otherwise it recomputes events, staves and counts.
The finished-bar settle task keys on -1 while running (so it does not restart per event while running) and on events.count once finished.

purpose: The in-thread editor for a previously sent user message: it wraps PromptEditor titled 'Edit message' around the message's text and attachments, and above the actions shows a box describing what the working tree changed since that message with an optional switch to undo those file changes. Sending calls runtime.resend to rewind the thread to before the message (optionally restoring files) and resend the edit; the edit state lives on ThreadRuntime.messageEdit so closing and reopening the thread preserves it.

side_effects: .task(id: edit.id) (lines 64-69) always calls `runtime.revertPreview(for: edit.id)`, awaits `.value`, and unless cancelled assigns `changes = Changes(result)`, even when init already filled `changes` from cachedRevertPreview. In ThreadRuntime (lines 1765-1789) revertPreview returns the same cached Task while the entry has the current diffRevision and is under 10 s old, and cachedRevertPreview returns a result only under that same condition, so normally the task re-assigns the same result; only if the entry expired or diffRevision changed between init and the task does a fresh preview run, and it can then replace a cached .found with a new .found or .unavailable.

send() (lines 156-171): begins `guard canSend else { return }`, so onSubmit from PromptEditor (keyboard submit) is gated exactly like the disabled Send button. Then restore = false; if changes is .found, restore = restoresFiles && !preview.files.isEmpty; sets isSending = true, error = nil, and in a Task awaits runtime.resend(edit.id, text:, attachments:, restoreFiles: restore); on success sets runtime.messageEdit = nil; on failure sets error to error.localizedDescription; always resets isSending.
cancel(): sets runtime.messageEdit = nil (closes the editor, discarding the edit).

feature_notes: B2->B3's substantive change: the row stack's container changed from `LazyVStack` to a plain `VStack` (B3 lines 384-388, replacing B2's single `LazyVStack(...)` line), with a new comment explaining why -- rows of varying height at the visible edge sent a lazy stack pinned to the bottom into a placement loop that never returned to the run loop, causing release hangs of 16 seconds to 20 minutes. Because an eager stack has no ceiling of its own, B3 adds a companion cap: a new `TimelineWindow.eagerLimit = 96` constant (B3 lines 1805-1811, inserted after `page = 24`) and a new clause inside `.onChange(of: lastEntryID)` (B3 lines 702-706, inserted right after the existing arrival guard) that drops the window back to the newest `TimelineWindow.initial` (24) blocks whenever the eagerly-rendered `visible` count exceeds 96 while the reader is following the conversation's end. Net effect: the timeline no longer virtualizes rows at all: every block in the current window is always fully materialized, and the window itself is kept bounded by actively evicting older blocks (back to 24) once it grows past 96, rather than by lazy on-screen instantiation. This is an internal reliability fix (the B2 hang) with an observable side effect for the port: any implementation must not rely on a virtualizing/recycling list control for this specific stack (that would reintroduce the exact placement-loop risk B3 documents fixing), and must reproduce the 96-block eviction-while-pinned behaviour, which the pinned B2 baseline never had.

Two spec records (porting/spec/CHAT.json) sit exactly inside the touched ranges and need more than a line-number recite: PR-CHAT-045 ('The lazy window opens at three blocks...') cites B2 TimelineWindow.swift:1795-1799 as the whole enum body (firstPaint/initial/page + closing brace); in B3 that same content is unshifted-content-but-interleaved (the enum now also holds eagerLimit before its closing brace), and neither PR-CHAT-045 nor PR-CHAT-192 (which cites the same enum) documents the new eviction behaviour at all. PR-CHAT-132 ('A new row at the end brings a reader who was at the end down to it...') cites B2 :685-703 as the whole onChange(of: lastEntryID) handler; B3 inserts the new eagerLimit-eviction clause in the middle of that exact handler, so the requirement's evidence range now spans genuinely new logic its expected_result text never mentions.

UI-CHAT-001 (the timeline's 'list' UI record) cites B2 :359-425, which spans the LazyVStack->VStack line (B2 :384); its stated geometry/typography/states describe layout only, never virtualization, so the swap does not falsify anything it asserts -- a pure line-shift recite is sufficient there.

Every other requirement/UI citation into this file that falls at or after B2 line 384 shifts by a mechanical amount (+4 for B2 385-698, +9 for B2 699-1798, +12 for B2 1799-2314, confirmed against the B2 total line count of 2314 cited verbatim in CHAT.json:238's own B1->B2 note and matching this B3 file's measured 2326 lines); PR-CHAT-128, PR-CHAT-135, PR-CHAT-044, PR-CHAT-192 and UI-CHAT-060 (checked individually) fall in these shift zones without their described behaviour changing.

The C# skeleton at src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.cs is unimplemented (every member throws MARROW_STUB; unit status TODO in porting/deps/units.json) and its per-member '// :NNN-MMM' citations still point at B2 line numbers throughout, so nothing already-built needs correcting, but the eventual implementation must build the eager+96-cap window behaviour described above rather than the plain lazy/virtualized list the B2-era skeleton comments (and the retired LazyVStack) would suggest, and the skeleton's citation comments need re-basing onto the B3 line numbers computed above when the unit is picked up.
unresolved_questions: Whether a new parity_matrix requirement should be filed for the eagerLimit=96 eviction-while-pinned behaviour (distinct from PR-CHAT-045's initial-window sizing), or whether it is folded into PR-CHAT-045/PR-CHAT-132 as an amendment -- this is an owner/spec-refresh decision, not a reading question.

Whether Avalonia's virtualizing panel (if one was ever planned for this stack) must be avoided entirely per the B2 hang B3 documents, or whether a virtualizing control without SwiftUI's specific placement-loop defect would be acceptable -- needs an explicit engineering decision when App.Views.Chat.ThreadTimeline is implemented.

feature_notes: B2->B3 removes the rail's entire manual NSCursor push/pop bookkeeping and replaces it with the declarative `.pointerStyle(.link)` modifier. Deleted: the `ownsCursorPush` @State flag, the `if !ownsCursorPush { NSCursor.pointingHand.push(); ownsCursorPush = true }` guard inside onContinuousHover's `.active` case, the `releaseCursor()` private method, its call from onContinuousHover's `.ended` case, and its call from a now-deleted `.onDisappear { releaseCursor() }` on the GeometryReader. Added: a single `.pointerStyle(.link)` modifier on the same Color.clear hit-area view. The end-user-visible outcome (a pointing-hand cursor while hovering the rail, restored to the system default off it, including on a disappear-while-hovering) is very likely unchanged, since `.pointerStyle` is documented to scope itself to the view's own hover lifetime; but the *mechanism* the spec explicitly encodes as testable behaviour is gone.

Two spec records are built directly around the retired push/pop mechanism and need reclassification, not just a line recite. PR-CHAT-072 ('Hovering the rail previews a tick...', status IMPLEMENTED) cites B2 :214-229 as 'pushes a pointing-hand cursor on first entry ... pops the cursor', lists a side_effect of 'A pointing-hand cursor is pushed ... and popped exactly once', a failure_case of 'A disappear while hovering pops the pushed cursor exactly once, guarded by an ownership flag', and a windows_path of 'Windows has no NSCursor push/pop stack: model it as an explicit LIFO cursor-owner stack and mirror each push and pop site one for one (port_impacts.md 310)'. None of that push/pop machinery exists in B3 any more. UI-CHAT-003 (the rail's UI record) likewise states in its interactions/notes that hover 'pushes a pointing-hand cursor' which 'must be popped exactly once, including on a disappear while hovering'.

The already-built C# port (src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/TimelineMinimap.cs, unit status DONE) implements PR-CHAT-072's B2-era windows_path literally: a private `CursorOwner` record, a static `List<CursorOwner> CursorOwners` LIFO stack, `PushCursor`/`ReleaseCursor`/`ApplyCursorOwners` methods, and a code comment at line 462 reading ':214-227. Windows cursor ownership mirrors each push and pop through this explicit LIFO stack.' That comment's own justification (mirroring B2's push/pop sites) no longer matches the pinned source: B3 has no push/pop sites left to mirror, only a single scoped modifier. The LIFO stack may still produce the same visible cursor today, but it is now solving a problem (safe nesting of multiple imperative pushes/pops) the source itself no longer has.
unresolved_questions: Whether TimelineMinimap.cs's CursorOwner/LIFO-stack mechanism should be simplified to a plain scoped-cursor toggle (matching B3's .pointerStyle semantics more directly) now that the B2 push/pop hazard it was built to mirror is gone, or left as-is because it still produces the same visible result -- an engineering-decision question, not a reading one.

Whether PR-CHAT-072 and UI-CHAT-003's evidence/side_effects/failure_cases/windows_path text should be rewritten to cite `.pointerStyle(.link)` instead of the retired NSCursor push/pop description; the underlying user-visible claim (pointing-hand cursor while hovering, normal cursor otherwise) appears unchanged and is not itself in question.

purpose: TimelineRows.swift holds the SwiftUI view for every kind of row the chat transcript can show. It covers the user's iMessage-style bubble with its quote chips, pencil editor and 'Edit from this message?' revert dialog; the Hydra team rows (head report pill, lead brief pill with the cooking shimmer, finished-head pills, the streamed delegation card, the merge pill with its animated dot track); attachment strips and thumbnails; assistant replies with their right-click action list; collapsible tool work groups, individual tool rows that open a diff, an image, a head's steps popover or inline output; the plan badge, todo checklist, notice row, turn-end duration line, and the collapsed finished-turn block with its edited-files card and revert/review round buttons. It also owns the shared vertical geometry (TimelineMetrics) and the pure text helpers the rows use: tool labels and verbs (ToolPresentation), the work-group summary sentence (WorkGroupSummary), Hydra report summaries, merge-note URL parsing and the last-fenced-code-block scan used by 'Copy last code block'.

User row: VStack trailing spacing 6, row padded leading 96, bottom padding -(22 + 6) = -28 so the hover line sits in the next gap. Confirmation dialog title 'Edit from this message?', buttons 'Revert and keep file changes' and 'Revert files too' (destructive), message 'This message and everything after it leave the thread, and your prompt returns to the composer.'

Hydra report pill: HStack spacing 8; Hydra mark 18x18 Chrome.secondaryText or overlapping glyphs (HStack spacing -4, glyph size 18); title .chat(.callout, weight: .medium) primaryText 0.9, 1 line, tail; 'chevron.right' .chat(.caption2, weight: .semibold) Chrome.secondaryText only when there are details; tooltip 'Show the message' (empty when no details); 'Open' link .chat(.caption, weight: .semibold) secondaryText tooltip 'Open in the browser'; background .tint opacity 0.1 radius 18; padded trailing 96 (left-aligned).

FinishedHeadPill: glyph 18 with status, name styled via HydraNameStyle on primaryText 0.75 + ' failed' / ' was stopped' / ' finished working', callout medium; chevron.right caption2 semibold secondaryText; tint 0.1 pill; tooltip 'Show the report'.

HydraShimmer: band width max(24, textWidth / 3), sweep period 1.8 s, 30 fps (minimumInterval 1/30) paused while ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling; gradient primaryText opacity 0 -> 0.9 (at 0.5) -> 0; offset x = -band + phase * (width + band); phase comes from the global clock, `CGFloat(context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: Self.sweep) / Self.sweep)` (500), so every shimmer on screen is in the same phase and none restarts on appear; disabled under reduce motion.

Brief pill: '\(persona.name) is starting to cook…' (with shimmer, glyph isRunning) while cooking, else '\(persona.name)'s brief'; glyph 18; callout medium primaryText 0.9; chevron.right; tint 0.1 pill; focusable(false); tooltip 'Show the brief'; right-aligned with leading padding 96; attachments strip above.

Delegation titles: 'Summoning heads' (streaming or none read), 'Summoning|Summoned \(name)', 'Summoning|Summoned a head', 'Summoning|Summoned \(n) heads'.

"Merging")…' callout medium primaryText 0.9 with shimmer; new stage transition insertion opacity+offset y 5 / removal opacity+offset y -5; slot clipped with 6 pt vertical / 2 pt horizontal slack; Animation.smooth(duration: 0.3) for changes; row appear/disappear .settleGlide with .spring(Chrome.glideSpring); outcome title callout medium primaryText 0.9 with chevron when details; 'Open' link; accessibility label outcome title or 'Merging the team's work: \(stage)'; tint 0.1 pill; trailing 96.

TimelineMetrics.rowSpacing : 0) (2663); folded answer stack .padding(.bottom, TimelineMetrics.rowSpacing) (2679); HydraHeadsList .padding(.bottom, hasFiles ? Files popover: up to 12 rows (path callout 1 line middle truncation, 'Binary' caption secondaryText or DiffStatLabel), padding h12 v7; overflow line 'and 1 more file' when exactly 13 else 'and \(count - 12) more files' callout secondaryText.
feature_notes: UserMessageRow dispatch order: message.isFromHydra -> HydraReportRow; else message.isHydraBrief -> HydraBriefRow; else the bubble. isEditing = entry.turnID != nil && runtime.messageEdit?.id == entry.turnID. The pencil toggles runtime.messageEdit between nil and PromptEdit(id: turnID, text: message.text, attachments: message.attachments). The editor syncs on anchor capture and on isEditing change and closes on disappear.

Right-click on a user message builds its actions from snapshots; 'Copy message' copies MessageText.plain(text), 'Copy as markdown' copies raw text; both go through ProseReflow.reflowed. 'Edit from here' only sets menuRequests.confirmRevert, which the row resets and turns into isConfirmingRevert = true. Revert runs Task { _ = try? await runtime.revert(to:restoreFiles:) }.

lastCodeBlock scans lines split on "\n": each line with prefix ``` toggles open/closed; a closed block's lines joined by "\n" become the candidate; an unclosed trailing block is ignored; the last closed block wins.

HydraReportRow: personas = (message.hydraHeads ?? []).map(HydraRoster.persona(at:)). With no personas (a note from Hydra itself): text split at the first newline (maxSplits 1, empty subsequences omitted); title = first line minus one trailing '.', default 'Hydra'; body = remainder trimmed; link = leadingURL(body); details = body, or body without its first line when a link was found. With personas: title = reportSummary, body = full text, no link.

reportSummary: names with no '(failed' / '(stopped' outcome are listed as '\(list) is done' (1) or 'are done' (more); each other head adds '\(name) failed' or '\(name) stopped'; joined with ', ' and passed through TextCleanup.singleLine(limit: 140). list(): '' for none, 'A' for one, 'A, B and C'. reportOutcomes reads lines trimmed of whitespace starting '## ' with a ':'; name = characters 3..<colon trimmed; lowercased text from the colon containing '(failed' -> 'failed', else '(stopped' -> 'stopped'.

leadingURL: first line trimmed of spaces must start (case-insensitively) with 'http://' or 'https://' and contain no whitespace, then URL(string:). withoutFirstLine returns '' when there is no newline, else everything from the first newline, trimmed.

Report pill popover choice: link + MergeRequestLink(url:) + HydraMergeNote.parse(details, link:) -> HydraMergePopover; else personas -> HydraReportsPopover(title:text:personas:); else HydraReportPopover(text: body). The button is disabled and does nothing when details is empty. .task(id: body) warms markdown for [body] or each head body from HydraReportDigest.parse(body).heads.

HydraHeadsWorkingRow reads model.helpers(of: runtime.threadID) filtered by isHydraHead, indexes their hydra infos by index (first wins), and shows a FinishedHeadPill for each requested index found, in the caller's order. finishedHeads(in:) returns [] when no head is running; otherwise finished heads whose batch still has a running head, or (no batchID) whose finishedAt >= earliest running startedAt.
FinishedHeadPill accessibility title: '\(name) failed' (.failed), '\(name) was stopped' (.stopped), '\(name) finished working' (otherwise); opens HydraHeadReportPopover(head:).

HydraBriefRow: persona = runtime.thread?.hydra?.persona ?? HydraRoster.persona(at: 0). hasOutput = the entry has a turnID and another entry (different id) shares it; memoized per runtime.entries.count via onChange(of: count, initial: true). cooking = !hasOutput && runtime.isRunning. Popover HydraBriefPopover(persona:, task: runtime.thread?.hydra?.task, text: message.text).

HydraDelegationBlock: reading = HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations(inBody: json[...]) cached in a 200-entry RecentCache keyed by the JSON string; streaming = !reading.isComplete && !sent. persona(named:) returns nil for nil/blank names, else HydraRoster.persona(named:). projectName: nil for nil/blank; a value containing '/' becomes its lastPathComponent (falls back to the whole value if that is empty).

HydraMergeOutcome parses the outcome note exactly like a Hydra note: title via withoutTrailingStop(first line ?? 'Hydra'), body = rest trimmed, link = leadingURL(body), details = body or body minus first line.

HydraMergeRow: while phase is .merging and runtime.isHydraMerging is false the row renders EmptyView (the pill goes away). Track step = runtime.hydraMergeStep?.rawValue ?? 0 while running, else HydraMergeStage.allCases.count - 1. trackMode: no outcome -> .running; outcome with flourish -> .done; else .resting. flourish turns on when isMerging goes true -> false and outcome.title contains 'Hydra merged', and off again after Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(1100)). Tapping the track or title toggles the report popover (arrowEdge .bottom, presentedChrome) only when details is non-empty. Popover content (1113-1119): when outcome.link, MergeRequestLink(url:) and HydraMergeNote.parse(outcome.details, link:) all succeed it shows HydraMergePopover(note:); otherwise the fallback is HydraReportPopover(text: outcome.body), the full body including any leading URL line, not details.

HydraMergeTrackBody math: trackWidth = count*4 + (count-1)*3; dotCentre(i) = i*7 + 2; lit(i) = max(position + 0.35 >= i ? 1 : 0, clamp(done*(count+1) - i, 0, 1)); side = 12 + 6*rest; x = (dotCentre(position) - 6)*(1 - rest); y = -arc*(1 - rest) + 1*rest; frame width = trackWidth + (18 - trackWidth)*rest, height 20, topLeading.

AttachmentThumbnail: first state image comes from ThumbnailMemory (so revisited photos do not fade in); .task(id: path) uses ThumbnailMemory else ThumbnailCache.shared.thumbnail(for:pointSize:fillingSquare: true), stores it, fades in with easeOut 0.15. Anchor view is mounted only after the first hover and never when anchorless. togglePanel uses the slot's lazily created panel or the caller's coordinator.
AssistantMessageRow 'Add to reply' ignores the request if runtime.draft.quotes already has a quote with identical text; runtime is captured weakly.
WorkGroup: a single entry renders a bare ToolRow. startsCollapsed changes only ever collapse (one-way). WorkSteps hides all but the last 2 entries until 'N earlier steps' is tapped.

WorkGroupSummary.text: one pass records per kind whether any call is running; parts in order edit, read, command, search, web, mcp, agent, other with labels Editing/Edited files, Reading/Read files, Running/Ran commands, Searching/Searched, Browsing/Browsed, Calling/Called tools, Delegating/Delegated tasks, Using/Used tools; 'Worked' when no tool entries; parts after the first get a lowercased first character; joined by ', '. symbol(for:) returns the symbol of the first kind present in that order, default 'wrench.and.screwdriver'.

ToolRow logic: edits = call.edits with non-empty path; opensDiff = edits non-empty; imagePath resolved only when not a diff; showsOutput = !opensDiff && (output non-empty || detail non-empty); opensImage = imagePath != nil && (kind == .read || !showsOutput); headID = runtime.hydraHead(forTool: entry.id) for .agent calls; not tappable rows render as plain text. Tap: head -> toggle steps popover; diff -> runtime.showDiff(on: anchor, edge: .minY, turn:, focusEdits: edits); image -> panel toggle with PreviewImages.attachment(for:) at edge .minY; else toggle inline output with .snappy(0.24) and reveal.

Head text for linked agent calls: '\(running ? "Sending out" : "Sent out") \(persona.name): \(call.title)'. departingHead: title trimmed; if 'Name: task' and Name is a roster persona -> (persona, persona.name, task) (1731): the roster's canonical name, not the text typed before the colon; else (persona at 0, nil, title unless it is one of 'subagent', 'agent', 'task', '' (case-insensitive) in which case ''). departureLabel: running 'Sending out \(who)\(rest)', failed 'Could not send out \(who)\(rest)', else 'Sent out \(who)\(rest)' with who = name ?? 'a head' and rest = ': \(task)' or ''. departureStatus: running nil, failed .failed, else .completed.

ToolPresentation.label strips a leading word equal to a kind root: command [run, bash, shell, exec, execute, command], read [read, view, open, cat], edit [edit, write, multiedit, create, notebookedit, apply_patch, patch], search [search, grep, glob, find], web [fetch, webfetch, websearch, browse], mcp [call], agent [delegate, agent, task], other [use]; then joins verb + subject with a space, dropping empty parts. Verbs: Running/Ran, Reading/Read, Editing/Edited, Searching/Searched, Browsing/Browsed, Calling/Called, Delegating/Delegated, Using/Used. stats returns nil when no edits or additions+deletions == 0. mcpParts splits the title at ' · ' (space, middle dot, space), both sides trimmed and non-empty, and needs MCPCatalog.entry(matching: server). mcpLabel = '\(entry.name): \(tool)' (running is unused).

HydraHeadStepsPopover: report shown only when the head isFinished and its summary trimmed is non-empty. statusLine = outcome ('Working…', 'Done', 'Failed', 'Stopped') + ('1 tool' or '\(n) tools' when toolCalls > 0) + RelativeTime.duration(finishedAt.timeIntervalSince(hydra.startedAt)) whenever `if let finishedAt = hydra.finishedAt` (2021-2023), not gated on isFinished (only the report section uses isFinished, 1888), joined ' · '. steps(in:) drops the first user entry (the brief), keeps later user entries and assistant entries with non-blank text, keeps all tool and notice entries, drops reasoning, turnEnd, plan, todos.

ToolDetailView: output trimmed of newlines; lineCount = 1 + number of 0x0A bytes; collapsed when not expanded and lineCount > 30, showing the text before the 30th newline (head(of:lines:) scans UTF-8 bytes).
DiffDetailCache keys on path + "\n" + diff and parses with DiffParser.parseHunks(diff, path:), 60-entry cache.

PlanCard proposed buttons: 'Implement plan' closes the popover then runtime.implementPlan(entry.id); 'Dismiss' closes then runtime.dismissPlan(entry.id); both disabled when runtime.pendingPlanApproval != nil || runtime.isRunning.

TurnEndRow.label: '.completed' and '.running' -> 'Worked for \(duration)', '.interrupted' -> 'Stopped after \(duration)', '.failed' -> 'Failed after \(duration)', duration from RelativeTime.duration(summary.duration).

TurnFinishedBlock.Derived: assistant entries with any non-whitespace character go into assistantEntries and answerEntries (hasResponse = true); plans into collapsedPlans; non-info notices into collapsedNotices; each tool entry clears answerEntries, adds .agent calls to headEntries and sets hasEdits when edits exist. If answerEntries ends empty the last assistant entry is used. Plans or non-info notices also set hasResponse. When expanded, detailGroups = TimelineGroup.build(content, showReasoning: false) minus .heads groups. The derivation is memoized in @State after render via onChange(of: key, initial: true).

TurnFinishedBlock body: changes = summary.changes ?? legacyChanges; showsBody = showsHeads || hasFiles || (expanded ? detailGroups non-empty : hasResponse). Divider and all content appear only when showsBody. Expanded: groups rendered as AssistantMessageRow (summary nil), single-tool WorkGroup, PlanCard, TodoListRow, NoticeRow or multi-entry WorkGroup with its startsCollapsed; folded: FoldedAnswerView for answer entries with non-empty text, then plans, then error/warning notices. Heads list always below; TurnFileCard last with onRevert = revert(to: turnID, restoreFiles: true).
