Word boundaries for @ and / detection are only 0x20, 0x0A and 0x09 (lines 446-449); 0x0D (CR), U+2028 and U+2029 are not boundaries. With CRLF line breaks the character directly before a word typed on a new line is still 0x0A, so detection works; a text store that ends lines with a lone CR or a Unicode line/paragraph separator would make the word run back across the break and defeat @ and / detection. The Windows text control must store line breaks as LF or CRLF for identical behaviour.

Path handling assumes '/' separators: Entry.name = `(lowercased as NSString).lastPathComponent` (line 1168), the suggestion title `(path as NSString).lastPathComponent` (line 461) and `ToolTitles.relativePath(url.path, to: directory)` (line 1283); git ls-files output uses '/'. A Windows directory walk yielding '\' separators would change the name-based scores (1000/800/600) and the titles unless paths are normalised to '/'.

The enumerate() skip list is an exact, case-sensitive match on url.lastPathComponent (line 1278); on a case-insensitive file system such as NTFS a folder named, for example, "Node_Modules" or "Build" would not be skipped by this test.

feature_notes: Diff popover coordination: onAppear and on threadID change call diffPopover.sync(isVisible: runtime.isDiffVisible); isDiffVisible changes sync; diffOpenRequest change calls reopen; onDisappear and column hidden close it. The changes-tab action clears diff focus, sets diffAnchor nil, clears diffSelection if set, and sets isDiffVisible true only when it was false (written last).

Suggestion list lifecycle: onChange(suggestions) shows AnyView(suggestionMenu()) with itemCount or hides; hidden on disappear, on thread change and when the column is hidden; column shown again refocuses only if takesFocusOnAppear. Command list changes re-run cursorMoved if focused; commandErrors change re-shows the list if focused and visible.
blur(): if the click was not inside the suggestion popover, cancels controller.suggestionRefresh and clears suggestions.

handleKey with the list visible: up = max(0, selected - 1); down = min(count - 1, selected + 1); tab/submit/steer pick the selected item; escape sets dismissedSuggestions and clears; deleteAtStart returns false (not consumed). Without the list: submit -> send(); steer -> steer(); up/down -> recall; escape -> takeBackRunningTurn if running, else hide terminal if visible, else toggleDiff if diff visible, else not consumed; tab not consumed; deleteAtStart removes draft.command first, else the last quote (both animated with Chrome.panelSlide), else not consumed.
send(): no-op on empty draft; clears historyIndex and suggestions; running -> runtime.interruptAndSend() (comment: with heads at work it queues instead), idle -> runtime.send().

steer(): no-op on empty draft; clears historyIndex and suggestions; queues via runtime.queueDraftAsFollowUp() only when runtime.canQueue and the queueChat chord equals keyCode 36 + command; otherwise runtime.send(). The else branch applies in the running state too: when the queueChat chord is rebound away from KeyChord(keyCode: 36, modifiers: .command) or !runtime.canQueue, steer() calls runtime.send() even while a turn runs, unlike send(), which calls runtime.interruptAndSend() while running (lines 374-378). Doc comment verbatim (lines 384-387): "Command-Return: steer the running turn by queueing the draft behind it. Idle, there is nothing to steer behind, so it just sends. The menu owns the chord while a turn runs; this path only sees it when the command is disabled or rebound, so it falls back to send once the chord moves." So steer() is a fallback: while a turn runs, Command-Return is normally handled by the menu command, not by the text view.

recall(older:): prompts = sentPrompts without empty strings; not consumed if none or if the draft has attachments; allowed only when the text is empty or equals the prompt at historyIndex. Older: next = (recalledIndex ?? count) - 1, returns true without change at the oldest. Newer: requires a recalled index; moves forward or, past the newest, clears historyIndex and text.

cursorMoved: resets dismissedSuggestions, calls runtime.warmSession() if the text is non-empty, cancels the previous refresh Task and starts a new @MainActor Task whose body is `guard !dismissedSuggestions else { return }; await refreshSuggestions(cursor: controller.cursorLocation)` (lines 433-436), so an Escape that sets dismissedSuggestions after the Task was scheduled suppresses that refresh.

refreshSuggestions: first `guard cursor > 0, cursor <= text.length else { if suggestions.isVisible { suggestions = SuggestionState() }; return }` (lines 441-444), so a caret at position 0 or past the end hides the list. Then word = run of characters before the caret back to space (0x20), newline (0x0A) or tab (0x09), in UTF-16 units. '@' prefix: fileIndex.search(rest), drops result if cancelled, items value "@<path> " title lastPathComponent detail path symbol "doc". '/' prefix only when the word starts at index 0: kind .command. Empty items hide the list. Selection is kept (clamped) only if the range location is unchanged, else 0.

commandSuggestions: built-ins first "plan" detail "Turn plan mode on or off"; "compact" detail "Summarize the conversation to free up context" when provider.supportsCompact (Provider.swift:151 at B2: .codex, .claude, .copilot, .deepseek, .meta, .zai, .pi); then provider commands for commandKey; ranked by SlashCommand.suggestions with recentCommands[provider.rawValue]; value "/<name> ", title "/<name>", symbol "command" for built-in else "sparkles".

pick(): command kind with a SlashCommand removes the typed word and sets runtime.draft.command = DraftCommand(...) animated, then focuses; otherwise replaces the word with suggestion.value (file mention with trailing space) and focuses.

attach(): room = max(0, 8 - current count); dropped = sources.count - min(sources.count, room); Storage.attach does the actual adding. Notice strings verbatim: single image source "The image was left out: a message holds 8 attachments"; one dropped "One file was left out: a message holds 8 attachments"; else "<n> files were left out: a message holds 8 attachments" (8 is Self.maxAttachments interpolated). Always refocuses. Notice clears after Task.sleep 5 s with Chrome.panelSlide via `.task(id: attachmentNotice) { guard attachmentNotice != nil else { return }; try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(5)); guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }; withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide) { attachmentNotice = nil } }` (lines 219-225). The wait restarts only when the notice string changes: note() only assigns `attachmentNotice = message` (line 523), so two consecutive drops that produce the same message (for example both "One file was left out: a message holds 8 attachments") leave the task id unchanged, the timer does not restart, and the notice clears 5 s after the first drop. The source comment "a second drop restarts the wait" holds only for a different message.

chooseFiles(): NSOpenPanel allowsMultipleSelection true, canChooseDirectories false, prompt "Attach"; on .OK attaches panel.urls as .file sources. Paperclip opens DownloadsPopover when settings.recentDownloadsPicker is true, else chooseFiles directly; popover pick closes it then attaches the URL; chooseOther closes it then runs chooseFiles.

goesToHead = hydraAlwaysHeads && hydraIsOn; queueGoesToHead = (hydraQueueHeads || hydraAlwaysHeads) && hydraIsOn; headsProvider = hydraHeadsProvider(of: pair) when hydra is on and a pair exists, nil when equal to the thread's provider.

ContextMeter hasCredits = CreditsReader.exposesCredits(provider) && settings.hasAPIKey(for: provider). Ring hidden entirely while the usage panel is popped out (settings.showsUsagePanel). Pop-out closes the popover then sets showsUsagePanel = true with Chrome.panelSlide.

FileIndex.prepare: sets directory; loops while not cancelled and directory unchanged: if a cache entry exists, assigns its entries and returns unless `Date.now.timeIntervalSince(cached.builtAt) > Self.freshness` (strictly greater than 60 s, so an age of exactly 60 s is still fresh); a stale cache is kept in `entries` and served while the rebuild runs behind it (line 1122 comment: "A stale index is served and rebuilt behind it."); `entries = []` happens only when there is no cache at all; joins an in-flight build for the same directory; if `Self.building.count >= 2`, awaits `Self.building.values.first` (an arbitrary element of an unordered Dictionary, not necessarily the oldest build) and then `continue`s, re-reading the cache; else starts a build Task that inserts into the cache and removes itself from building. Applies fresh entries only if still current and not cancelled.
FileIndex.build: Entry lowercased path, name = lastPathComponent of the lowercased path, lengthPenalty = min(path.count, 99), isASCII = all UTF-8 bytes < 128.

FileIndex.search: empty needle returns the first limit (8) paths in index order. Scoring: name == needle 1000; name prefix 800; substring of name 600; substring of full lowercased path 400; subsequence of lowercased path 100; minus lengthPenalty. Keeps a top-limit list by insertion (ties keep earlier entries first since insertion is before the first strictly lower score); checks cancellation every 2,048 entries and returns [] when cancelled.

contains(): ASCII fast path with memmem on UTF-8 bytes; falls back to String.contains if the haystack contains byte 13 (carriage return) or storage is not contiguous. isSubsequence(): ASCII byte walk, restarting in grapheme mode on byte 13; non-ASCII uses Character comparison.

FileIndex.list: if Git(directory).isRepository() and listFiles() non-empty, first 60,000 files; else enumerate(): skips hidden files and package descendants, skips names node_modules, build, dist, .build, DerivedData, Pods, target, and any item deeper than level 16 (skipDescendants). The test is `skipped.contains(url.lastPathComponent) || enumerator.level > 16` (line 1278), an exact case-sensitive Set match on the last path component applied before the isDirectory check, so it also skips plain files with those names, not only directories; an item at level > 16 is itself skipped, not just its descendants. It then excludes directories, stores ToolTitles.relativePath(url.path, to: directory), stops at 20,000 results.

B1->B2: 12 changed lines, no behavioural change beyond fonts and one refactor. (1) Line 478 commandSuggestions: the inline provider test 'thread.provider == .codex || .claude || .copilot || .deepseek || .meta || .zai || .pi' became 'thread.provider.supportsCompact'; Provider.swift:151 at B2 lists exactly the same seven providers, so the /compact built-in shows for the same providers. (2) Fixed point sizes became dynamic text styles: attachment notice .system(size: 11) -> .system(.subheadline); Usage popover header .system(size: 12, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.callout, weight: .semibold); DraftChips icons .system(size: 10, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.footnote, weight: .semibold) (command and quote chips); chip labels .system(size: 11, weight: .medium) -> .system(.subheadline, weight: .medium) (command) and .system(size: 11) -> .system(.subheadline) (quote excerpt); chip xmark .system(size: 9, weight: .bold) -> .system(.caption2, weight: .bold) (both chips); SuggestionPopoverRow icon .system(size: 12) -> .system(.callout), title .system(size: 13) -> .system(.body), detail .system(size: 12) -> .system(.callout). Everything else in the file is byte-identical to 1.6.0.

Confirm on a reference capture whether the xmark grew by 1 pt.

feature_notes: B2->B3 removes the static `sizeFormatter: ByteCountFormatter` (countStyle .file) property and its call site `Self.sizeFormatter.string(fromByteCount: Int64(size))`, replacing the one call site with `Int64(size).formatted(.byteCount(style: .file))` -- Swift's newer FormatStyle API in place of the older ByteCountFormatter class, same countStyle. No other line in the file changed. This is a pure API-surface swap with no stated change in rounding, unit thresholds or locale behaviour on Apple's own side; the observable file-size string (e.g. '1.2 MB') is expected to be identical, though this report has not independently verified byte-for-byte string parity between the two APIs across edge values (0 bytes, exactly 1 unit boundary, very large files).

PR-COMPOSER-078 ('The Downloads popover lists the 15 most recently modified...') cites B2 :39-96 for `load()`, which spans the removed 6-line static-formatter block; its expected_result only says 'the formatted size when it is above zero' and never names ByteCountFormatter, so this needs only a line-range recite (39-96 in B2 becomes a shorter span in B3, since 6 lines were deleted with no insertion), not a behaviour reclassification.

The already-built C# port (src/Marrow.App/Views/Composer/DownloadsPopover.cs, unit status DONE) already calls a shared `SwiftFormatters.FileByteCount(size, SwiftFormatters.CurrentLocale.Current)` helper rather than reimplementing ByteCountFormatter inline, so this file's diff requires no code change in the port; the open question is whether that shared helper (part of the F.ICUFormatters unit, a dependency of this unit) was itself validated against ByteCountFormatter's exact output or against `.formatted(.byteCount(style:))`'s, which only matters if the two Apple APIs ever diverge.
unresolved_questions: Confirm F.ICUFormatters' FileByteCount output matches `Int64(_:).formatted(.byteCount(style: .file))` (the new B3 call), not only the retired `ByteCountFormatter(countStyle: .file)` it may have been validated against originally -- not checked in this reading pass.

purpose: A 36-line wrapper that puts a queued follow-up prompt into a PromptEditor titled "Edit follow-up" with Cancel and Save buttons, saving through ThreadRuntime.updateFollowUp and clearing runtime.followUpEdit on either outcome so the edit state lives on the thread, not in this view.

side_effects: runtime.updateFollowUp(edit.id, text: edit.text, attachments: edit.attachments) rewrites the queued follow-up
runtime.followUpEdit = nil on save and on cancel, which is what closes the popover
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI @Bindable (Observation) and the Liquid Glass button styles .glass / .glassProminent (macOS 26 era)
persisted_fields: None directly; the follow-up queue persistence happens inside ThreadRuntime.updateFollowUp

feature_notes: B2->B3 removes every manual NSCursor push/pop call in this file and replaces the grip's cursor entirely with a declarative `.pointerStyle(isDragged ? .grabActive : .grabIdle)` modifier. Deleted: `NSCursor.closedHand.push()` at the start of dragChanged when a new drag begins, `NSCursor.pop()` at the top of dragEnded, and the grip's whole 13-line onHover/onDisappear/onChange(of: isDragged) block that pushed NSCursor.openHand on hover (guarded by `!isDragged`), popped it on hover-end, popped it again on disappear if still hovering, and popped it a third way if isDragged went false while not hovering ('the hover's open hand is still pushed with no leave to pop it'). Added: `.onHover { hovering in isHoveringGrip = hovering }` (icon-brightening only, cursor removed) plus the single `.pointerStyle(...)` modifier. As with TimelineMinimap.swift, the end-user cursor outcome (open/relaxed hand while hovering the grip, closed/grabbing hand while dragging) is very likely preserved by the new API's named grabIdle/grabActive styles, but every one of the old push/pop edge cases the code hand-rolled -- including a documented leak -- no longer has code to leak.

Three spec records (porting/spec/COMPOSER.json) are built directly around the retired mechanism. PR-COMPOSER-159 ('The grip is a 28 by 22 hit area that shows a grab cursor...', status IMPLEMENTED) cites B2 :380-410 quoting the literal `NSCursor.openHand.push()`/`.pop()` calls, lists side_effects 'Pushes and pops a cursor', and its windows_path reads 'An explicit LIFO cursor-owner stack mirroring each push and pop site (port_impacts X8(a))'. PR-COMPOSER-163 ('Releasing over a pair target bundles the rows...') cites B2 :285-298 for dragEnded and explicitly says in its own expected_result 'the held row settles back into its slot on a spring ... and the cursor is popped' -- describing the now-deleted `NSCursor.pop()` call. UI-COMPOSER-052 (the grip's UI record) lists states 'hover pushes the open-hand cursor', 'dragging pushes the closed-hand cursor', and, most significantly, 'a row removed mid-drag with the pointer off the grip leaks one cursor push (upstream defect 53)' -- a documented B2 bug. Since B3's `.pointerStyle` is scoped to the view and has no manual stack to leak, this specific defect-53 leak scenario appears to no longer reproduce upstream, which is a candidate for retire_behaviour_removed pending owner confirmation (exact-parity porting normally means replicating even upstream bugs, but only bugs the pinned source still has).

The already-built C# port (src/Marrow.App/Views/Composer/FollowUpQueueTab.cs, unit status DONE) does not implement either the B2 or the B3 cursor distinction at all: the grip's `Cursor` is set once to a plain `new Cursor(StandardCursorType.Hand)` and never changed between hover and drag (checked directly: no cursor-changing code exists in OnPointerPressed/OnPointerMoved/OnPointerReleased/EndPointerDrag). This is a pre-existing gap versus B2's open-hand/closed-hand distinction, not something newly introduced by this diff, but it means the port currently matches neither B2's nor B3's cursor behaviour, and PR-COMPOSER-159's already-'IMPLEMENTED' status is not actually backed by matching cursor code in this file.
unresolved_questions: Whether UI-COMPOSER-052's 'upstream defect 53' cursor-leak state should be marked retired now that B3's pointerStyle mechanism has no push/pop to leak, or whether the defect needs independent confirmation against the compiled B3 app before retiring a documented-bug requirement -- an owner decision, not a reading question.

Whether FollowUpQueueTab.cs's single static Hand cursor is an accepted, already-ruled-on simplification (an ED/OD this report did not locate) or an outstanding gap that should be filed as its own defect against the DONE unit -- not resolved by this reading pass.

purpose: Defines PromptEditor, the shared 520 pt wide editor body used to edit a queued follow-up or a sent message: a title, a ComposerTextView with Return-to-submit and Escape-to-cancel, the attachment list, a caller-supplied extra section, an add-files button with a recent-downloads popover and an NSOpenPanel fallback, and caller-supplied action buttons. The doc comment at line 27 says "the largest page is measured once, here", but the code does not enforce once: pageHeight is a `private let`, not @State, so the measurement (one NSHostingView per question) re-runs on every QuestionSheet init, while selections/written/page keep their @State values across re-inits.
Single-choice pick (not multiple) on any page but the last calls advance(after: 0.18): the page moves on 0.18 s later. Picking on the last page does not auto-send.
onPick fires only when the tapped choice ends up selected (current.contains(choice.label)); deselecting does not advance.
Single choice toggles: tapping the selected choice clears the question's selection to []; multiple choice appends or removes the label.
Return in the text field calls advance(): on a non-last page it moves on; on the last page it sends only when unansweredCount is 0.
advance() on the last page recomputes answers and sends only if every question has at least one value; otherwise does nothing.

The delayed advance (single-choice pick on a non-last page, `advance(after: 0.18)`) checks `guard page < count - 1` only when called, then spawns an unstored Task that after 0.18 s runs `page += 1` from whatever page is current then, with no bounds re-check and no cancellation. So a dot tap or Previous within the 0.18 s is followed by +1 from the new page (a dot tap to the last page within 0.18 s pushes page to count, past the last page); Skip or Send within the 0.18 s closes the popover and answers, and the task still runs its `page += 1` afterwards on the dismissed sheet.

Answers: per question, the selected labels (full label text, including any ' (Recommended)' suffix) followed by the written text trimmed via String.trimmed, appended only when non-empty. Skip sends an empty dictionary [:].
A question counts as answered when its answer array is non-empty; isComplete means unanswered == 0.

bareLabel strips a trailing " (Recommended)" (case-insensitive compare of the last 14 characters) and marks it recommended; otherwise the label is kept whole and marked recommended if it contains "recommended" anywhere, so the pill can show beside an unstripped label.
Choices are keyed by index (id: \.offset) so identical labels both render, but selection is by label string, so two identical labels select together.
Send order: closePopover?() first so the popover animates away from the badge, then runtime.answer.

purpose: Holds every piece of the software-update story shown on the Settings About page: a parser that turns a GitLab release description into three categorised sections (UpdateReleaseNotesDigest with ReleaseNoteCategory New features / Bug fixes / Refinements), the three tinted tappable cards and their bullet popovers, and the About chrome accessory made of an identity pill (app icon plus "v<version>") and a version pill that is either a status seal (Up to date / Check failed / Not checked yet), the blue "Update & restart" button, or an animated install progress slider. It also contains the frame-driven progress slider itself (an exponential chase of the download fraction, a blue gradient fill revealed by a leading clip, 14 deterministic twinkling sparkles seeded by SplitMix64 and a white head), the unread UpdateAvailableDot, the AboutSoftwareUpdateSection that runs a check when the page opens and plays the post-relaunch celebration sweep with haptics, and the AboutUpdateCheckRow with its "Check now" button and relative last-checked text.

feature_notes:
Notes parsing (lines 103-105): `for line in raw.split(separator: "
", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)` keeps empty lines; each line is `line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)` (Foundation CharacterSet.whitespaces: Unicode general category Zs plus tab, not newlines); lines that are empty, exactly "---", or start with "<" are skipped. Swift Character rule: the separator is the Character "
", and "
" is a single grapheme Character that does not equal "
", so notes with CRLF line endings do not split at all. They arrive as one line; if it starts with "## New features
..." category(forHeader:) (line 153) fails because the lowercased text is not an exact match, isHeader (line 142) is true, current = nil (line 117), nothing is collected, the digest is empty and releaseBody (lines 749-754) falls back to the raw MarkdownView. A port using JS split("
") plus trim() (which also strips ) would show cards for the same notes; to match B2 it must not split on "
".

A bullet is a line whose first character is one of - U+2010 U+2013 U+2014 U+2212 * • followed by a space or tab, with a non-empty trimmed body. Bullets before any recognised section header are dropped. Each bullet has inline markdown stripped (links [text](url) -> text, **bold** -> bold, `code` -> code, applied in that order) and is kept only if non-empty.

A non-bullet line that names a category sets the current section, whether bare or with # heading or ** bold chrome, trailing spaces/tabs/colons trimmed; matching is case-insensitive: "new features" or "new" -> New features; "bug fixes", "fixes" or "bugs" -> Bug fixes; "refinements" or "improvements" -> Refinements.

Any other heading (one or more # followed by space/tab or nothing, or a line that starts and ends with ** and is longer than 4 characters) closes the current section (current = nil), so e.g. a Thanks to contributors section is left out. Plain text lines that are neither leave the current section unchanged.
Sections are emitted in the fixed order New features, Bug fixes, Refinements; empty or missing ones are absent. Bullets are de-duplicated case-insensitively keeping the first occurrence.

Rollup: if the last kept bullet contains a word equal to "extra" (lowercased, punctuation trimmed) that is not the first word, and the preceding word's digit characters parse to an Int > 0, that bullet becomes the section's rollup and its number is rollupCount ("Fixed 12 extra issues…" counts as 12). changeCount = bullets.count + rollupCount.
parse(nil) or parse("") returns an empty digest; parse memoizes the last (raw, digest) pair and returns the cached digest when raw is identical.
The page re-parses only when checker.update?.version changes (.onChange(..., initial: true)). If the digest is empty but the notes are not, the raw notes are rendered as Markdown instead of cards.
Card tap toggles its popover (tapping the open card closes it); a card with no section does nothing and is disabled.

FractionChase: the first advance snaps displayed to target; a target below displayed snaps back down; dt is clamped to [0, 0.25] s; step = remaining * (1 - exp(-dt / max(response, 0.01))), then at least minimumSpeed * dt, capped at the target; within 0.0001 of the target it snaps to the target.

SmoothedUpdateProgressSlider frame clock runs at up to 60 fps and pauses when settled (displayed fraction == target) or while ScrollActivity reports scrolling; settled resets to false whenever target.value changes. The chase is created caught up to target.value so a post-relaunch sweep does not start from zero.

Head x = trackHeight/2 + (width - trackHeight) * clamp(value, 0, 1). Fill opacity is 0 at or below 0.012, 1 at or above 0.05, smoothstep t*t*(3-2t) in between. The fill is revealed by a rounded clip of width max(headX, trackHeight/2) and corner radius height/2.

Sparkle motion: twinkle = 0.5 + 0.5*sin(time*speed + phase); horizontal drift = sin(time*speed*0.31 + phase*2.1) * drift; sparkle canvas runs at up to 30 fps and pauses when there are no sparkles or while scrolling.

SparkleParticle.field uses SplitMix64: state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15; z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9; z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB; z ^= z >> 31; value = Double(z >> 11) / 2^53. Per particle the draws are in order x = r, y = 0.12 + r*0.76, size = 1.2 + r*1.6, speed = 0.9 + r*2.4, phase = r*2π, drift = 0.6 + r*1.4. Seed 0x5EED_D80B, count 14.

Version pill logic: isReady = checker.updateAvailable && checker.update != nil && !progress.showsProgressUI. Standing precedence: lastError != nil -> failed; else lastCheckedAt == nil -> unchecked; else upToDate. While installing, slider response is 0.15 with reduce motion, else 0.72 while phase == .celebrating, else 0.3; minimumSpeed is 0.12 while celebrating, else 0.

Standing tooltips verbatim: upToDate "Droppy Code <AppInfo.version> is the latest version"; failed = checker.lastError, or "The last check did not reach GitLab"; unchecked "Droppy Code has not asked GitLab for a release yet".

releaseDetail (lines 781-791) joins with " · ": "Released <date, .long, no time>" when releasedAt exists, then `ByteCountFormatStyle(style: .file).format(size)` when size exists, then always "Update & restart installs it in place and relaunches." The .file style output is decided by Foundation, not this file: Apple documents the .file count style as the platform file-size style, which on macOS is the decimal (1000-based) style, e.g. "12.3 MB" for about 12,300,000 bytes, not 1024-based. A Windows port must format with 1000-based units (not StrFormatByteSize, which is 1024-based) and pin the exact digits and locale from a macOS sample.

Celebration sweep (startCelebrationSweep, lines 795-818): first `celebration?.cancel()` cancels any earlier sweep, then `let reduceMotion = reduceMotion` snapshots reduce motion once when the sweep starts (a later change to reduce motion does not affect a sweep already running); then in a @MainActor Task: wait 550 ms; abort unless !Task.isCancelled and progress.phase == .celebrating; finishCelebrationSweep(); with reduce motion: haptic .alignment then 900 ms; otherwise 900 ms, haptic .alignment, 450 ms, haptic .levelChange, 700 ms (cancellation checked between steps); then completeCelebration(). Leaving the page mid-sweep completes the celebration at once.

Check row detail verbatim: while checking "Asking GitLab for the latest release…"; otherwise checked = "Checked <relative named date>." or "Not checked yet."; with an error "<error> <checked>"; with a ready update "Droppy Code <version> is ready to install. <checked>"; otherwise "Droppy Code checks GitLab for new versions a few times a day. <checked>".

B1->B2: (1) strippedInlineMarkdown no longer uses three cached NSRegularExpression statics (linkPattern, boldPattern, codePattern) with a stripped(_:with:) helper and "$1" template; it now uses Swift Regex literals with String.replacing and the first capture, same three patterns in the same order, doc comment says it is cheap because parse memoizes. (2) Fixed-point fonts switched to system text styles: card count size 11 -> .subheadline; popover title size 13 semibold -> .body semibold; popover version size 11 -> .subheadline; bullets size 13 -> .body; rollup size 12 -> .callout; identity pill version size 12 semibold -> .callout semibold; both version pill titles size 12 semibold -> .callout semibold; Release notes link size 12 medium -> .callout medium and its arrow size 10 semibold -> .footnote semibold. (3) Popover colours changed: version text .tertiary -> Chrome.secondaryText, bullets .secondary -> Chrome.secondaryText, rollup .tertiary -> Chrome.secondaryText. The card title stays .system(size: 12.5, weight: .medium). File shrank from 852 to 845 lines; no strings, logic or timings changed.

purpose: New in B3 (commit d70cff8fe 'refactor: audit cleanups ... shared MCP and provider code'): a non-final @MainActor base class that owns the one floating NSPanel, the Escape key monitor and the present/close lifecycle that MCPKeyPanel (width 380) and MCPSetupPanel (width 400) previously each duplicated verbatim in B2. present(_:) measures the SwiftUI content at the fixed width, sizes the panel to max(height, 100), parks it 24 points in from the top-right of NSScreen.main's visibleFrame, installs the Escape monitor and orders it front without activating the app; close() removes the monitor and orders the panel out. feature_notes: Status A: the file does not exist at B2. Its entire body (present sizing/placement/orderFront :17-25, close :28-31, makePanel :33-56, startEscapeMonitor :58-65, stopEscapeMonitor :67-70) is the code B2 duplicated in MCPKeyPanel.swift (B2 :22-30, :33-36, :38-61, :63-75) and MCPSetupPanel.swift (B2 :34-43, :45-49, :63-86, :88-100); the B3 diffs of those two files delete exactly that code and replace it with 'final class X: FloatingGuidePanel', 'private init() { super.init(width: 380|400) }' and 'present(content)'.

The only textual differences from the B2 bodies are the literal 380/400 becoming the stored width, 'private var panel' becoming 'private(set) var panel' on the base, and MCPSetupPanel's close becoming 'override func close() { presentedEntryID = nil; super.close() }'. The override reorders the B2 sequence (stopEscapeMonitor, presentedEntryID = nil, orderOut) to (presentedEntryID = nil, stopEscapeMonitor, orderOut); all three are synchronous main-actor steps, so nothing observable changes.
Escape in the setup panel still clears presentedEntryID: the monitor calls self.close(), which dispatches to MCPSetupPanel's override because FloatingGuidePanel is a non-final class.
Each subclass singleton still owns its own NSPanel and its own escape monitor, so the key panel and the setup panel remain two separate windows, exactly as in B2.

No spec record cites FloatingGuidePanel.swift yet. PR-MCP-214, PR-MCP-215, PR-MCP-216, PR-MCP-220, UI-MCP-070 and UI-MCP-078 cite the B2 MCPKeyPanel/MCPSetupPanel line ranges whose code now lives here; their behaviour text remains correct and only their source_evidence (plus the ':41' / ':66 .nonactivatingPanel' pointers in the PR-MCP-215 windows_path and the UI-MCP-070/078 notes, now FloatingGuidePanel.swift:36) needs re-citing.

purpose: Renders the Hydra pairs cookbook, a fixed 460x540 panel opened as a popover from the Hydra settings page's Pairs section. It resolves every HydraCookbook recipe against the current provider registry and settings, lists the recipes that resolve to a concrete HydraPair as ready rows each with a one-click Add button (or an "Added" label once the pair is in settings), and lists recipes whose provider is not set up under a dimmed "Needs a provider" heading. When the panel appears it loads the model catalog of every ready provider so recipes can pick their models.

purpose: Builds the Settings page for Hydra, the feature where one chat leads a team of helper "heads": a hero card with the master hydraEnabled switch, then sections for Heads, Messages, When the team is done and Pairs that all dim to 0.5 opacity and disable while Hydra is off, and an always-enabled informational Where heads run section. It binds a dozen AppSettings hydra* flags to ChromeRow toggles, visual pickers and a segmented head-cap picker, lists the configured HydraPairs with a hover edit affordance and a remove button, and adds pairs by picking the first installed and enabled provider without a pair yet. The file also contains the HydraPairEditor popover that edits a pair's name, lead provider, model and effort, heads provider, model and effort, and heads-at-once cap, with rules that reset dependent fields when the provider or model changes and loads provider catalogs on demand.

Changing lead provider (only if different): inside model.updateHydraPair `guard $0.provider != provider else { return }`; sets provider, clears orchestratorModel and orchestratorEffort; if workerProvider == nil clears workerModel and workerEffort; else if workerProvider == new provider sets workerProvider = nil. `Task { await registry.loadCatalog(provider) }` (line 405) sits outside the update closure, so it runs whenever the binding setter is called, including a re-pick of the same provider where the guard made the edit a no-op (whether GlassPickerButton calls the setter on a re-pick is decided in GlassPickerButton, not this file).

Changing lead model: sets orchestratorModel; clears orchestratorEffort if the new model option exists and does not list that effort. Same rule for the heads model and workerEffort against headsProvider.

Changing heads provider: inside the update closure `let chosen = provider == $0.provider ? nil : provider` then `guard $0.workerProvider != chosen else { return }`; otherwise sets workerProvider = chosen and clears workerModel and workerEffort. Outside the closure `if let provider { Task { await registry.loadCatalog(provider) } }` (line 455) loads the raw picked provider, not `chosen`, and runs even when the guard returned early (it would also run for a provider equal to the lead, though the options at line 443 exclude pair.provider). The picker shows nil unless pair.sendsHeadsElsewhere.
Name field: empty text stores name = nil; the popover's auto focus is dropped on appear so the caret only appears after a click.
catalogProviders(pair) = [provider, headsProvider] when sendsHeadsElsewhere else [provider]; the editor's .task keyed on it loads each catalog in order.

purpose: The Settings MCP page. It stacks a lead card ('Connected servers lead' with a hover info popover of three facts), a Connected section listing connected catalog servers sorted by name (switch, tool count and version, a menu with Refresh / Show tools / Disconnect), the Custom section of the user's own servers with an Add server row, and one two-column LazyVGrid per MCP category of server cards whose button reads Connect, Sign in, Waiting/Connecting, Fix it, Try again or Sign in again by MCPConnectionState; a newly connected card celebrates for 900 ms with a SettleChime before moving to Connected unless Reduce Motion is on. It also hosts MCPCustomEditor (name, stdio/http kind, command, one-argument-per-line args, URL, environment variables or headers whose values can be locked into the Keychain, save through mcp.saveCustom and saveCustomValues, refresh when an edited server was connected), the hover-or-click info popover with Connects/Needs/Tools/docs link, FlowLayout chips, and MCPIcon.

purpose: MCPSetupPanel.swift holds the singleton floating panel MCPSetupPanel.shared that appears when an MCP server refuses on its own side (the needsSetup state): the first presentation for a server opens the guide's pageURL in the browser, and a re-entry guard keyed on the recorded entry id makes a repeated present for the same server only order the panel front, so a failing re-check never reopens the page or rebuilds the steps. It also defines MCPSetupPanelView, the SwiftUI content: header (MCPIcon 26, entry name, guide title, xmark close), the guide reason, numbered step rows, the guide.pageLabel button, Check again or a Checking spinner, the post-check status line (needsSetup warning or failed message), and a 'Connected · N tools' success view that closes the panel 1.2 s after the server connects. In B3 the class no longer owns its NSPanel, its Escape key monitor or its placement code: it subclasses the new FloatingGuidePanel (FloatingGuidePanel.swift) with width 400 and keeps only presentedEntryID, isPresenting, present(entry:guide:model:), a close() override and fit(height:).

feature_notes: SOURCE FACT: Grip cursor mechanism rewritten. B2 pushed NSCursor.closedHand in dragChanged on a new drag (B2 :120) and popped in dragEnded (B2 :139); the grip pushed NSCursor.openHand on hover (suppressed while dragged), popped on leave, on disappear while hovered, and on drag release away from the grip (B2 :185-199). B3 removes all NSCursor calls from this file: the grip's onHover now only sets isHoveringGrip (:183) and the cursor is the declarative `.pointerStyle(isDragged ? .grabActive : .grabIdle)` (:184). The doc on isHoveringGrip changed from "for the grab cursor" to "which brightens its icon" (:170). Consequence for the spec: PR-SETTINGS-186's cursor text (push/pop, three balancing guards, Windows path 'balance every push with a pop') describes behaviour that no longer exists; the cursor is now a per-view style keyed on isDragged, with no global cursor stack and so no stranded-cursor failure mode.

SOURCE FACT: The provider disclosure header (B2 :341-364, inline in ProviderModelsSection) was extracted into a new non-private `struct CollapsibleProviderHeader` (:415-448) taking `subject`; ProviderModelsSection now calls it with subject "model list" (:326) and SettingsView.swift:647 calls it with subject "provider settings". Help, a11y value, hint and header trait are the same strings as B2 for this page ("Hide the model list" / "Show the model list" / "Shows or hides the model list"), now built by interpolation `"Hide the \(subject)"`. No observable change on the Models page; ChromeQuietButtonStyle now has a single use site (ModelsSettingsPage.swift:440) serving both pages.

purpose: A small @MainActor @Observable object that tracks whether a settings pane is being scrolled right now, reports that to the global ScrollActivity under one fixed pane UUID so effects that should not run under a moving finger rest, and exposes a separate isFrozen flag that tells settings rows to stop hovering and animating while content slides under the pointer.
state_owned: isScrolling: Bool (observable, private setter)
isFrozen: Bool (observable, private setter)
isCoasting: Bool (@ObservationIgnored)
settle: Task<Void, Never>? (@ObservationIgnored, the debounce task)
side_effects: Registers and unregisters with the global ScrollActivity.shared singleton under the fixed pane UUID
Spawns a @MainActor Task that sleeps 150 milliseconds as the settle debounce, cancelling the previous one on each note()
platform_assumptions: Swift Observation (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored) and @MainActor isolation
Structured concurrency with Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(150)) and Task.isCancelled
Assumes a caller that can distinguish an active drag or wheel movement from a coasting flick, which on macOS comes from NSEvent scroll phase and momentum phase
ui_elements: No views: it drives row hover suppression through isFrozen and effect pausing through isScrolling elsewhere
feature_notes: note() is documented as 'a frame of movement': the first call flips isScrolling true and calls ScrollActivity.shared.setScrolling(true, timeline: Self.pane, reporter: self); every call restarts a 150ms debounce, after which isScrolling and isCoasting go false, isFrozen is cleared if set, and ScrollActivity is told scrolling stopped.
isFrozen is raised in note() only when `!isCoasting && !isFrozen`, so once the flick is coasting, further momentum frames do not re-freeze the rows.
coast() sets isCoasting = true and clears isFrozen immediately, so a click that stops a flick always reaches its target; the comment names this 'the chat timeline's rule'.
end() cancels the settle task, sets it to nil, clears isFrozen and isCoasting, then `guard isScrolling else { return }` so it only reports scrolling stopped when it had reported it started.
The pane key is a single `private static let pane = UUID()` shared by every instance, so all settings panes report under one timeline id rather than one per instance.
The settle task guards `guard let self, !Task.isCancelled else { return }` before mutating state, and captures self weakly.
unresolved_questions: The callers of note(), coast() and end() are not in this file, so which NSEvent phases map to coast() versus note() cannot be confirmed here.
ScrollActivity.shared's semantics - what pauses when a timeline reports scrolling and what the `reporter:` argument is used for - are defined elsewhere.
Whether isFrozen is consumed by every settings row or only some is not determinable from this file.

purpose: Implements the Shortcuts settings page: one card per AppShortcut.Section, each row naming a shortcut with a fixed-width recorder control, followed by a read-only "Composer" card listing six built-in chords that cannot be changed. It also contains the whole shortcut-recording machinery: the Keycap model and its drawn 3D keycap view, the popover that shows live keycaps with a verdict tint and Clear / Reset to default actions, and ShortcutRecordingSession, which installs a local NSEvent monitor, judges each chord against ShortcutStore on key-down and commits it 300 ms after every key is released.

begin: closes any active session first, resets latched/heldKeyCode/verdict/message, seeds heldModifiers from NSEvent.modifierFlags intersected with KeyChord.allowedModifiers, shows caps, then installs the monitor for [.keyDown, .keyUp, .flagsChanged] and the resign-active observer

Monitor (lines 545-554): `guard let self, self.isActive else { return event }` passes every event through unchanged when the session is inactive; event types other than flagsChanged/keyDown/keyUp return the event; otherwise the handler runs and the event is swallowed (return nil). keyDown: repeats ignored (`guard !event.isARepeat`); `if keyCode == 53, flags.isEmpty { cancel(); return }` runs before `guard !isFinishing else { return }`, so plain Esc cancels even during the 300 ms commit wait; Esc with an allowed modifier is judged as an ordinary chord; otherwise (unless finishing) records heldKeyCode and heldModifiers = flags and judges KeyChord(keyCode:modifiers:)
judge: store.refusal(for: chord, replacing: shortcut) non-nil gives verdict .rejected with message = refusal text; nil gives .accepted and clears the message; the chord is latched either way

letGo runs when the last key and modifiers are released: accepted sets isFinishing, waits 300 ms (Task.sleep .milliseconds(300)), then if still active calls onCommit(latched) and closes; rejected clears the latch and returns to listening; listening just refreshes
flagsChanged: when no modifiers remain and no key is held, letGo; otherwise refresh caps; ignored while finishing (except for tracking heldModifiers)
keyUp only counts for the held key code; with no modifiers held it triggers letGo

refreshCaps (lines 659-674): `if let latched, verdict != .listening` shows Keycap.caps(for: latched); else `let modifiers = Keycap.modifierCaps(for: heldModifiers, phase: .pressed); if modifiers.isEmpty { next = [Keycap.ghostCommand] } else if let heldKeyCode { modifiers + key cap } else { modifiers + [Keycap.ghostKey] }`. So the single ghost ⌘ appears whenever no modifier is held, even while a key is held (when no latched non-listening verdict applies); the held key is shown only together with at least one modifier. caps are only reassigned when different
close() cancels finishTask, removes the monitor and observer, clears isActive/isFinishing and calls onClose once (which sets isPresenting = false)

purpose: Draws the "Token activity" heatmap that leads Settings > General: a header with Daily/Weekly/Cumulative mode chips, a one-canvas grid of week columns with square cells coloured on a five-step accent ladder, a strip of month labels, and a footer with the sum of every value in TokenLedger.shared.dailyTotals (`ledger.dailyTotals.values.reduce(0, +)`, line 91; this file applies no year filter, and whether dailyTotals holds only one year is decided in TokenLedger, which was not read; only the fallback tooltip "Total tokens recorded this year." says year) and a Less-to-More legend. It is plain page content, not a card, and keeps its mode view-local; the grid is rebuilt from TokenLedger.shared.dailyTotals only when the totals or the mode change, and a mode switch blends each cell from its old to its new colour over 0.45 s through an animatable modifier.

purpose: WallpaperCard is the SwiftUI Settings card that lets the user put a picture of their own behind the app's glass. It shows a 150 pt tall clickable/droppable preview (the chosen image with a 60% sized glass mock window over it, or an empty drop placeholder), a "Wallpaper" row with Remove and Choose/Change buttons, and, only when a wallpaper exists, a "Softness" row whose 0...1 slider blurs the picture and which offers a reset-to-sharp button when softness is above 0.005. All state lives in the WallpaperStore.shared singleton; the card itself only owns the drag-hover flag and drives an NSOpenPanel (sheet on the key window, else a free-standing panel) whose picked URL is passed to store.install(from:). launch() refuses when from.width <= 1 or from.height <= 1, and refuses entirely when Reduce Motion is enabled
launch() removes any existing glide for the same threadID before appending, so a thread has at most one ghost in the air
A launch is aimed at a fallback rect just past the list's edge, so if the new row never reports a frame the ghost slips out under the clip instead of landing

land() re-targets a glide only when the glide exists, is younger than the 0.5 second landingWindow, and its direction matches the settled flag; the latest report inside the window wins and the interpolation absorbs the re-targeting
Per-thread ObservedValue<Bool> hiding cells mean a launch, landing or finish re-renders only the two rows of that glide plus the layer, not every row in the list
setHiding writes only when the value actually changes, so a row is never re-rendered for a write that said what it already showed
arrive() runs at settlingDuration - 0.12 seconds and un-hides the real row so it shows under the ghost's last frames; finish() removes the ghost 0.12 seconds later, so the handover never shows a gap
finish() re-derives hiding as glides.contains { $0.threadID == threadID && !$0.hasArrived }, so a thread relaunched meanwhile stays hidden
Geometry interpolates x, y, width and height linearly in the spring-driven progress p, so the ghost resizes as well as moves between the two row frames
lift = min(smoothstep(0, 0.12, p), 1 - smoothstep(0.7, 1, p)): the row lifts within the first 12 percent of the flight and has set back down through the last 30 percent
fill = max(departureFill + (arrivalFill - departureFill) * p, 0.12 * lift), so an unfilled row still shows a faint plate at up to 0.12 while airborne
smoothstep is t * t * (3 - 2 * t) with t = (x - edge0) / (edge1 - edge0) clamped to 0...1
The keyframe track is a single SpringKeyframe(1.0, spring: RowGlideAnimator.spring) from an initial value of 0.0, triggered by hasStarted flipping true in onAppear
render() snapshots any Face view at the given size, aligned .topLeading, with the colorScheme forced into the environment so a ghost matches the theme it was captured in
hasLanded is set by land() but is never read anywhere in this file

purpose: The thread sidebar, shown in the window column or in the Threads popover (inPopover, which closes on selection). It holds the 'Search threads' field with arrow-key result walking, the bell ActivityViewToggle, a lazy list in either the project layout (projects with counts, pinned then open threads, a Settled header that folds settled threads) or the activity layout ('Needs attention', 'Pinned', Today/Yesterday/weekday/date groups, Settled), helper rows with a dotted connector, Hydra head glyph cards (twelve shown, the rest behind a chevron) and folded-helper stubs, then 'Add project' (NSOpenPanel) and 'Settings' with an update dot. One list-wide 4 pt DragGesture reorders open thread rows live among their peers with spring slides and a haptic per swap; rows show hover actions, a settle check, an archive button with a Genie ghost, a fold chevron, rename/delete/archive popovers anchored on the row, and context menus built from snapshots through SidebarMenuRequests. Placement, helper grouping, item and search caches keep re-renders cheap, and MinuteClock ticks relative times once a minute.

purpose: New in 1.6.2: a @MainActor enum TerminalFont whose single public entry point preferred(fallbackSize:) picks the NSFont the embedded SwiftTerm view draws with, so that a Starship or powerline prompt's Nerd Font icons render instead of empty boxes. It reads the font the user configured in Ghostty (plain-text config), iTerm2 (defaults 'New Bookmarks' / 'Normal Font') and Terminal.app (archived NSFont in the default profile), ordering running terminals first, then prefers a configured font that covers four Nerd Font probe glyphs, else that font's installed Nerd Font sibling family, else any installed family whose name contains 'nerd font', else the configured font itself, and finally the monospaced system font.

persisted_fields: Reads, never writes. Ghostty config keys: "font-family" (FIRST occurrence wins: `case "font-family" where name == nil:`; comma list allowed, first entry taken, spaces and double quotes trimmed) and "font-size" (`case "font-size": if let points = Double(value), points > 0 { size = CGFloat(points) }` has no such guard, so it runs on every matching line and the LAST valid font-size in the file wins; default 12 when absent).
Terminal.app domain com.apple.Terminal: "Default Window Settings" (profile name, default "Basic"), "Window Settings" dictionary, the profile entry's "Font" (Data, archived NSFont).

iTerm2 domain com.googlecode.iterm2: "New Bookmarks" array of dictionaries, each "Normal Font" string formatted as PostScript name, a space, then the size (e.g. last space-separated token parsed as Double).
ui_elements: No UI. Default fallback size 12 pt; final fallback NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular).
feature_notes: preferred(): configured = configuredFonts(); returns the first configured font where hasNerdGlyphs is true; otherwise, if any configured font exists, returns nerdSibling(of: first) ?? firstInstalledNerdFont(size: first.pointSize) ?? first; with no configured font returns firstInstalledNerdFont(size: fallbackSize) ?? monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: fallbackSize, weight: .regular).

configuredFonts(): readers in fixed order ghostty, iTerm2, Terminal; the running ones (by bundle identifier) come first in that order, then the non-running ones; compactMap calls every reader, so all three sources are read each time.

Ghostty parse: per file, lines trimmed of whitespace, lines starting with "#" and lines without "=" skipped, key and value split at the first "=" and trimmed. size resets to 12 for each file. The first file that yields a non-empty name that resolve() can turn into a font wins; otherwise the second file is tried; otherwise nil.

Ghostty comment handling: only whole lines whose trimmed text starts with "#" are skipped (line 41 `guard !line.hasPrefix("#"), let equal = line.firstIndex(of: "=") else { continue }`). A trailing comment stays in the value: `font-size = 14 # big` gives the value "14 # big", `Double(value)` is nil, and the size is silently left at its previous value (12 by default). The same trailing text would stay in a font-family value, since only spaces and double quotes are trimmed from it.
Ghostty config URL order: home + "Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config", then home + ".config/ghostty/config".

iTermFont iterates every bookmark in array order (it does not look up the default profile GUID) and returns the first whose "Normal Font" parses to a size and for which `NSFont(name: parts.dropLast().joined(separator: " "), size: CGFloat(size))` (line 87) is non-nil. This is a DIRECT NSFont(name:size:) call, not the resolve() helper: unlike ghosttyFont (line 55 `resolve(name, size: size)`), there is no fallback to a normalized family-name match, so a name that is not an exact PostScript or family name gives nil for that bookmark and the loop moves on to the next.
terminalFont uses profile = defaults "Default Window Settings" ?? "Basic" and returns nil if 'Window Settings', the profile entry or its 'Font' Data is missing, or if unarchiving fails.

Nerd probes (line 96): U+E0B0, U+E0B6, U+F015, U+F0035, built with `.compactMap(UnicodeScalar.init)`; hasNerdGlyphs requires all four to be in coveredCharacterSet (`nerdProbes.allSatisfy { covered.contains($0) }`). The file's own comment (lines 94-95) groups them as "a powerline cap, two Font Awesome marks and a Material one from the supplementary plane"; that is the source's description (so it counts one powerline cap, not two). Which Nerd Font range each code point belongs to is not stated beyond that comment.
normalized(name): lowercased, spaces and "-" removed, then "nerdfont" replaced by "nf" (so "GeistMono Nerd Font" and "Geist Mono NF" both become "geistmononf").

nerdSibling(of:): target = normalized(familyName) + "nf"; first installed family whose normalized name equals target, opened at the same point size. A family that is already a Nerd Font variant yields a target ending in "nfnf" and finds nothing.
firstInstalledNerdFont(size:): first family in availableFontFamilies whose name localizedCaseInsensitiveContains "nerd font".
resolve(name:size:): NSFont(name:size:) first; else the first installed family whose normalized name equals normalized(name).

B1->B2: added in 1.6.2 (the whole 138-line file is new; diff shows 138 insertions). TerminalStore.swift switched from NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular) to TerminalFont.preferred() in the same release.

Whether NSFont(name:) resolving a family name (rather than a PostScript name) picks the Regular face on every family; the file relies on it but does not say.

purpose: TerminalStore.swift holds the model side of the embedded terminal: TerminalSession wraps one SwiftTerm LocalProcessTerminalView running the user's login shell in a pseudo terminal with Droppy-specific environment variables, applies theme colours only when the appearance changes, and can tell through sysctl whether the shell owns the terminal foreground. TerminalStore is the @Observable per-thread registry of sessions and the selected session, with open, run-script, ensure, restart-in-place, close, close-all and terminate-all operations; a private TerminalBridge delegate marks a session not running when its process exits.

terminate() is `guard isRunning else { return }; view.terminate(); isRunning = false` (lines 59-63): it kills the process through SwiftTerm only while isRunning is true, and is a no-op once the shell has already exited (processEnded() set isRunning = false). close(), restart(), closeAll and terminateAll all call it, so they do not call view.terminate() on an exited shell.

Caret colour Chrome.accentNSColor; selection background accent.withAlphaComponent(0.3). Both are set inside applyAppearance AFTER `guard appliedDark != isDark else { return }` (line 48), so a change of the theme's accent while dark/light stays the same never reaches an open session's caret or selection; only a light/dark flip (or a new/restarted session, whose appliedDark starts nil) re-reads Chrome.accentNSColor.

Default tab title "Terminal N" where N = sessions(for: threadID).count + 1 at open time (lines 120-121: `let number = sessions(for: threadID).count + 1` and `title ?? "Terminal \(number)"`). There is no running counter, so numbers repeat after a close: with "Terminal 1" and "Terminal 2" open, closing "Terminal 1" and opening a new one gives a second "Terminal 2". Parity keeps this; a monotonically increasing counter would diverge.
feature_notes: Environment: LoginEnvironment.current plus TERM="xterm-256color", COLORTERM="truecolor", TERM_PROGRAM="Droppy Code", DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT=<directory>; passed as "KEY=VALUE" strings.

execName is "-" + last path component of the shell; with no command args are []; with a command args are ["-l", "-i", "-c", "<command>; exec <shell> -l"] so the tab drops into an interactive login shell after the script.
foregroundJobIsTheShell returns false for pid <= 0 or a failed sysctl; true when e_tpgid == e_pgid.

processTerminated arrives from SwiftTerm and hops to the main actor to call processEnded() (isRunning = false). The other three delegate callbacks are empty (terminal title changes and cwd updates are ignored).
selected(for:): the session whose id equals selection[threadID], else the last session.
open: appends and selects the new session. run(script) opens with title script.name and command script.command.
ensureTerminal opens a default session only if the thread has none.

restart: terminate old (no-op if already exited), create a fresh TerminalSession with same threadID, directory and title and command nil (a script tab restarts as a plain shell), replace it at the same index (append if not found), select it. Because it constructs a new TerminalSession, TerminalFont.preferred() runs again and the new view's appliedDark starts nil, so font and colours are re-derived at that moment.
close: terminate, remove, and if it was selected select the thread's last remaining session (nil if none).
closeAll(for:) terminates each and removes the thread's entries; terminateAll terminates every session without removing them.

purpose: Declares the eight-page content script of the first-run welcome tour as a static array of TourPage values (asset image name, title, description) inside enum Tour, derives the spelled-out theme count from AppTheme.allCases so the themes page copy cannot drift, and exposes Tour.present(model:) which hands the pages to TourWindowController.shared and sets settings.hasSeenTour = true on both finish and close.

Tour.themeCount: computed on each access, no storage

Opens the borderless floating tour window through TourWindowController.shared.present

Page 2: image "tour-hydra", title "Meet Hydra", body "One chat, many heads. The lead writes the briefs, sends helper agents out in parallel, each in a copy of your project, and their work lands back in your checkout."

Page 3: image "tour-pairs", title "Pair a strong lead with quick heads", body "Put a Claude lead over Gemini or OpenCode heads. Pick the pair from the model picker, cap how many heads run at once, and give each side its own effort."

Page 5: image "tour-threads", title "Threads, when you want them", body "Hide the sidebar and the chat has the whole window. The Threads button brings the list back as a floating panel: the same search, the same rows, and it goes away as soon as you pick one."

Page 6: image "tour-recipes", title "Recipes for a team", body "Hydra's cookbook holds ready-made pairs: a lead, its heads and the effort each side gets, from the providers you have signed in. Pick one in Settings and every new chat starts on it."

themeCount spells out AppTheme.allCases.count with NumberFormatter .spellOut in en_US, then uppercases only the first character: spelled.prefix(1).uppercased() + spelled.dropFirst(). At commit dd2b86e AppTheme declares 26 cases (system, light, dark, catppuccinMocha, catppuccinLatte, dracula, tokyoNight, nord, gruvbox, gruvboxLight, oneDark, everforest, kanagawa, rosePine, solarizedDark, solarizedLight, githubDark, githubLight, ayu, nightOwl, monokai, claude, claudeLight, codex, cursor, matrix), so page 8 reads "Twenty-six themes, from Catppuccin to Kanagawa, ...".
The doc comment explains why this is computed rather than literal: the copy said twenty-five after the twenty-sixth theme was added.
Both finishing the tour (Done) and closing it with the checkmark mark it seen: onFinish and onClose each set hasSeenTour = true, so the tour is not shown again after either path.
Tour.present passes no width/continueButtonTitle/finishButtonTitle, so the controller's defaults apply (width 660, "Continue", "Done").

purpose: TourWindowController is the @MainActor singleton that presents the welcome tour in its own borderless, transparent, floating NSWindow, centred over the visible main window titled "Droppy Code" (or the screen). Before showing it measures every page's bottom panel with an off-screen NSHostingView of TourBottomPanelSizingView and fixes the card height to image height plus the tallest panel, turning off the hosting view's sizing options so the window never grows or shrinks between pages; it re-fronts an existing tour instead of opening a second.

Flow: Use reset -> phase .confirming(id); Cancel -> .idle; Reset now -> spend() (lines 293-307): `phase = .applying(row.id)`, then `settle?.cancel()` (cancels the previous Task, e.g. one still in its 4-second sleep), then `settle = Task { ... }` that awaits consumeResetCredit(provider, row.credit?.id) and sets `phase = .done(outcome)` or `.failed(error.localizedDescription)` with no cancellation check, then `try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(4))`, and only the reset to `.idle` is guarded by `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }`. A cancelled task whose request is still pending would still write .done/.failed when it returns; the UI makes that overlap hard to reach because "Use reset" is `.disabled(isApplying)` while any row is .applying and "Reset now" only shows in .confirming. onDisappear cancels settle.

purpose: WindowManager.swift is the factory and cache for Droppy Code's two real windows (the main thread window and the Settings window) plus an unsaved capture window used for website screenshots (the line 74 comment says "at a fixed size", meaning the caller-given size; the window itself is built with resizable: true at line 77); it builds each as a plain titled AppKit NSWindow of a DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow subclass with a transparent, full-size-content title bar and puts a SwiftUI tree inside a FrameHostingView. It owns the single AppModel instance of the app (let model = AppModel()), so every hosted SwiftUI tree gets the same model through HostedEnvironment. The file also defines WindowLiveResize, an @Observable per-window flag flipped by AppKit's live-resize notifications that views read to hold their settle animations and heavier layout work while the window or a pane is being resized, and HostedEnvironment, the modifier that injects the model, the live-resize object, the app zoom (new in 1.6.2), the capsule button border shape and the theme accent tint into every window root and every separately hosted chat column. HostedRoot additionally maps the chosen theme to both SwiftUI's preferredColorScheme and the process-wide NSApp.appearance.

Coordinate system: AppKit origin is bottom-left and y grows UP; Windows/Electron origin is top-left and y grows DOWN. The x formulas map unchanged, but the y clamp does NOT: line 52 `frame.origin.y = min(max(frame.origin.y, visible.minY), visible.maxY - frame.height)` keeps the window's TOP edge (title bar) on screen when the window is taller than visible.height, because origin.y is the bottom edge. Copying it literally as `min(max(top, wa.y), wa.y + wa.height - h)` would keep the BOTTOM edge instead. Windows equivalent that keeps upstream's behaviour: `top = max(min(top, wa.y + wa.height - h), wa.y)` (min first, then max). The centring midpoint formulas (lines 48-49) are symmetric and map directly. screen.visibleFrame (outside knowledge: excludes menu bar and Dock) -> Electron display.workArea.

window.center() (lines 43, 68, 82) is AppKit's NSWindow.center(). Outside knowledge (Apple documentation, not this source): it places the window exactly centred horizontally and 'somewhat above center vertically' on its screen, not at the exact vertical centre. Electron's BrowserWindow.center() or (workArea - size) / 2 would sit lower than upstream for the first-run main window (no saved frame), for a newly built Settings window, and for every fallback Settings placement (no main window, main hidden or miniaturised). The exact AppKit vertical offset is not given in this file.

`.rounded()` (lines 48-49) is Swift's FloatingPoint.rounded() with no argument. Outside knowledge (Swift standard library): its rule is .toNearestOrAwayFromZero, so halves round away from zero (-10.5 -> -11, 10.5 -> 11). JS Math.round rounds halves toward +infinity (Math.round(-10.5) === -10), so the port must use `Math.sign(v) * Math.round(Math.abs(v))` to match on displays left of or above the primary.

`(main.screen ?? NSScreen.main)?.visibleFrame` (line 50): main.screen is the screen the main window is on; outside knowledge (Apple documentation): NSScreen.main is the screen containing the window that has keyboard focus, not the primary display. Electron mapping: screen.getDisplayMatching(mainWindow.getBounds()), falling back to the display of BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow(), not screen.getPrimaryDisplay(). Source fact: the clamp sits inside `if let visible = ...`, so when both are nil NO clamping happens and the rounded centred frame is applied as is.

Style mask `.resizable` (line 94, only when resizable is true). Outside knowledge (AppKit, not this source): a resizable titled window gets an enabled green zoom button and is full-screen capable by default; without .resizable the zoom button is disabled. So main (resizable: true, line 63) and capture (resizable: true, line 77) windows can be zoomed / made full screen, and the Settings window (resizable: false, line 81) cannot. Checked in B2 DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/WindowChrome.swift: configure(_:) (lines 107-132) does not touch collectionBehavior or the window buttons, and placeTrafficLights lays out .closeButton, .miniaturizeButton and .zoomButton with isHidden = false. purpose: Holds the two verbatim system-prompt blocks the app injects for its anti-slop writing and editing guidance: the full enabled block headed '[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance]' and the short cancellation block headed '[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance: off]' used when the toggle is off.
state_owned: static let enabledInstructions (multi-line String literal: header line plus 4 paragraphs)
static let disabledInstructions (multi-line String literal: header line plus 1 sentence pair)
platform_assumptions: None beyond Swift multi-line string literals; the file imports nothing at all, not even Foundation
feature_notes: enabledInstructions first line is exactly '[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance]'.

Paragraph 1 verbatim: 'Give the shortest complete answer, leading with the result. Use plain, natural language. Skip filler, hype, stock openings, repeated summaries and unsolicited closers. Preserve requested detail, facts, uncertainty, blockers and required validation.'

Paragraph 2 verbatim: 'Make focused edits using existing patterns. Add comments only for non-obvious reasons, constraints or pitfalls; omit banners, obvious narration and speculative TODOs. Preserve useful documentation. Avoid unrelated cleanup, dependencies and abstractions.'

Paragraph 3 verbatim, containing a typographic right single quote in 'product’s': 'For UI work, follow the product’s components, typography and colors. Prefer purposeful structure and real content; preserve accessibility, responsive layouts and visible loading, empty and error states.'

Paragraph 4 verbatim: 'Reuse evidence, read relevant sections and batch independent lookups. Avoid repeated scans, polling and echoed logs. Perform required checks; brevity never excuses incomplete work. Apply this guidance to delegated work too. Report changes, affected files and material limits once. User requests and project requirements take precedence.'
disabledInstructions verbatim: header '[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance: off]' then 'Disregard earlier app-provided anti-slop guidance. Continue following user requests and project requirements.'

instructions(enabled:) is a single ternary returning enabledInstructions or disabledInstructions; there is no empty or nil case, so an off toggle still injects text. The comment above disabledInstructions explains why: 'Resumed conversations may still contain the enabled guidance.'
The product name 'Droppy Code' is hard-coded inside both prompt headers, so a rename changes the prompt text the model sees.
unresolved_questions: Which call site injects these strings, and whether the off block is sent on every turn or only on resumed sessions, is not determinable from this file; the comment implies resumed conversations are the reason but the call site is elsewhere.

purpose: Hydra.swift is the Core model and prompt layer of Hydra, the one-chat-many-heads mode: it defines the persisted pair and head-profile settings (HydraPair, HydraHeadProfile), the per-launch resolution (HydraLaunch with its 8-head uncapped concurrency), the Droppy-run head budget (HydraBudget 24/120/160 tools, 25/35 min, 3 min report), the 25-name dragon roster, the persisted head record (HydraHeadInfo, HydraLanding) and the delegation-round budget (HydraDelegationBudget, maxRefusals 3). Its HydraPrompts enum builds every word the lead and the heads are told: the native and fallback lead policies with their brief, verification, project, auto-merge, review and report-style rules, Claude --agents / Copilot customAgents / Codex config overrides, the merge-state note (mergeStatus), the fenced ```hydra delegation block parser and its sent/leaving markers, the head prompts, and the report message the lead receives. At B3 the auto-merge rule, the failed/held merge-state notes and the report duration format change; everything else is byte-identical and only shifted.

purpose: HydraCookbook.swift holds the curated table of ready-made Hydra lead-and-heads pairs offered in the Settings > Hydra cookbook panel. Each HydraPairRecipe names models rather than providers: each side lists the providers that serve its model best first and the catalogue name fragments to look for, with an optional effort and head cap, so the panel can resolve a recipe against whatever providers are set up. purpose: HydraDelegationStream.swift reads a lead's ```hydra delegation block while the reply is still streaming, so each head can be dispatched as soon as its entry's closing brace arrives instead of after the whole block. It provides a whole-text incremental reader (HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations(in:) / (inBody:)) and a stateful byte-at-a-time parser class (HydraDelegationStreamParser) that consumes only newly appended text, plus the single shared entry reader delegation(fromEntry:) that both the streaming readers and the whole-block parser in Hydra.swift use, so all agree on which entries are kept and how they are titled.

streamedDelegations(inBody:): skips JSON whitespace; first byte '[' -> array mode, '{' -> single bare entry mode, anything else -> returns empty, not complete. Walks bytes tracking strings with backslash escapes; at depth 0 a '{' marks entry start; when a '}' returns depth to 0 the slice is parsed with JSONValue.parse and delegation(fromEntry:) and appended if readable (unreadable entries silently skipped); a bare entry completes the block at its closing brace; depth < 0 marks complete (broken block); ']' at depth 0 completes; a '`' at depth 0 at line start completes (closing fence). atLineStart begins true and is set after every byte to (byte == '\n').

delegation(fromEntry:): requires entry["prompt"] as a string that is non-empty after trimming, else nil. task = trimmed "task" or ""; if empty the title is TextCleanup.singleLine(prompt, limit: 60). name = trimmed "name" ?? trimmed "head" (the ?? falls back only when "name" is absent or not a string, not when it is empty); empty -> nil. project = trimmed "project" ?? trimmed "repo"; empty -> nil. profile = trimmed "profile"; empty -> nil. The prompt kept is the trimmed prompt. The fallback title is TextCleanup.singleLine(prompt, limit: 60) (Text.swift:26-31): `let remaining = text.drop(while: \.isNewline)`; the line runs to the first newline Character; it is trimmed with `.whitespaces` (not newlines); and `line.count > limit ? String(line.prefix(limit - 1)) + "…" : line`, so at most 59 grapheme clusters plus "…" (60 Characters total).

HydraDelegationStreamParser.ingest(text): ignored once complete; feeds each UTF-8 byte to readOpener until inBody, then readBody; stops at completion. Doc: reads only newly appended bytes; completed/replaced messages get a fresh parser; the runtime's sent watermark prevents already dispatched entries repeating.

readOpener state machine (bytes, ASCII-lowercased for A-Z): states 0-2 count backticks (96), any other byte resets to 0; state 3: space(32), tab(9) and further backticks are skipped, 'h'(104) -> 4, else 0; states 4-7 expect 'y'(121) 'd'(100) 'r'(114) 'a'(97), mismatch -> 1 if the byte is a backtick else 0; state 8 (after 'hydra'): '-'(45) -> 9, else readOpenerEnd; states 9-12 expect 's' 'e' 'n' 't', same mismatch rule; states 13 and 14 -> readOpenerEnd; state 15 (after CR) needs LF(10) to enter the body, else reset. readOpenerEnd: space/tab -> 14, CR(13) -> 15, LF(10) -> body, else reset (1 on backtick). So the parser accepts ```hydra and ```hydra-sent (with any case, optional spaces/tabs, CRLF), and also four or more leading backticks; it does not accept hydra-leaving.

readBody (:191-225): before the shape is known, whitespace (32, 9, 13, 10) is skipped with an early return (so atLineStart is NOT updated by it and stays true from its initial value, :141); the first other byte decides isArray = (byte == '['(91)); in array mode that '[' is consumed; otherwise that first byte falls through and is processed like any body byte. Bytes are appended to `entry` while depth > 0; '"'(34) opens strings, '\\'(92) escapes, '{'(123) at depth 0 starts a new entry buffer, '}'(125) closing to depth 0 parses the buffer with JSONValue.parse(String(decoding:as: UTF8.self)) and delegation(fromEntry:), clears the buffer, completes if not array; depth < 0 completes (:218); ']'(93) at depth 0 completes (:219); '`'(96) at depth 0 at line start completes (:220). Consequences for a non-'[' first byte: '`' completes the block at once (atLineStart still true), ']' completes it, '}' drives depth to -1 and completes it, '"' opens a string that hides later braces until it closes, '{' starts a bare entry that completes the block at its closing brace, and only other bytes are ignored until a '{'. So for an empty block "```hydra\n```" the class parser reports isComplete = true, while streamedDelegations(inBody:) (:36-45, `default: return result`) reports isComplete = false: the two streaming readers disagree on completion, not only on readability.

foldsHelpers is the inverted computed mirror of expandsHelpers: get { !expandsHelpers }, set { expandsHelpers = !newValue }.

Library.init(from:) decodes projects and threads as [Lenient<Project>] and [Lenient<ChatThread>] then compactMap(\.value), so one corrupt record does not lose the whole library.

Project.hydraPairID is the rule new chats in that project start on; nil means no rule and the app's remembered pair is used (comment names AppModel.newThread). The pair must be in Settings with its provider switched on or the rule does not apply.
ChatThread.hydraPairID is explicitly legacy: kept for decoding only, since new threads use the best fit for their provider and model.
hydraSpawnCount records how many heads this chat has sent out so far and gives the next head its place in the roster.

parentThreadID makes a thread a helper (a merge helper, for now); a helper opens in its parent's floating panel and afterwards sits under its parent in the sidebar as a smaller row for as long as the parent is there.

sortOrder is the thread's place after its project is reordered by dragging (nil keeps newest first); activityOrder plus activityOrderDay do the same inside the activity layout, and a thread active on a later day goes back to newest first.

purpose: MCPCustom.swift models MCP servers the user defines in Settings › MCP › Custom: a stdio command with arguments and environment variable names, or a streamable-HTTP URL with header names, stored lean in custom-mcp.json without any variable values. It turns a custom definition into an MCPCatalogEntry so connecting, probing, the Keychain, provider configs and the key panel treat it like a built-in server, and it holds the editor's save validation (MCPCustomError) with its user-facing messages, the variable-key rule and the remote-URL rule (https anywhere, http only for localhost).
key_symbols: struct MCPCustomServer: Codable, Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable { enum Kind: String, Codable, Sendable { case stdio, http }; struct Variable: Codable, Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable { var key: String; var isSecret = false; var id: String { key } }; var id: String; var name: String; var kind: Kind; var command = ""; var args: [String] = []; var env: [Variable] = []; var url = ""; var headers: [Variable] = []; private enum CodingKeys { id, name, kind, command, args, env, url, headers }; init(from:); init(id:name:kind:); var variables: [Variable]; static func makeID(_ name: String) -> String; var summary: String; func catalogEntry() -> MCPCatalogEntry }

enum MCPCustomError: Error, Equatable { case emptyName; case takenName(String); case emptyCommand; case badURL; case badVariableKey(String); case duplicateVariableKey(String); var message: String; static func validVariableKey(_ key: String) -> Bool; static func validate(_ server: MCPCustomServer, existingIDs: Set<String>) -> MCPCustomError?; static func validRemoteURL(_ text: String) -> Bool }

Character.isLetter / isNumber are Unicode-aware in makeID and validVariableKey (non-ASCII letters are kept/allowed).
User-facing text says "Runs on this Mac:" and the doc comment says http only "on this Mac"; secret variable values go to the macOS Keychain.
