Variable (:15-19) has synthesized Codable, so both `key` (String) and `isSecret` (Bool, despite `var isSecret = false`) are REQUIRED on decode; a hand-edited `{"key":"TOKEN"}` without isSecret makes decodeIfPresent([Variable]) throw and the whole MCPCustomServer decode fail, despite the doc comment at :37-38 ("Decoded tolerantly ... rather than dropping the whole list"). Caller (navigation): MCPStore.swift:246-248 decodes the file as one `try? JSONDecoder().decode([MCPCustomServer].self, from: data)`, so any one failing entry leaves `customs` at its previous (initial) value, i.e. the whole custom list is not loaded; MCPStore.swift:271-276 saves with JSONEncoder [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]. No values are stored here: non-secret values go into mcp.json's MCPConnection.values, secret ones into the Keychain.

Validation messages verbatim: emptyName "The server needs a name."; takenName "A server named “<name>” already exists."; emptyCommand "A stdio server needs a command."; badURL "The URL must start with https:// (or http:// for a local server)."; badVariableKey "“<key>” is not a valid variable name: letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, starting with a letter or `_`."; duplicateVariableKey "“<key>” is listed twice." (curly quotes U+201C/U+201D; backticks are literal characters in the message).

catalogEntry() presentation for customs: vendor "Custom", category .developer, asset "" (no image), colorValue 0 with isMonochrome true (wears the text colour), docsURL "", each variable becomes a field labelled with its key, empty placeholder, kind .secret or .text.
feature_notes: makeID(name): walk name.lowercased(); letters/numbers appended; any other character appends one "-" unless the previous output was a dash (lastWasDash starts true, so leading separators are dropped and runs collapse); a trailing "-" is removed; result "custom-" + slug, or "custom-server" when the slug is empty ("!!!"). Custom ids therefore never collide with catalog ids.
variables = env for .stdio, headers for .http.

catalogEntry() (:93-118): fields = variables.map { MCPField(key: $0.key, label: $0.key, placeholder: "", kind: $0.isSecret ? .secret : .text) } (:94-96), which takes MCPField's defaults (MCP.swift:29-34) help = nil, defaultValue = nil and isRequired = true, so every custom variable is a required field and needsInput is true whenever the custom server has any variable. `fields` is NOT de-duplicated: duplicate keys give duplicate fields. placeholders = Dictionary(variables.map { ($0.key, "{\($0.key)}") }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first }) (:98) keeps the first of duplicates (drafts can reach the editor header before duplicate keys are validated); transport .stdio(command: command, args: args) or .http(url: url, headers: placeholders); for stdio entry.env = placeholders. Resolution (MCP.swift) then fills {key} from the user's values and drops empty ones. The raw, untrimmed name, command, args and url are used here and in summary (:82, :85), while validate() and validRemoteURL check `server.command.trimmed` (:157) and `text.trimmed` (:173): a URL saved with surrounding whitespace passes validation but reaches `.http(url: url, ...)` untrimmed, and summary's `URL(string: url)?.host() ?? url` parses the raw string (falling back to showing the raw url when it yields no host).
validVariableKey: first character must be a letter or "_"; every character must be a letter, number, "_", "-" or "."; empty key is invalid.

validate(server, existingIDs) order: trimmed name empty -> .emptyName; makeID(trimmed name) in existingIDs -> .takenName(trimmed name); stdio with trimmed command empty -> .emptyCommand; http with !validRemoteURL(url) -> .badURL; then for each variable in order: invalid key -> .badVariableKey(key); duplicate -> .duplicateVariableKey(original key), where http header keys are compared lowercased (case-insensitive) and stdio env keys case-sensitively; nil when valid.

validRemoteURL(text): trims; URLComponents must parse with a scheme and a non-empty host; scheme lowercased must be https or http; http is allowed only when host.lowercased() is one of "localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1", "[::1]"; https allowed for any host.

B1->B2: three lines changed, `.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` replaced by the new `.trimmed` extension in validate (name at line 151, command at line 157) and validRemoteURL (line 173). Same semantics; line count unchanged at 183; no behavioral change.
unresolved_questions: validate() checks makeID(name) against existingIDs with no exclusion for the server's own id; whether the editor removes the edited server's id from existingIDs when re-saving is decided by the caller (Settings MCP editor, other bundle).
Whether URLComponents reports the host of "http://[::1]:port" as "::1" or "[::1]" (the list accepts both) must be pinned for the Windows URL parser.

Whether the editor writes back trimmed name, command and url before saving (validate() trims them for checking but does not mutate the server, and catalogEntry()/summary use the raw values) is decided by the caller (Settings MCP editor / MCPStore, other bundle).

purpose: Parses a link found in a chat into a merge request or pull request reference for three forge families, and builds the exact title and prompt for the helper thread that lands it with glab, gh or tea and then syncs the checkout.
key_symbols: MergeRequestLink.Forge (case gitlab, case github, case gitea)
state_owned: url: URL
forge: Forge
number: Int
side_effects: No direct side effects; the prompt it returns instructs an agent to run the forge CLI and 'git pull --ff-only'
platform_assumptions: Assumes the forge CLIs glab, gh and tea are installed and signed in on the machine
Assumes the helper thread runs with the project checkout as its working directory, since every instruction says 'from this directory'
ui_elements: label renders '!95' on GitLab and '#95' everywhere else: forge == .gitlab ? "!\(number)" : "#\(number)"
title renders 'Merge \(label)', described as the same words as the link popover's Merge row
feature_notes: Parsing filters out '/' components, then tries three shapes in order: an index of 'merge_requests' with index >= 1 and a positive Int immediately after it is GitLab (any GitLab host, and extra path segments such as 'diffs' after the number are tolerated); else parts.count >= 4 with parts[2] == "pull" and a positive Int at parts[3] is GitHub (github.com or a GitHub Enterprise host); else parts[2] == "pulls" with a positive Int at parts[3] is Gitea, Forgejo or Codeberg. Anything else returns nil.
All three branches require number > 0.
The Gitea case comment states one CLI, 'tea', serves Gitea and its forks, Forgejo and Codeberg among them.

GitLab land text verbatim: 'Use glab from this directory: `glab mr merge \(number) --yes`. If GitLab answers that the request is still being checked (a 405), wait a few seconds and try again; if it reports conflicts, stop and say so instead of resolving them.'
GitHub land text verbatim: 'Use gh from this directory: `gh pr merge \(number) --merge`. If GitHub reports the pull request is not mergeable, stop and say so instead of resolving it.'

Gitea land text verbatim: 'Use tea from this directory: `tea pulls merge \(number)`. If tea is not installed or signed in to this host, or the pull request is not mergeable, stop and say so instead of working around it.'

Prompt body: 'Merge \(label) now: \(url.absoluteString)', a blank line, the forge's land text, then 'Once it is merged, sync the checkout: if this directory is on main with a clean working tree, run `git pull --ff-only`; otherwise leave the working tree alone and say so. Do not rebuild, install or relaunch anything. Reply in a few lines with the merged commit and the request\u2019s link.'
Exact command lines to port: 'glab mr merge N --yes', 'gh pr merge N --merge', 'tea pulls merge N', 'git pull --ff-only'.
The prompt is deliberately self-contained because a native provider reads no AGENTS.md before it starts.
unresolved_questions: The GitLab branch checks only index >= 1 and never that the preceding component is the GitLab '/-/' separator, so a path without '-' would still parse as GitLab; whether any caller depends on that leniency is not visible here.

purpose: Defines the provider catalogue (ProviderKind, 14 cases) with every per-provider constant the app keys off: display name, CLI executable, icon asset name, login command hint, install URL, API-key host/source/env var, and capability flags (ACP transport, rewind, local /compact, image support). It also holds the small shared model enums for runtime approval mode (RuntimeMode with title, one-line summary and SF Symbol), plan/build interaction mode and local/worktree workspace mode, the ModelOption value type with its custom decoder (absent or null optional keys fall back to defaults; a wrong-typed value still throws) and name-shortening rules for the picker and composer chip, and the SlashCommand type with its suggestion ranking and its parsers for Claude command lists and Codex skill lists. At 1.6.2 it adds the separate OpenCode Go provider and the supportsCompact flag.

SlashCommand.name(in:) (lines 301-304): `guard text.first == "/" || text.first == "$" else { return nil }; return text.dropFirst().split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace).first.map(String.init)`. split omits empty subsequences by default, so whitespace right after the sigil is skipped: "/ help" returns "help" (not nil), "/help me" returns "help"; nil only when nothing but whitespace (or nothing) follows the sigil, e.g. "/" or "/   ".

SlashCommand.suggestions: lowercases the query; recent ranks map name -> smallest index in `recent`; dedupes by exact command name (first occurrence kept); filters to names whose lowercase contains the needle (all when needle empty); sorts prefix matches first, then by recent rank ascending (Int.max when not recent), ties broken by lowercased name ascending.

SlashCommand.codexInput(for:): when skillPath is set and name(in: text) == name, returns two items: [{"type":"text","text":"$" + text with its first character dropped}, {"type":"skill","name":name,"path":skillPath}]; otherwise [{"type":"text","text":text}]. So a "/skill" typed with a slash is sent to Codex with a "$" sigil; and because name(in:) skips leading whitespace, "/ skill" also matches skill "skill" and is sent as "$ skill" (space kept).

SlashCommand.claudeCommands: each entry's name is entry["name"] as string, else the entry itself if it is a string; detail is entry["description"] or the default "Claude Code command"; entries without a name are dropped.

SlashCommand.codexSkills: iterates result["data"] array, each entry's "skills" array; skips skills whose "enabled" is explicitly false or that lack "name" or "path"; detail is skill["interface"]["shortDescription"], else skill["description"], else ""; skillPath = path.

purpose: Implements the "forward this chat into a new thread" snapshot: a Codable ThreadContinuation that stores the source thread id and title, a creation date, a rendered text context of the earlier conversation, the referenced attachments and a truncation flag. The static capture function turns a ThreadDocument's user and assistant items into a size-bounded transcript (48,000 characters, always keeping up to 4,000 characters of the first real user request and then the newest messages backwards), folding in any previous continuation the source itself inherited; the prompt property wraps that context in fixed instructions and BEGIN/END markers for the next assistant.

ThreadContinuation.init(sourceThreadID: UUID, sourceTitle: String, createdAt: Date = .now, context: String, attachments: [Attachment] = [], isTruncated: Bool = false)
private static let truncationMarker = "… [parts of the forwarded conversation were omitted here to keep the context within its size limit] …"
static func capture(sourceID: UUID, title: String, document: ThreadDocument) -> ThreadContinuation

private struct ContinuationUnit { enum Role: String { case user = "User"; case assistant = "Assistant"; var label: String { "\(rawValue):" } }; var role: Role; var text: String; var attachments: [Attachment]; func rendered(limit: Int? = nil) -> (text: String, wasLimited: Bool) }

state_owned: Instance fields of ThreadContinuation only; no statics other than the three constants.
side_effects: None. capture and prompt are pure; createdAt defaults to Date.now at construction.
platform_assumptions: Foundation UUID, Date and Codable (synthesised). Thread files are written with JSONEncoder.storage (Services/Store/Storage.swift:382; Core/Support/Coding.swift:20-25: dateEncodingStrategy = .iso8601, outputFormatting [.sortedKeys]) and read with a JSONDecoder whose dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601 (Storage.swift:76-77). Foundation's .iso8601 strategy writes whole seconds with no fractional part (e.g. "2026-09-22T10:15:30Z"), so createdAt (Date.now) loses sub-second precision on round trip; a JS port using toISOString() writes milliseconds, a different stored format that the .iso8601 decoder does not accept.

All length arithmetic uses Swift String.count, i.e. extended grapheme clusters (doc comment: counted in Swift characters rather than bytes, so a chat full of emoji is not cut short). A JS port must count graphemes (Intl.Segmenter), not UTF-16 code units, to reproduce the same cuts.
prefix/suffix on String are grapheme-based as well.
persisted_fields: Stored inside ThreadDocument under key "continuation" (optional). Keys: "sourceThreadID" (UUID string), "sourceTitle" (String), "createdAt" (Date), "context" (String), "attachments" ([Attachment] with id/name/path/mimeType), "isTruncated" (Bool). Synthesised Codable: all keys required when decoding a ThreadContinuation (no custom lenient decoder), but ThreadDocument decodes it through container.value(.continuation, default: nil), so a malformed one becomes nil.
ui_elements: No UI. Model-facing prompt text only (listed verbatim in feature_notes).
feature_notes: Unit selection: iterate document.items in order. .user: skip if isFromHydra or isHydraBrief; text = message.text.trimmed; skip if text empty and no attachments; append role User with the message attachments. .assistant: text = HydraPrompts.withoutDelegationBlock(message.text), which trims: Hydra.swift:1165-1169 is `var kept = text; if let range = delegationBlockRange(in: text) { kept.removeSubrange(range) }; return kept.trimmed` (trimmed = trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)). So assistant units have the delegation block removed and are trimmed of whitespace and newlines, and a whitespace-only assistant message is skipped by `guard !text.isEmpty`; append role Assistant with no attachments. All other content kinds (reasoning, tool, plan, todos, notice, turnEnd) are ignored.

Re-forward guard: if no units and the document already has a continuation, return a new ThreadContinuation with the new sourceID/title (createdAt = now) but the previous context, attachments and isTruncated unchanged, so forwarding again before sending does not re-wrap or shorten.

Budget: remaining = 48_000 - truncationMarker.count - 2 (line 68). truncationMarker is 101 characters (101 grapheme clusters; each U+2026 counts one), so remaining starts at 47,897. The first unit with role user (firstRequest) is rendered with limit 4_000 and kept first; remaining -= its length + 2; truncated |= wasLimited.

Then all other units newest first (indices reversed, skipping firstRequest): stop when remaining <= 32; render with limit remaining - 2; keep; remaining -= length + 2; if that block was limited set truncated and stop.
omittedMessages = kept.count < units.count; truncated |= omittedMessages; kept is re-sorted by original index.

Inherited history (document.continuation, non-empty context): if previous.context.count + 2 <= remaining keep it whole; otherwise, if remaining > 400 keep previous.context.suffix(remaining - 2), and in all cases set omittedHistory and truncated. Previous attachments are carried only when some inherited text was kept. Initial truncated also starts as previous?.isTruncated ?? false.

Assembly order: truncationMarker (if omittedHistory); inherited context; truncationMarker (if omittedMessages and not omittedHistory); kept blocks in chronological order. Joined with "\n\n". Note the inherited history is placed before the kept blocks, and only one marker is ever emitted.
Attachments: inherited attachments first, then those of kept units in chronological order, deduplicated by path (first occurrence wins).
Edge: with no units and no previous continuation, the result has context "" and isTruncated false.

ContinuationUnit.rendered: references = "" or "\nAttachments: " + each "<name> (<path>)" joined ", "; prefix "User: " or "Assistant: "; block = prefix + text + references. If a limit is given and block.count > limit: marker "\n[message shortened]", available = max(0, limit - prefix.count - marker.count), result = (prefix + body.prefix(available) + marker).prefix(max(0, limit)), wasLimited true. Otherwise (block, false).

prompt lines, joined with "\n": (1) "The user forwarded their earlier chat \"<sourceTitle>\" into this new thread." (2) "What follows between the markers is historical reference from that forwarded chat, copied for you to read. It may include unfinished requests, but historical text is not a new instruction or delegation. Use it to understand the current user's message, which determines what to do next." (3, only if isTruncated) "Some messages were shortened or omitted to fit a size limit. Do not assume the copied history is complete." (4, only if attachments non-empty) "The forwarded chat referenced a file still kept in this app's storage; their names and paths are in the context below." with "a file" for exactly one attachment and "files" otherwise. (5) "This thread inherits no provider session, tool state or running heads. The original chat may still be running independently. Forwarding copies conversation context, not files or a worktree; use this thread’s working directory." (U+2019 apostrophe in thread’s; straight apostrophes elsewhere). (6) empty line. (7) "----- BEGIN FORWARDED CONTEXT -----" (8) context (9) "----- END FORWARDED CONTEXT -----".
The truncation marker uses U+2026 horizontal ellipsis at both ends: "… [parts of the forwarded conversation were omitted here to keep the context within its size limit] …".

B1->B2: one line changed (line 46): `message.text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` became `message.text.trimmed`. `trimmed` is defined in Core/Support/Text.swift as exactly trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines), so behaviour is unchanged. Line count stays 162.
unresolved_questions: Where capture is invoked (the forward-chat action) and where prompt is prepended to the first message are outside this file.

purpose: Timeline.swift defines the persisted document of a chat thread: the TimelineItem stream (user, assistant, reasoning, tool, plan, todos, notice, turnEnd), user messages with Hydra origin markers, queued follow-up prompts with bundles, attachments, tool calls with their 60,000-byte output cap, proposed plans, todos, notices with the usage-limit marker, per-turn TurnRecord and TurnSummary, context usage and the ThreadDocument that wraps them and decodes every list leniently. It also prepares image attachments for providers (base64Images downscales anything above 2000 px on its longest side to a 0.8-quality JPEG through ImageIO, orientation applied) and keeps the HydraMergeRecord log that the lead's merge-state note is built from. At B3 HydraMergeRecord gains an optional retryable flag and its held outcome is documented as legacy-only.

purpose: One observation of newly consumed tokens as a provider reported it, with the accumulation rule for merging observations and a field-by-field decoder so a record written by a build that knew fewer fields still reads as the observation it was.
state_owned: provider ProviderKind
totalTokens Int
inputTokens Int? = nil
outputTokens Int? = nil
cachedInputTokens Int? = nil
model String? = nil
agentID String? = nil
platform_assumptions: None; a pure Foundation value type
persisted_fields: Codable keys: provider, totalTokens, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens, model, agentID
Decode behaviour: provider is required (decode, not value); totalTokens defaults to 0; inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens, model and agentID all default to nil
Stored inside TurnRecord.tokenSpends in a ThreadDocument
feature_notes: Semantics fixed by the doc comment: the amount is what this event is responsible for, the usage one request or one turn just consumed, never the occupancy of a context window, which ContextUsage carries separately.
cachedInputTokens is a subset of totalTokens (input the provider served from its cache), so it is never added on top of input tokens; only totalTokens is authoritative.

agentID names the head a provider ran inside the session when the usage belongs to that head. A head's spend is the account's spend and belongs to the head alone: a consumer must not attribute an event carrying an agentID to the session's lead as well.

merge(_:) always adds totalTokens, but the three optional breakdowns go through sum(), which returns nil unless both sides are non-nil, so merging a detailed spend with one that lacks a breakdown erases that breakdown rather than reporting a partial total.
merge(_:) does not touch provider, model or agentID, so the receiver's identity always wins.
The explicit memberwise init exists because the hand-written init(from:) would otherwise suppress the synthesized one.
unresolved_questions: Whether inputTokens plus outputTokens is expected to equal totalTokens for providers that report all three is not stated; only the cachedInputTokens subset rule is spelled out.

purpose: Codable leniency and the two shared JSON coders for on-disk storage: a KeyedDecodingContainer helper that supplies a default for keys older saves lack, a Lenient<Element> wrapper that swallows a bad element instead of failing its collection, and JSONEncoder.storage / JSONDecoder.storage configured with ISO8601 dates and sorted keys.

JSONEncoder.storage: process-wide shared encoder instance
JSONDecoder.storage: process-wide shared decoder instance
platform_assumptions: Foundation Codable, JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder with .iso8601 date strategies
@autoclosure default so the fallback is only built on a miss
persisted_fields: Date encoding strategy for all storage JSON: .iso8601 (encode and decode)

feature_notes: value(_:default:) double-unwraps: ((try? decodeIfPresent(T.self, forKey: key)) ?? nil) ?? fallback() so both a throw and an explicit null fall back to the default, which makes missing keys in older saves non-fatal
Lenient never throws from init(from:); it sets value = try? Element(from: decoder), so a corrupt element inside an array becomes a Lenient with value == nil rather than aborting the whole decode
Storage JSON writes keys in sorted order, which keeps file diffs stable across saves

purpose: Self-monitoring for main-thread freezes: a dedicated background thread posts a block to the main queue every 0.5 s and, when the main thread has not answered for 4 s, runs /usr/bin/sample against the app's own pid and writes the captured stacks to ~/Library/Logs/Droppy Code/hang-<stamp>.txt. feature_notes: start(): under the lock, returns early if started is already true; otherwise sets started = true and lastPong = Date(), then starts the thread. Thread body: while true { Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.5); ping(); check() }.

ping(): DispatchQueue.main.async { lastPong = Date(); reportedThisStall = false }. While the main thread is stuck these blocks queue up; they all run once it recovers, which clears reportedThisStall so the next stall gets its own report (doc comment: "One report per stall; the next stall gets one of its own.").

check(): stalled = Date().timeIntervalSince(lastPong); returns nil unless stalled >= 4 (stallThreshold) and reportedThisStall is false; when it fires it sets reportedThisStall = true, so at most one report per stall. The seconds printed in the log (line 79) and the header (line 91) are this `stalled` value at the moment of detection, not the total length of the freeze: check() runs once per loop after `Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.5)` (line 52) and fires on the first tick with stalled >= 4, so with the watchdog thread on schedule the figure is about 4.0 to 4.5 (plus loop overhead) however long the freeze lasts. A port must print the detection-time value, not a measured total.

feature_notes: request(): if isClosed throws RPCError(code: -32000, message: "The agent process is not running."). Otherwise id = .int(nextID), nextID += 1, checks cancellation, stores the continuation in pending and writes {"id", "method", "params"}. On task cancellation, a main-actor Task removes the pending entry and resumes it with CancellationError (no cancel message is sent to the agent).
write(): no-op when closed; drops "params" when it equals .null; adds "jsonrpc": "2.0" only when sendsVersion is true; sends .object(message).
notify() writes {"method", "params"}; respond(result) writes {"id", "result"}; respond(errorCode) writes {"id", "error": {"code", "message"}}.

handle(): non-object messages ignored. A message with a string "method" is a request if it has a parseable "id" (goes to onRequest; if onRequest is nil, responds with code -32601 and message "Method not found"), otherwise a notification to onNotification. Missing params become .null.

handle() responses: requires a parseable id with a pending entry, else ignored. If "error" exists and is not null, resumes throwing RPCError(code: error.code ?? -32603, message: error.message ?? "The agent returned an error.", data: error.data); else resumes with "result" ?? .null.

RPCID from a JSON double is `case .double(let id): self = .int(Int(id))` (line 10): Int(_:) truncates toward zero, so 3.0 and 3.7 both become .int(3), and Swift's Int(_: Double) traps (the process crashes) for NaN, infinity or a double outside Int's range (JSON text can carry an out-of-range number such as 1e300). This differs from JSONValue.int (JSONValue.swift line 86), which returns nil for a non-finite double. RPCID has separate `.int` and `.string` cases, so a string id "3" never matches a pending `.int(3)` and such a response is ignored.
start(): readTask iterates process.messages holding self weakly per message; when the stream ends calls didClose().

didClose(): once only; sets isClosed, tail = process.errorTail.trimmed, fails every pending continuation with RPCError(code: -32000, message: tail empty ? "The agent process exited." : tail), then onClose?(tail).

B1->B2: one line changed in didClose (line 144): process.errorTail.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) became process.errorTail.trimmed (the new String.trimmed in Text.swift, which is the same whitespacesAndNewlines trim). No behavioural change.

close() is only `func close() { process.terminate() }` (lines 101-103): it does not set isClosed and does not fail `pending`. Pending requests fail only when process.messages ends and didClose() runs, which is at stdout EOF or 1 s after exit (StdioProcess.didExit asyncAfter 1 s -> finishOutput); if SIGTERM is ignored, exit itself waits for StdioProcess.terminate's SIGKILL at 3 s. In that window request() still passes the `if isClosed` guard, write() still sends, and StdioProcess.send enqueues `try? handle.write(contentsOf: payload)` on writeQueue after terminate()'s `writeQueue.async { try? handle.close() }`, so the write fails silently and the request waits until didClose().

purpose: New in B3: a @MainActor generic registry, PendingReplies<Value: Sendable>, that parks one CheckedContinuation<Value, Error> per string request id so a stdio provider can await the reply line carrying that id. purpose: A generic two-generation (current/previous) cost-bounded cache struct used for thumbnails and other recent-item memories: hits in the previous generation are promoted into the current one, and when the current generation exceeds its count limit or cost budget it is demoted wholesale to previous and a fresh current is started.

platform_assumptions: Pure Swift value type; no Apple framework dependency beyond importing Foundation
feature_notes: Generational eviction rather than LRU: when current.count >= limit or currentCost > costLimit - cost, the whole current map becomes previous (dropping the old previous) and current is emptied and re-reserved to limit
A read that hits `previous` removes it from previous, subtracts its cost from previousCost, and re-inserts it into current, so recently used items survive the next rotation
An entry whose cost exceeds costLimit is rejected outright (guard cost <= costLimit else { return }), after the existing entry for that key has already been removed
insert() always calls removeValue(for:) first, so re-inserting a key never double-counts cost
init clamps: limit = max(1, limit), costLimit = max(0, costLimit); insert clamps cost = max(0, cost)
contains() checks both generations; value(for:) has the promotion side effect and is therefore mutating
Effective capacity is up to 2x limit in terms of what can still be found, since previous entries remain readable

purpose: The incremental byte framer for child-process stdio, supporting two wire framings: newline-delimited messages and LSP-style Content-Length headers separated by CRLFCRLF, with a scan cursor so re-scanning is bounded and a finish() that flushes a trailing unterminated line.

platform_assumptions: Foundation Data slicing semantics; no macOS-specific API
feature_notes: Line framing splits on the single byte 0x0A (LF); the delimiter itself is not included in the returned message
Content-Length framing: the header block ends at the exact bytes \r\n\r\n; the header is UTF-8 decoded and scanned for a line whose name, trimmed of whitespace and lowercased, equals "content-length"
A header without a usable Content-Length (unparseable or negative) is skipped: contentLength returns nil and the loop continues past that header without emitting a message
The partial-header rewind is `search = max(start, buffer.endIndex - 3)`, so a separator split across reads is still found (3 bytes of the 4-byte separator may remain unscanned)
finish() returns the leftover buffer only in .lines framing and only when non-empty; in .contentLength framing a truncated body is dropped. It always resets buffer, scanned and bodyLength
After each append pass the buffer is re-based to `start` only when start moved, and `scanned` records the unsearched distance so bytes are not re-scanned from the beginning each read

Spans are computed in milliseconds as (now - max(busySince, switchStart)) * 1000 and reported as Int
Measurement window is 1 second: once now - switchStart >= 1 it logs "switch to <label>: blocked <n> ms, busy <m> ms in 1 s" and clears switchStart
A second selection inside the window logs "switch to <label>: blocked <n> ms, busy <m> ms before the next switch" before restarting the measurement
The signpost name is "switch" and the title is passed as a %{public}s argument
The label is truncated to the first 24 characters of the title
All log interpolations are marked privacy: .public

feature_notes: Lines 1-82 (AppInfo, TextCleanup, the SimpleDiff doc comment and diffLimit) are byte-identical to B2; only SimpleDiff.unified changed and DiffOp was added. B2 lines 83-111 became B3 83-165, B2 112 -> B3 166, B2 113-133 -> B3 205-225 (+92): FileEdit extension B2 114-125 -> B3 206-217, nilIfEmpty B2 128 -> B3 220, trimmed B2 130-132 -> B3 222-224. git diff: one hunk @@ -80,34 +80,126 @@.

Size guard moved first (B3 :91-103): when old.utf8.count + new.utf8.count > 200_000 the function now runs only the common head/tail scan and returns Stats(diff: nil, additions: newLines.count - prefix - suffix, deletions: oldLines.count - prefix - suffix). The values equal B2's added.count/removed.count, so over-cap results are unchanged, but the four slice constructions that ran before the guard at B2 (upstream defect 47, PR-STORE-111) are gone; only the line split still precedes the guard, because the counts need it.

Under the cap the counts are now exact: removed/inserted offset sets from newLines.difference(from: oldLines) (:105-112), additions = inserted.count, deletions = removed.count (:164). At B2 every line between the first and last change was counted as both removed and added, so two small edits far apart reported inflated counts; B3 reports only the lines that actually changed. Over-cap edits still use the head/tail approximation, so the two paths count differently.

No-change result is new: when the difference is empty (texts equal line by line under Swift String ==, including two empty texts) unified returns Stats(diff: nil, additions: 0, deletions: 0) (:113-115). B2 returned a context-only hunk (e.g. "@@ -1,0 +1,0 @@" for two empty texts, "@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n same" for "same"/"same"). Downstream at B3: TimelineRows.swift:2128 and DiffInspector.swift:165 show nothing for a nil diff, and ThreadRuntime.swift:3447 (settleCommand, PR-RUNTIME-192) replaces a row's edits with the git-snapshot edits only when every edit's diff is nil, so a provider edit whose old and new sides are equal (e.g. a Claude Edit with neither string, PR-PROVCLI-359) no longer blocks that replacement.

Hunk assembly (:117-164): both texts are walked together emitting DiffOp lines numbered from 1; at each step a removed old line wins, then an inserted new line, otherwise a context line whose text is taken from the OLD side (:130). Changes whose op indices are at most 2*contextLines+1 = 7 apart (6 or fewer unchanged lines between) share one hunk; otherwise a new hunk starts (:154-162). Each hunk spans 3 context ops before its first and after its last change, clamped to the stream (:143-145), and hunks are joined with "\n" with no file header lines.

Header format (:146-150): "@@ -<oldStart>,<oldCount> +<newStart>,<newCount> @@" where oldStart/newStart are the first old/new line numbers present in the hunk slice, or 0 if the slice holds no line of that side, and oldCount/newCount count ops carrying that side's number. B2 printed one start number (prefix - leading + 1) on both sides; B3's new-side start is independent and is 0 for an empty side ("" -> "a" is now "@@ -0,0 +1,1 @@\n+a", "a" -> "" is "@@ -1,1 +0,0 @@\n-a"). The ",count" is still always printed, including 1.

Doc comment changed from "A compact unified hunk between two texts, trimming the unchanged head and tail." to "A compact unified diff between two texts, one hunk per run of changes with context." (:86), plus the contextLines comment "Unchanged lines kept on each side of a change; hunks closer than twice that merge." (:83) and the over-cap comment "Too large for an exact diff, so count by the unchanged head and tail instead." (:92).

Hand trace against the existing C# fixtures (ENGINEERING inference, not run): single-change cases (one-hunk a..h fixture, "a\n"->"b\n", the CRLF fixture, canonical-equivalence context and trailing old-spelling fixtures, FileEditTextTests keep/old/new/more) produce the same text at B3; the ("",""), ("","a"), ("a","") and ("same","same") rows change as described above.
unresolved_questions: The hunk text now depends on which lines Swift's CollectionDifference matches when several minimal edit scripts exist (e.g. old ["a","a"] vs new ["a"]: removing offset 0 gives "-a\n a", removing offset 1 gives " a\n-a"). That algorithm lives in the Swift standard library of the toolchain that built 1.7.0, not in the pinned tree. Before implementing, the orchestrator needs pinned evidence of it (the stdlib Diffing.swift at the toolchain's tag, or fixtures produced by the macOS reference build), and the C# port must reproduce it rather than use a generic diff library whose tie-breaking differs.

Cost at B3 (not yet measured): if the stdlib difference is a plain Myers descent that stores its V-array trace, a whole-file Write (old "") of N lines under the 200000-byte cap does O(N^2) work and memory. Whether that is observable (UI stall) on the reference build is unmeasured; an output-identical fast path for an empty side would be an ENGINEERING DECISION needing a recorded equivalence proof, not a source fact.

purpose: Image attachment thumbnailing: a shared actor that downsamples files with ImageIO off the main actor, coalesces concurrent requests for the same key into one detached decode, and caches results by cost; plus ThumbnailMemory, a main-actor RecentCache of already-decoded CGImages so a row scrolling back into view draws its photos in the same pass.

state_owned: thumbnails: RecentCache<String, Thumbnail> with limit 120 and costLimit 32 * 1_024 * 1_024 (32 MB)
inFlight: [String: Task<Thumbnail?, Never>] (decodes under way, for later callers to join)
decodes: Int (count of started decodes, exposed for tests of the sharing)
ThumbnailMemory.images: RecentCache<String, CGImage> with limit 120 and costLimit 16 * 1_024 * 1_024 (16 MB)
side_effects: Reads image files from disk via CGImageSourceCreateWithURL on a detached task
Spawns detached decode tasks at .userInitiated priority
platform_assumptions: ImageIO and CoreGraphics (CGImageSource thumbnail creation), macOS/Apple platforms only
kCGImageProperty / kCGImageSource CFString option keys
Swift actors and @MainActor isolation; Thumbnail is @unchecked Sendable because CGImage is not Sendable
ui_elements: Cache key format "<path>#<pixels>#<fillingSquare>" where pixels = max(1, Int((pointSize * 2).rounded(.up))), i.e. a fixed 2x point-to-pixel scale
ThumbnailMemory key format "<path>#<Int((pointSize * 2).rounded(.up))>" (no fillingSquare component)
feature_notes: A 2x scale factor is assumed for every request: pixels = max(1, Int((pointSize * 2).rounded(.up)))
fillingSquare mode enlarges the requested max pixel size by the aspect ratio max(w,h)/min(w,h), clamped to 2048 pixels, so a square crop is still filled at full resolution

Decode options: kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways true, kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform true (EXIF orientation applied), kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately true, kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize = pixels
Request coalescing: concurrent callers for the same key await the same Task; a caller giving up waits the decode out rather than cancelling it for the others (comment is explicit about this)
The in-flight entry is only cleared and the result only cached when inFlight[key] is still that same task, so a superseded decode does not evict a newer one
Cancellation: an early return of nil if Task.isCancelled on entry, and the result is discarded (returns nil) if the caller was cancelled by the time the decode finished
Cache cost is image.bytesPerRow * image.height in both caches, so the byte budgets are real decoded-bitmap bytes
The stated motivation is 15 thumbnails for the downloads popover decoding side by side instead of serially
unresolved_questions: Who writes into ThumbnailMemory (the view that stores a decoded CGImage after drawing it) is outside this bundle.

grep -n "droppy-logo" across porting/spec/*.json finds three records that describe the image by its SwiftUI asset name rather than its file path: PR-SETTINGS-248 and PR-UPDATE-086 (both citing SettingsView.swift:1083-112[4/5] MadeByDroppyRow, 'a Link holding the \"droppy-logo\" image at 40 x 40') and UI-UPDATE-026 (colors field: 'the logo asset is \"droppy-logo\" at interpolation .high'). None of the three literally cite this file's path, and their cited line ranges are entirely inside SettingsView.swift, which is not part of this bundle and was not touched by this recolor, so their cited lines are untouched and unshifted -> recite_lines_only / no entry needed; none of the three hardcodes a specific color value that the recolor would falsify.

Concrete, verified port_impact: unit App.Views.Settings.SettingsView (porting/deps/units.json) maps DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift -> src/Marrow.App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.cs and lists PR-SETTINGS-248/PR-UPDATE-086/UI-UPDATE-026 in its records_todo; that target file already exists (11339 bytes) but is still status TODO. The actual image bytes the port ships, src/Marrow.UI/Assets/Images/droppy-logo.png, are sha256 0f5d9663a0d23c458ab8e2783237596e5618d482f4ac23f00ead91eccef04388 and 51677 bytes -- byte-for-byte the B2 (1.6.2) source image, confirmed against E:\Droppy\reference\droppy-code-v1.6.2\...\droppy-logo.png. It has not been updated to the B3 pixels (this file, 42660 bytes, sha256 307aca6...). The port's copy must be replaced with this B3 file's bytes to keep the Made-by-Droppy credit-row logo at parity with the pinned B3 source.

purpose: Defines the app's in-memory unified-diff model (DiffFile / DiffHunk / DiffLine) and a hand-written parser that turns raw `git diff` text, or a provider's bare per-file hunks, into numbered, kind-tagged lines for the diff UI.
key_symbols: DiffFile fields: path, oldPath: String?, change, isBinary, hunks: [DiffHunk], reportedAdditions: Int?, reportedDeletions: Int?
DiffFile.id == path; DiffFile.additions / .deletions (reported value wins, else counted from hunks); DiffFile.name == lastPathComponent; DiffFile.directory (parent + "/", empty string when at root)
struct DiffHunk: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { id: Int, header: String, lines: [DiffLine] }
struct DiffLine: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { id: Int, kind, text, oldNumber: Int?, newNumber: Int? }
DiffParser.parseHunks(_ text: String, path: String) -> DiffFile
state_owned: Parser-local mutable state inside parse(): files, current: DiffFile?, hunk: DiffHunk?, oldLine, newLine, lineID counters. No stored global state; the enum is a namespace with only static methods.
side_effects: None. Pure text parsing, no I/O, no process launches.
platform_assumptions: Foundation only; uses NSString path bridging (lastPathComponent / deletingLastPathComponent) and therefore Unix '/' path separators for the name and directory helpers.
ui_elements: No views; supplies the model the diff views render. DiffFile.directory renders as a trailing-slash parent path, empty string at repository root.
feature_notes: Line-prefix dispatch inside parse(): 'diff --git ' starts a new file (closes the previous file and hunk); 'new file mode' -> .added; 'deleted file mode' -> .deleted; 'rename from ' -> .renamed plus oldPath = remainder; 'rename to ' -> path = remainder; 'Binary files' or 'GIT binary patch' -> isBinary = true; '--- /dev/null' -> .added; '+++ /dev/null' -> .deleted, any other '+++ ' -> path = stripPrefix(dropFirst(4)); '@@' starts a hunk.

Header-block lines are only interpreted while hunk == nil or the line itself begins with '@@' (guard `if hunk == nil || line.hasPrefix("@@")`), so text inside a hunk is never mistaken for a file header.

Body-line classification: '+' -> .addition with newNumber = newLine then newLine += 1; '-' -> .deletion with oldNumber = oldLine then oldLine += 1; '\\' (the '\ No newline at end of file' marker) -> .note with text = String(line.dropFirst(2)), dropping backslash AND space; ' ' or empty -> .context with both oldNumber and newNumber, both counters advance.
A trailing empty line that is the very end of the patch is skipped: `if line.isEmpty, rawLine.endIndex == patch.endIndex { continue }` so a final newline does not become a spurious context line.
lineID is a single monotonically increasing counter shared by hunks and lines (incremented once per hunk header and once per body line), giving stable Identifiable ids within one parse.

parseHunks(_:path:) synthesizes a header when the text lacks one: "diff --git a/\(path) b/\(path)\n" + text, parses it, falls back to DiffFile(path: path, change: .modified, isBinary: false, hunks: []) when parse returns nothing, then force-overwrites file.path = path.

headerPath() prefers the text after the LAST ' b/' occurrence in the 'diff --git ' line (range(of:options:.backwards)), so paths containing ' b/' still resolve; otherwise falls back to stripPrefix of the whole remainder.
stripPrefix() removes surrounding double quotes when both are present and count >= 2, then removes a leading 'a/' or 'b/' (exactly 2 characters).

hunkStarts() splits the '@@ -a,b +c,d @@' header on spaces, takes the first token beginning with '-' and the first beginning with '+', drops that sign character, splits on ',' and parses the first field; a missing token or unparsable digits default to 1.
Any line before the first 'diff --git ' header is discarded (`guard current != nil else { continue }`).
unresolved_questions: hunkStarts() picks the first space-separated token starting with '-' or '+'; for a '@@' header whose trailing section-heading text starts with '-' or '+' the real ranges still come first, so it is benign in practice, but nothing in this file guards it explicitly.

purpose: A single convenience initializer that rolls an array of parsed DiffFile values up into a FileChangeSummary: per-file entries plus the repository-wide addition and deletion totals shown on a turn's change badge.
state_owned: Local accumulators only: entries: [File] with reserveCapacity(files.count), additions, deletions.
side_effects: None; pure value transformation.
platform_assumptions: Foundation import only; no macOS-specific API in this file.
ui_elements: No views; the resulting FileChangeSummary is the +/- counts model.
feature_notes: Each DiffFile becomes exactly one FileChangeSummary.File(path: file.path, additions: file.additions, deletions: file.deletions, isBinary: file.isBinary); file order is preserved, nothing is filtered, and binary files contribute whatever counts DiffFile reports (0 unless reportedAdditions/reportedDeletions were set).
Totals are the plain sum of every file's additions and deletions: no cap, no de-duplication by path, no special handling for renames.
entries.reserveCapacity(files.count) is the only performance concession; the loop reads file.additions and file.deletions once each into locals before appending.
unresolved_questions: The memberwise shape of FileChangeSummary and its nested File type is declared in another file outside this bundle, so I cannot confirm whether File carries further fields with defaults.

purpose: Git.swift is the app's only wrapper around the git command line and the three forge CLIs (glab, gh, tea): every git process is spawned through Git.run with the argv prefix ["-c", "core.quotepath=false", "-c", "color.ui=false"], GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 over LoginEnvironment.current, a 120 s default budget and 300 s at named sites. It owns repository queries (status --porcelain=v2 parsing into GitStatus, branches into GitBranch, remote and forge detection), commit/publish (commitAll, push, pushBranch, createPullRequest, mergePullRequest with GitLab 405 retries), the Hydra landing primitives (captureTree over private GIT_INDEX_FILE indexes, commitWork, compare-and-swap updateRef, dirty/ignored/present path queries, hasOperationInProgress marker checks), checkpoint refs under refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/<thread>/<turn>-<phase> with WorkingTreeWatch-assisted tree capture, revert preview/restore, chunked diff, detached worktrees and three-way patch apply. At B3 (1.7.0) it gains a rebase-onto-remote capture (captureTree(paths:onto:from:)) that builds the team's paths on top of origin's current commit with per-file git merge-file, a force option on pushBranch for Hydra-owned branches, and a recovery path that turns a forge's 'already exists' failure into the URL of the existing request.

NEW createPullRequest fallback (:193-195): after the forge switch and before Self.check(result), `if !result.succeeded, let existing = Self.existingRequestURL(in: result, web: await remoteWebURL()) { return existing }`. A failed create whose output says the request already exists now returns that request's URL instead of throwing; the doc comment says a retried merge then carries on with that request rather than failing on it. remoteWebURL() is awaited on every failure (one extra git remote get-url origin) because it is an argument of the call.

NEW static existingRequestURL(in:web:) (:202-218), also called from AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:462: text = output + "\n" + errorOutput; nil unless text.lowercased() contains "already exist"; then the first #/https://\S+/# match that parses as a URL is returned (GitHub and Gitea print the address); otherwise the first #/!(\d+)/# match plus a non-nil web URL: when web.user is non-nil, URLComponents drops user and password (keeping the original when .url is nil), and the result is web.appending(path: "-/merge_requests/<digits>") (GitLab names it as !<number>). An unparseable https match falls through to the !<number> branch rather than returning nil.

purpose: The model behind the 'undo this thread's changes' preview: the files a revert would put back, each with its add/delete counts, a binary flag and a kept flag for files the checkout has changed again since the thread last touched them, plus a parser for `git diff --numstat -z` output.

var additions: Int and var deletions: Int (sums over restorable only)
state_owned: var files: [File] is the only stored property; File.isKept is the only mutable per-file field and defaults to false, every other File field is a let.
side_effects: None; pure parsing and aggregation. The numstat text is produced by Git.previewRestore, not by this file.
platform_assumptions: Foundation's CocoaError for the parse failure; no AppKit or macOS UI dependency.
ui_elements: No views; supplies the preview list (path, additions, deletions, binary marker, kept marker) and the aggregate counts the revert sheet shows. Only non-kept files contribute to the totals.
feature_notes: init(numstat:) splits the whole text on NUL ('\0'), then splits each entry on tab with maxSplits: 2 and omittingEmptySubsequences: false, requiring exactly 3 fields with a non-empty third field, otherwise throwing CocoaError(.fileReadCorruptFile).

A binary file is recognised only when BOTH count fields are exactly "-"; its additions and deletions are then recorded as 0 and isBinary is true. A single "-" in one field alone fails Int parsing and throws.
Non-binary counts must parse as Int and be >= 0, otherwise the initializer throws CocoaError(.fileReadCorruptFile).

Documented semantics: 'A file the checkout has changed again since the thread last left it is somebody else's work now: it is listed, marked kept, and left alone.' Kept files stay visible in `files` but are excluded from `restorable`, `additions` and `deletions`.
Field order assumed from git numstat: added, removed, path.
The memberwise init(files:) is written out explicitly rather than synthesized, so RevertPreview(files: []) is the empty-preview value Git.previewRestore returns for an empty path list.
unresolved_questions: Whether the numstat text ever arrives in the `-z` rename form (two extra NUL-separated path records); Git.previewRestore passes `--no-renames` so the three-field assumption holds inside this bundle, but a caller outside it using renames would fail the parse.

purpose: TouchedPaths.swift is a caseless `enum TouchedPaths` namespace of pure, nonisolated static helpers that reconcile file paths an agent reported editing with repository-relative paths in a diff. It normalizes absolute or relative reports against the checkout root, rejects paths outside the checkout (other folders, `..` climbs, URLs) so they are never staged, classifies build-output and tool-cache paths that must never be landed or merged, and matches a DiffFile against a set of touched paths allowing for subfolder-relative reports.

side_effects: None: pure string and path computation; the file makes no explicit file system calls.
platform_assumptions: POSIX paths: `/` separator in prefix checks (`base.path + "/"`, `root + "/"`), `path.hasPrefix("/")` as the absolute test, `split(separator: "/")` in isBuildOutput, and `hasSuffix("/" + path)` in matches. A Windows port needs drive-letter/UNC absolute detection and backslash and forward-slash handling. Case: upstream compares CASE-SENSITIVELY everywhere (`path.hasPrefix(prefix)` l.11, `full.hasPrefix(prefix)` l.27, `buildOutputNames.contains(name)` l.44, `touched.contains(path)` and `hasSuffix("/" + path)` / `hasSuffix("/" + $0)` l.57), even though a default macOS APFS volume is case-insensitive. Case-sensitive comparison is therefore B2 behaviour; case-folding for NTFS would be a deliberate divergence from B2 to be recorded as such, not something parity requires.
`~` expansion via NSString.expandingTildeInPath (home directory) needs a Windows equivalent (%USERPROFILE%).
NSString.standardizingPath and URL.standardizedFileURL (remove `.`/`..`, macOS /private symlink quirks) must be replaced by Windows path normalization.

`.DS_Store`, `.noindex`, `-Xcc`, `DerivedData`, `xcuserdata`, `.swiftpm`, `ModuleCache` are macOS/Xcode artifacts; keeping the list verbatim is harmless for parity, and Windows-specific caches are not listed upstream.

ui_elements: None.
feature_notes: normalize: empty path -> ""; base = URL(fileURLWithPath: root, isDirectory: true).standardizedFileURL; path resolved relative to base and standardized; prefix = base.path with a trailing "/" ensured; if the path starts with prefix it is stripped; otherwise returned as the standardized absolute path (never nil, unlike relative).

relative: trims whitespace and newlines; returns nil when empty or containing "://"; expands a leading "~"; root standardized; absolute = path if it starts with "/" else root appended with path; standardized; must have prefix root + "/" (trailing slash ensured) else nil; returns the remainder, nil if empty (so the root itself gives nil).

isBuildOutput: splits on "/" omitting empties; true if any component is ".DS_Store", ends with ".noindex", or is in buildOutputNames. Matching is exact and case-sensitive per component; `build` and `dist` are deliberately not listed (doc comment: "a source folder called `build` or `dist` stays the project's business").

Doc comments cite the history: a head's build left "2,700 compiler cache records under `DroppyCode.xcodeproj/-Xcc`"; `.commandcode` is Command Code's taste-file folder that "rode along into two repositories' history before it was listed".
matches: over [file.path, file.oldPath] (nil oldPath dropped), true if touched contains the path exactly, or any touched entry hasSuffix("/" + path), or path hasSuffix("/" + touched entry).

B1->B2: One line changed: in relative(_:root:) line 20 `var path = path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` became `var path = path.trimmed`, using the new String.trimmed helper (defined in Core/Support/Text.swift as exactly `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`), so behaviour is unchanged. Line count unchanged at 60.

normalize vs relative are NOT the same normaliser and can answer differently for the same input: normalize (l.6-13) does no trimming (relative uses `path.trimmed`, l.20), does no `://` rejection (relative: `guard !path.isEmpty, !path.contains("://") else { return nil }`, l.21), has no explicit `~` handling (relative: `if path.hasPrefix("~") { path = (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath }`, l.22), and standardizes with `URL(fileURLWithPath:relativeTo:).standardizedFileURL` (l.8-9) where relative uses `(root as NSString).standardizingPath` and `(absolute as NSString).standardizingPath` (l.23, l.25). The absolute test differs too: normalize lets URL(fileURLWithPath:relativeTo:) decide, relative tests `path.hasPrefix("/")` (l.24). When path equals root, normalize returns the standardized absolute root (it lacks the `base.path + "/"` prefix, so nothing is stripped, l.10-12) while relative returns nil (`full.hasPrefix(prefix)` fails at l.27). normalize never returns nil: a path outside root comes back absolute. A port must keep two separate functions. Whether URL(fileURLWithPath:) itself expands a leading `~`, and whether standardizedFileURL and NSString.standardizingPath differ in `..` or `/private` handling, are Foundation behaviours this file does not establish.
unresolved_questions: DiffFile's definition (path/oldPath semantics for renames) lives elsewhere and was not read in this bundle.

purpose: Merges the three sources of a turn's file changes into one diff: the checkpoint-to-checkpoint working-tree snapshot, the provider's own patch, and the agent's per-tool FileEdit records, filtering the snapshot down to the files the turn actually named and de-duplicating by path.
key_symbols: static func merge(snapshot: [DiffFile]?, providerPatch: String, edits: [FileEdit], touched: Set<String>?, root: String, repositoryRoot: String? = nil, providerFiles: [DiffFile]? = nil) -> [DiffFile]
private static func append(_ file: DiffFile, to files: inout [String: DiffFile])
state_owned: Local only: files: [String: DiffFile] keyed by path, known: Set<String>?, authoritative: Set<String>. No stored state; the enum is a namespace.
side_effects: None; pure computation over already-collected diff text.
platform_assumptions: Unix absolute paths (the hasPrefix("/") tests), Foundation URL standardization, '/' separators.
ui_elements: No views; produces the [DiffFile] the turn's diff view renders, sorted ascending by path ($0.path < $1.path).
feature_notes: repositoryRoot defaults to root when not supplied; reportedPath(_:) resolves a path against `root` and then normalizes it against `repositoryRoot`, so a path an agent reported relative to a subfolder lands repository-relative.

The `known` set exists only when `touched` is non-nil; it is seeded from the normalized touched paths and then grown with every reported file's path and oldPath and every non-empty edit path. With touched == nil no filtering happens at all.
Recorded rationale: 'The snapshot is the whole checkout between two checkpoints, so only files the chat's turns reported, the provider's own patch, or its tool edits name are taken from it.'

Snapshot files are normalized against repositoryRoot directly (TouchedPaths.normalize), while provider-patch files go through reportedPath (resolved against root first). A snapshot file is skipped when `known` exists and contains neither its path nor its oldPath.
`reported` is providerFiles when supplied, otherwise DiffParser.parse(providerPatch), so callers can pass pre-parsed provider files and skip a re-parse.

When a snapshot exists, provider-patch files are only added for paths that still begin with '/' (they did not resolve inside the repository root) and are not already present, so the snapshot stays authoritative for in-repository files.

Edits are only added when their normalized path is not already in `authoritative` (the keys after snapshot and provider merging) and, when a snapshot exists, only when the path begins with '/'. The edit's diff text is parsed with DiffParser.parseHunks(edit.diff ?? "", path:); when that yields no hunks, edit.additions and edit.deletions are written into reportedAdditions/reportedDeletions so the counts still show.

append(_:to:) de-duplicates by path: a first file for a path is stored as is; a second has its hunks appended with hunk.id = (existing.hunks.last?.id ?? 0) + 1 (recomputed per hunk as the array grows, so ids stay contiguous), its additions and deletions summed into reportedAdditions/reportedDeletions, and isBinary OR-ed in.
Because append sets reportedAdditions/reportedDeletions on any merge, a merged file's counts stop being derived from its hunks.
The result is files.values sorted by path ascending.
unresolved_questions: FileEdit is declared outside this bundle, so the exact semantics of edit.diff (nil versus empty string) and whether additions/deletions are optional could not be verified here.

The `path.hasPrefix("/")` conditions imply reportedPath can return an absolute path for work outside the repository root; whether any shipped caller relies on that branch or it is purely defensive is not determinable from this file.

ui_elements: No views; a pure performance service behind the diff and checkpoint pipeline.
feature_notes: Documented performance motive with verbatim figures: every snapshot is `git add -A` over the whole tree, '46 ms on a 4k-file repository and 200 ms at 60k', and most commands only read.

Correctness protocol: before trusting the change count a cookie file is written in the git directory and the answer waits for that cookie's own FSEvents event, because events arrive in order, so everything written before the cookie has been counted by the time it lands.

settledGeneration() waits at most 1 second (Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))) for the cookie event. A cookie that never arrives tears the stream down permanently, after which every later snapshot is a fresh capture. It returns nil without a stream and when FileManager.createFile fails.

The waiter list is resumed exactly once: whichever of the event (note) or the timeout (expireWaiter) removes the waiter from state.waiters is the one that resumes its continuation, and continuations are resumed outside the lock. A cookie already seen before the continuation is installed resumes immediately with true.

note(paths:flags:) per event path: a lost-event flag sets both changed and everything; a path under cookiePrefix updates the cookie number (max) and is not counted as a change; a path under gitPrefix is skipped entirely because 'Git's own writes (objects, refs, the index) do not change the working files'; any other path marks changed, and unless it sits under rootPrefix with more bytes than rootPrefixBytes it means the whole tree (everything = true).
A changed path is recorded as the directory holding the entry, relative to the root, or as the entry itself when it sits at the root (relative.lastIndex(of: "/") split).
generation is bumped with &+= 1 (wrapping) once per callback that saw any change, not once per path.

changedLimit = 64: while inserting, once the set already holds 64 or more entries new entries are inserted as their top-level directory; after the loop, if the set exceeds 64 the whole set is collapsed with topLevel, so 'a build writing thousands of files costs one walk of its output'. changed == nil means the whole tree must be walked.
pathspecs(_:) sorts the changed set and drops any path nested inside the previously kept one (path.hasPrefix(last + "/")), producing minimal non-overlapping pathspecs.

shared(for:gitDirectory:) returns an existing watch for the directory, else requires volumeIsLocal == true, else nil. A race where two watches are built is resolved by keeping whichever reached the registry first and tearing down the loser; the registry is capped at 32 with the oldest torn down on its own queue after any callback in flight. The comment records the bug this fixed: tearing down the registered watch instead 'stopped its stream and deleted the scratch index a capture may be writing through'.

The stream roots are [root] when the git directory is inside the root, else [root, gitRoot], because a linked worktree's git directory lives outside the working tree and the cookies are written there.
A stream that fails to start is invalidated and released immediately and state.stream stays nil, so the watch degrades to fresh captures.
tearDown() nils the stream under the lock, then stops, invalidates and releases it on the watch's own queue and removes the scratch index, so no callback can be running when the stream goes.

currentTree(indexPath:capture:) short-circuits to capture(nil, nil) when there is no settled generation (no stream): the caller must then use a throwaway index of its own. Otherwise it loops over a Lookup decision: .tree returns the cached snapshot tree when its generation AND its IndexStamp both still match; .join awaits a capture at the same generation and retries the loop when that capture failed, because only the owner may rebuild the scratch index; .wait awaits a capture at a different generation and re-decides; .own runs the capture itself.

IndexStamp compares only the checkout index file's modificationDate and size, because the index's content is part of what write-tree produces for paths the capture does not walk, as when the user stages files outside the directory.

Incremental pathspecs are only passed when state.snapshot?.index == index (the real index has not moved since the last snapshot); otherwise nil forces a full walk. The changed set is reset to [] at that moment so writes during the walk accrue to the next capture.

On a successful own capture the snapshot is stored with commit: nil; on failure state.changed is set to nil (forcing a full walk next time) and CocoaError(.fileReadUnknown) is thrown. The capture slot is cleared only when it is still this task's.

commit(of:) returns the remembered checkpoint commit only when the current snapshot's tree matches exactly; remember(commit:of:) writes it only when the snapshot is still that tree, which is what makes a turn starting on an untouched tree cost only an `update-ref`.
unresolved_questions: The FSEvents latency argument is 0 with kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer, so delivery timing is up to the OS; whether one second is always enough for the cookie on a busy volume is empirical and this file does not answer it, though the code degrades safely by tearing the stream down.

kFSEventStreamCreateFlagFileEvents yields per-file paths, but the code stores only the holding directory; whether any caller would benefit from file-level granularity is decided in Git.swift's capture closure, not here.
The registry cap of 32 and changedLimit of 64 are stated without a recorded measurement, unlike the 46 ms / 200 ms figures.

purpose: MCPHub.swift is the in-app MCP client that the model-API providers use (OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:510 awaits MCPHub.shared.tools(), :904 awaits MCPHub.shared.call). The actor MCPHub reads server specs from the exported claude.json (MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL, readSpecs :126-149, command preferred over url). It lists tools per server in sorted id order, caching successes and adding failures to a failed set. It routes "mcp__<server>__<tool>" call names (parse :109-117) to one private MCPClient actor per server, and reload() (:100-107, called from MCPStore.swift:283) drops every client, cache and failure. MCPClient talks JSON-RPC to a stdio child (at most one relaunch, then dead: ensureStdio :266-277) or to a streamable-HTTP endpoint (initialize once, adopt Mcp-Session-Id: httpRPC :310-341). It flattens tools/call content to text with "[image]" and "[resource: <uri>]" placeholders (callTool :202-224) and turns every failure into an MCPHubError literal. In B3 the file owns no transport machinery of its own. The stdio child, the line reader and the reply demultiplexing now live in MCPStdioConnection (MCPWire.swift:121-246) over StdioProcess. The message builders, the tools/list paging, the error extraction and the HTTP POST/SSE reader are now MCPWire statics shared with MCPProbe. MCPLiveProcesses (:355-376) still records every launched server, now as a StdioProcess, so AppDelegate.swift:60 can end them all synchronously at quit.

feature_notes: B2->B3 is a transport extraction: 62 insertions, 243 deletions. The MCPHub actor itself (:1-150), including tools(), call(), reload(), parse() and readSpecs(), is byte-identical except track(_:) now takes StdioProcess (:26). Lines 1-157 keep their B2 numbering.

MCPClient stdio: B2's Process/Pipe wiring, the HubConversation line buffer (B2 :496-533), the replies map (B2 :169-172) and the 10 ms polling waitStdio (B2 :393-418) are gone. Replaced by one MCPStdioConnection (MCPWire.swift:121-246) over StdioProcess: requests await a CheckedContinuation keyed by RPCID, replies for other ids are buffered, and a task group races the reply against Task.sleep(timeout). User-visible literals are unchanged: "The server didn't answer in time.", "The server quit (exit <code>).", "The server quit.".

Changed stdio semantics (SOURCE FACT, from MCPWire.swift and StdioProcess.swift). (a) JSON-RPC ids are allocated per connection starting at 1 (MCPWire.swift:126, :164-168), so after the single relaunch the new child's initialize is id 1 again; B2 continued the client-wide nextID. (b) A process found not running is reported with its exit code after waitForExit (MCPWire.swift:163), not the bare B2 :410 "The server quit.". (c) Pending requests fail only when the message stream ends, at stdout EOF or 1 s after exit (StdioProcess.swift:177-182), not on the next 10 ms poll after the termination handler. (d) Reply ids match by RPCID, so a reply with string id "1" no longer matches request 1; B2 used JSONValue.int, which parses strings. (e) Stdout lines lose trailing CR/space and an unterminated final line is delivered at EOF (StdioProcess.swift:147-157). (f) Stderr is kept in a bounded buffer (StdioProcess.swift:159-166) instead of drained and discarded, but the hub never reads errorTail.

stop() (:173-178) now calls MCPStdioConnection.stop() -> StdioProcess.terminate() (StdioProcess.swift:120-129): stdin is closed first, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL on the pid alone after 3 s. B2's private MCPClient.terminate (B2 :286-295) sent SIGTERM and after 1 s SIGKILL to the process group when the child led one. So reload() and a listing failure now leave a stubborn server's group alive up to 3 s and then kill only the leader.

HTTP: post (:343-352) delegates to MCPWire.post and now passes the JSON-RPC id (init id :317, nil for the notification :328, request id :335). SSE is read incrementally (URLSession.bytes, MCPWire.swift:72-102), and the first data: object whose id (via JSONValue.int) equals the request id is returned, so a held-open stream no longer hangs the call and a frame for another id is skipped. For a notification (id nil) an SSE response returns body nil without reading the stream (MCPWire.swift:92). A non-2xx now reads up to 2000 body bytes into MCPHTTPError.body, but the hub still reports only "The server answered <status>." (:350); a non-HTTP response is still "The server sent something unexpected: invalid reply." (:348).

The initialize params, request/notification builders, checkReply's "unknown error" fallback and the ten-page tools/list cursor loop are unchanged in value. They moved to MCPWire (MCPWire.swift:7-51), where protocolVersion "2025-06-18" is one constant used for both the params and the MCP-Protocol-Version header. clientInfo is still {"name": "Droppy Code", "version": "1.0"} (MCPWire.swift:13), so the OD-0012 F1 deviation citation moves there.

MCPLiveProcesses (:355-376) now holds StdioProcess. terminateAll still snapshots running processes, terminates each and immediately SIGKILLs survivors by group or pid, with a new comment (:370) that the delayed SIGKILL in terminate() never fires at quit. Because StdioProcess.terminate also queues a stdin close, quit now closes each server's stdin (asynchronously) as well.

MCPProbe was switched to the same MCPStdioConnection/MCPWire in B3 (MCPProbe.swift:94, :116, :124, :152). So the hub and the probe now share one stdio reader and one SSE reader. PR-MCP-186's windows_path 'Do not unify the two readers' and the probe halves of PR-MCP-111/117 need the MCPProbe reader's confirmation.
unresolved_questions: Windows quit-time tree kill: the hub's children are now StdioProcess. The C# StdioProcess launches with UsesJobObject = false (src/Marrow.Core/Support/StdioProcess.cs:13, ED-126), and ProcessLauncher.KillTree without a job falls back to TerminateProcess on the pid alone (src/Marrow.Core/Port/ProcessLauncher.cs:476-487). A straight port would therefore leak npx's node grandchild at quit, against PR-MCP-191 and PR-LAUNCH-058's windows_path. This needs a ruling: a job object for hub-launched StdioProcess children, or a pid-tree kill.

Whether any real MCP server echoes a JSON-RPC id as a string is unknown. B3 stdio no longer matches such a reply (RPCID .string vs .int), while B3 HTTP SSE still does (JSONValue.int parses strings). The port must reproduce both as-is; there is no evidence that the difference is intended.

A non-2xx body is now the first 2000 BYTES read from the stream, decoded and trimmed (B2: first 2000 characters of the whole decoded body), which is also the text searched for "MCP server disabled". An SSE reply is read line by line as it streams and returns at the first data: line that parses as an object whose id .int equals the request's id (B2: any object with an id key, after the whole body arrived); a request with id nil (the notifications/initialized POST) and an SSE content type returns a nil body without reading the stream. unresolved_questions: PR-MCP-111's windows_path requires a graceful close then a forced kill of the whole process tree at 1 s (so npx's node grandchild does not leak). Upstream B3 now waits 3 s and kills only the pid (StdioProcess.swift:126-127), and the C# StdioProcess already implements ED-126 for that (TerminationLadder.Stdio: stdin close, CTRL_BREAK, +3 s TerminateProcess on the pid alone, no job). purpose: Status M. MCPProxy is the loopback HTTP relay at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp/<server id> that providers are pointed at for OAuth servers: it persists its port in mcp/proxy-port (kernel-picked, repicked once on a bind failure), parses a request head up to 65536 bytes and a Content-Length body up to 32 MiB, forwards five client headers plus the route's headers and a fresh bearer token upstream with a 3600 s timeout, replays once on an upstream 401, and writes back Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id and Cache-Control. purpose: New in B3 (commit d70cff8fe 'refactor: audit cleanups - five bug fixes, shared MCP and provider code, layer rules restored'): the MCP JSON-RPC wire layer that MCPHub (the in-app tool hub) and MCPProbe (the settings-page connection check) now share instead of each carrying its own copy. The caseless enum MCPWire holds the protocol constant "2025-06-18", the initialize params (clientInfo {"name": "Droppy Code", "version": "1.0"}), the request/notification envelopes, the error-object reader, the ten-page tools/list cursor walker and a streamable-HTTP POST that reads the response as a byte stream and returns at the first SSE 'data:' line whose id equals the request id, so a server that holds its event stream open no longer hangs the caller. MCPStdioConnection wraps the shared Core StdioProcess for a stdio MCP server: it launches the child in the home directory, numbers requests from 1, parks each request on a CheckedContinuation keyed by RPCID (buffering replies that arrive before anyone waits), races each request against a Task.sleep timeout, and fails every pending request with MCPWireError.exited(status) once the child's message stream ends; it replaces B2's two polling loops (MCPHub.waitStdio at 10 ms, MCPProbe.nextReply at 5 ms) and the private HubConversation / StdioConversation buffers.

Changed - non-2xx error body (:77-84): read byte by byte until 2000 BYTES, decoded as UTF-8 (repairing) and trimmed with .whitespacesAndNewlines, carried in MCPHTTPError(status:body:). B2 probe decoded the full body and kept the first 2000 CHARACTERS; B2 hub ignored the body (still does: it maps to "The server answered <status>."). A non-HTTP response becomes MCPHTTPError(status: nil, body: ""), which Hub maps to "The server sent something unexpected: invalid reply." and Probe to malformed("invalid reply") as before.

Changed - stdio reply wait (:162-217): continuation-based instead of polling (Hub 10 ms, Probe 5 ms). Replies for ids nobody is waiting on are buffered (the probe used to DISCARD them), so a reply that beats its awaitReply registration is still delivered. Matching uses RPCID, so a server that echoes the id as a JSON string "1" no longer matches integer request 1 (B2 matched through JSONValue.int, which parses numeric strings); a double 1.0 still matches.

Changed - timeouts (:170-186): each request races awaitReply against Task.sleep(for: .seconds(timeout)); the loser is cancelled, and on timeout or any error the id's continuation is removed (abandon) and MCPWireError.timedOut (or the error) is thrown. Callers keep their texts: Hub "The server didn't answer in time.", Probe exitError(code: nil) -> timedOut or unauthorizedOAuth.

Changed - exit detection (:163, :189-196, :235-245): a request on a non-running process throws exited(await waitForExit()); otherwise pending requests fail with exited(status) only when StdioProcess.messages finishes (stdout EOF, or 1 s after the child exits when a grandchild holds stdout, StdioProcess.swift:177-182), after waitForExit. In B2 the hub reacted to the termination handler on its next 10 ms poll. Because waitForExit always yields a status, the hub now reports "The server quit (exit N)." where B2 could say "The server quit."

Changed - stop (:152-154): StdioProcess.terminate (close stdin, SIGTERM, SIGKILL to the pid alone after 3 s) replaces the B2 terminate of both MCPHub and MCPProbe (SIGTERM, then after 1 s SIGKILL to the process group when the child leads one, else the pid).

Changed - stderr (:156): errorTail is the last 4000 bytes of the StdioProcess stderr buffer (itself capped at 64000, cut to the last 16000). The probe now feeds that tail, not its whole stderr buffer, into exitError's OAuth substring test and exited message; the hub's stderr, discarded in B2, is now buffered but unused.

Changed - output framing (via StdioProcess): lines are split on 0x0A, trailing CR and spaces are stripped, non-JSON lines are dropped, and an unterminated final line is delivered at EOF (B2 ignored an unterminated last line).

Changed - id numbering (:126, :164-168): per connection from 1. A hub client restarted after a crash sends initialize with id 1 again; B2 continued MCPClient.nextID across the restart. The stdio probe's sequence (1 initialize, 2.. tools/list) is unchanged. (The remote probe's fixed id 2 for every tools/list page is an MCPProbe.swift:196 change, not this file.)

purpose: Implements the ProviderSession for the four Agent Client Protocol (ACP) agents Droppy Code drives over JSON-RPC on stdio: Cursor, OpenCode, Grok and Devin (doc comment line 23). It spawns the agent CLI with provider- and runtime-mode-specific arguments, performs the ACP initialize / session/new or session/load handshake (with one authenticate retry), maps model, effort, Fast and plan/build mode onto session/set_config_option, session/set_model and session/set_mode, and translates session/update notifications and session/request_permission requests into ProviderEvents (message and reasoning deltas, tool rows, todo checklists, slash commands, approvals, context usage). It also hosts the static catalog probe (probeModels) that starts a throwaway session in a temp folder and walks every model to learn each one's effort scale, plus a file-scope ACPLaunchGate actor that spaces process starts 1.5 s apart so agents sharing a SQLite store do not hit "database is locked".

purpose: AntigravitySession drives Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) in headless stream-json mode, with one persistent process per thread.
