purpose: CopilotSession is the @MainActor ProviderSession that drives the GitHub Copilot CLI as a child process started with `--headless --stdio`, speaking the Copilot SDK's Content-Length framed JSON-RPC protocol (one process per thread, session created or resumed under Droppy Code's own lowercased UUID so history survives relaunches in `~/.copilot/session-state`). It maps the CLI's `session.event` notifications (assistant deltas, reasoning, usage, tool execution, sub-agents, permissions, mode/title changes, errors, compaction, idle, shutdown) onto ProviderEvent values, answers the CLI's server requests (`userInput.request`, `exitPlanMode.request`, `autoModeSwitch.request`), translates Droppy's RuntimeMode/InteractionMode, model and effort into CLI RPCs, and implements approvals, questions, interrupt, compaction, rewind-based rollback and slash-command invocation. It also exposes static one-shot helpers that spawn a throwaway connection in the temp directory to list models (`models.list`), read sign-in status (`account.getCurrentAuth`) and read plan limits (`account.getQuota`), plus pure mapping helpers (tool-call titles, apply_patch path extraction, update_todo checklist parsing, permission descriptions, session-approval decisions, error-message enrichment). With Hydra on it creates the session with custom agents, appends the Hydra policy to the system message and forwards head (sub-agent) events wrapped in `.agentEvent`.

displayPath (lines 33-38): trimmed empty -> workingDirectory; `trimmed.hasPrefix(workingDirectory)` is a raw string prefix with no separator boundary, then ToolTitles.relativePath (ProviderSession.swift line 194-197) strips `root + "/"` only when present, else returns the path unchanged. So "/proj2/x" under "/proj" passes the prefix test but comes back unchanged, and displayPath(workingDirectory) returns workingDirectory itself; any other input returns the trimmed input.

readFile: resolveURL, then `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath:)` (true for directories too, so a directory path gets whatever FileHandle(forReadingFrom:) or read(upToCount:) throws, not a Droppy message); missing -> "No such file: <display>."; reads in chunks of min(65_536, readLimit + 1 - count) until more than 1,000,000 bytes; over limit -> "That file is too large to read (<byteCount> bytes)." using seekToEnd; decode UTF-8 then ISO Latin-1 (`String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) ?? String(data: data, encoding: .isoLatin1)`), else "That file is not readable as text.".

readFile with startLine or lineCount: `text.split(separator: "
", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)` on a Swift String splits by Character, and "
" is one Character that is not equal to "
", so a CRLF file is not split (it is one "line": "(lines 1-1 of 1)" plus the whole file). Parity decision for the port: a JS split('
') would split CRLF files. first = max(1, startLine ?? 1); first > count -> "(the file has <n> lines; start_line <first> is past the end)"; count = max(1, lineCount ?? 200); returns "(lines first-last of total)
" plus the slice joined with "
".

readFile without range: returns text unchanged when `text.utf8.count <= 60_000` (UTF-8 bytes); otherwise characterCount = `text.count` (Swift grapheme clusters, not UTF-16 units) and if > 60,000 returns `String(text.prefix(60_000))` (first 60,000 grapheme clusters) plus "\n…(truncated, <characterCount> chars total; read the rest with start_line and line_count)". A JS .length/.slice port would cut and count differently.
writeFile: inside the Mutations actor; "Could not encode that content." if UTF-8 encoding fails; cancellation checked between each step.

editFile (lines 92-120), inside the Mutations actor: the empty-old check ("old_string must not be empty. Read the file first, then edit an exact block.") runs BEFORE resolveURL, so an empty old_string with an outside path gets the empty-old error. Reads with `String(contentsOf: url, encoding: .utf8)` and has no existence check: a missing or non-UTF-8 file throws Foundation's error, not a Droppy string, and Latin-1 files readFile accepts cannot be edited. Counts non-overlapping matches with `current.range(of: old, options: [], range: remaining)` on NSString: no .literalSearch, so canonically equivalent composed/decomposed sequences match (precomposed "é" matches "e" + combining accent) and ranges are UTF-16; a JS indexOf port is stricter. 0 -> "That exact text was not found in <display>. Read the file and copy it exactly."; >1 -> "That text appears <n> times in <display>. Include more context so it matches once."; replaces the single match and writes UTF-8 atomically.

listFiles: base = working directory when `path.trimmed.isEmpty`, else resolveURL(path); non-directory -> "No such directory: <displayPath(path.isEmpty ? workingDirectory : path)>." (untrimmed check here, though displayPath trims, so the text is the same). Recursive: FileManager enumerator with [.skipsHiddenFiles, .skipsPackageDescendants], in enumerator order (NOT sorted); any entry whose lastPathComponent is in skippedDirectories is skipped (skipDescendants) even when it is a FILE named e.g. build, dist or target; directories are not listed; entries are ToolTitles.relativePath(url.path, to: workingDirectory), i.e. relative to the project root, not to base. Non-recursive: contentsOfDirectory sorted with Swift String < (case-sensitive); drops names in skippedDirectories (files too) and names starting with ".DS_Store"; each entry is relativePath(full, to: workingDirectory) + "/" for directories, so listing "src" yields "src/a.swift", not bare names; other hidden files are kept. Both: `if results.count >= 300 { results.append("…(truncated)"); break }` fires on the 300th entry even if nothing follows, so exactly 300 entries return 301 lines with the marker. purpose: OpenAICompatibleSession is the one @MainActor ProviderSession implementation behind the DeepSeek, Meta and Z.ai native API providers. Subclasses supply a Config (kind, title, agentIdentity, defaultModel, chatURL, contextWindow, maxOutputTokens, replaysReasoning, isVisionModel) and override applyProviderPayload, reasoningEffort(for:model:) and friendlyError. It runs the whole agent loop: the system prompt (mode line, Hydra fallback policy, anti-slop policy, project AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md guidance, today's ISO date), SSE streaming through a detached drain and a 30 ms StreamCoalescer actor, two transport retries at 1 s and 2 s for networkConnectionLost, timedOut and cannotConnectToHost, and the six built-in tools (read_file, list_files, search_text, write_file, edit_file, run_command) plus MCPHub tools. It also runs up to four concurrent approval-free reads, raises approvals with 'Approve' / 'Approve for turn' / 'Decline', and keeps the plan-mode block ahead of approve-for-turn. It applies the Hydra head wrap-up, pacing and final-report budget, condenses history (160,000 bytes down to 100,000, keeping the last 10 results whole), trims it above 60 messages, repairs tool-call chains, and stops a turn at a 200-round ceiling.

purpose: PiSession is the ProviderSession that drives the Pi coding harness as one long-lived `pi --mode rpc` child per thread, speaking LF-delimited JSONL over stdin/stdout: it launches pi with `--mode rpc -e <extension> --approve|--no-approve [--provider/--model] [--thinking] [--session <file>]`, performs the get_state then get_commands handshake, sends prompt/set_model/set_thinking_level/abort/compact lines, and turns message_start/message_update/message_end/tool_execution_*/agent_end/compaction_*/auto_retry_start/extension_error/extension_ui_request lines into ProviderEvents. It also owns Droppy's own approval gate for Pi: it writes a per-session JSON gate file (runtimeMode, interactionMode, finalReport, systemPrompt "") that the installed pi extension reads before each tool call, answers the extension's `droppy-gate ` select requests with "Allow" / "Allow for session" / "Deny" (remembering session grants by kind), and maps confirm/input/editor/select/notify extension UI requests to questions and notices. At B3 its stream-id bookkeeping, write snapshots, request continuations, tool-text extraction and grant keys are delegated to shared helpers (StreamedTextTracker, EditSnapshots, PendingReplies, ToolText, ApprovalRequest.Kind.grantKey) and its close path now releases every pending request with JSON null.

purpose: Defines the PlanLimits value model (rolling usage windows, an optional plan name, optional banked reset credits and an optional problem string) plus the ResetOutcome and ResetCreditError types used when spending a banked reset. The @MainActor PlanLimitsReader enum decides which providers expose subscription limits, dispatches the read to each provider's own reader (Codex, Antigravity, Copilot sessions, CommandCodeAPI, PiPlanLimits, ZaiAPI for the API-key path), and itself implements Claude's limit read: first the Claude Code OAuth usage endpoint using the stored login (credentials file or macOS Keychain), with a CLI-driven token refresh, and failing that a short-lived `claude -p` stream-json session that sends an `initialize` then a `get_usage` control request. It also holds shared helpers for window titles from minute counts, plan-name capitalisation, Codex plan-name mapping and Claude timestamp parsing.

readClaudeFromCLI (253-290) sends {"type":"control_request","request_id":"droppy-code-init","request":{"subtype":"initialize","hooks":null}}. Every message whose `type` is not "control_response" is skipped. The request id is read from the NESTED object, not the top level: `let response = message["response"] ?? .null; switch response["request_id"]?.string`. On "droppy-code-init" it sends {"type":"control_request","request_id":"droppy-code-usage","request":{"subtype":"get_usage"}}. On "droppy-code-usage": `let usage = response["response"] ?? .null; let rateLimits = usage["rate_limits"] ?? .null`, so the key paths are message.response.request_id, message.response.response.rate_limits (root for fallback/extra usage), message.response.response.rate_limits.limits (rows) and message.response.response.subscription_type. The plan name is `planName(usage["subscription_type"]?.string)` only, with NO " (Nx)" tier suffix (unlike the endpoint path's `login.planName`). Other request ids continue; stream end returns nil.

parseClaudeUsage (294-329): rows come from `limits.enumerated().compactMap`, so the index is the position in the raw `limits` array BEFORE rows lacking a numeric "percent" are dropped; ids can therefore skip numbers. kind = `limit["kind"]?.string ?? ""`, so a missing kind gives id "-<index>" (e.g. "-0"). id is `"\(idPrefix)\(kind)-\(index)"` with idPrefix = `titlePrefix.map { $0.lowercased() + "-" } ?? ""`. group = `self.planName(limit["group"]?.string) ?? "Usage"` (capitalises only the first character); model name from `limit["scope"]?["model"]?["display_name"]?.string`. percent is taken as reported and NOT clamped (ZaiAPI clamps to 0...100; Claude does not). resetsAt from `limit["resets_at"]?.string.flatMap(parseDate)`. When no row survives, falls back to root["five_hour"] / root["seven_day"] `utilization` with ids `"\(idPrefix)\(key)"` ("five_hour"/"seven_day" without a prefix) and resetsAt from `window["resets_at"]?.string.flatMap(parseDate)`. Extra usage is appended when root.extra_usage.is_enabled == true and utilization is numeric, id `"\(idPrefix)extra-usage"`, resetsAt nil. All three id forms take the lowercased titlePrefix. Returns nil when no windows; planName passed through; problem and resetCredits left nil.
parseDate strips any fractional seconds matching \.\d+ before ISO 8601 parsing, because Claude writes microsecond timestamps.

purpose: ProjectGuidance loads a project's own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md from the working directory root only (never parents, never a scan) and renders them into one system-prompt block for the native API sessions, which build their system prompt from scratch. It caches the rendered block and re-renders only when a file's size or modification date changes, and it enforces a 16,000-byte per-file and 24,000-byte total budget, replacing any file that does not fit with an instruction to read it through the read_file tool so no rule is silently dropped. Symlinks that resolve outside the working directory and non-regular files are ignored.

purpose: The @MainActor @Observable ProviderRegistry is the app's single source of truth for every provider's install/sign-in state (ProviderStatus with its summary strings "Not installed", "Signed in as ...", "Signed in", "Not signed in", "Installed · <version>"), for each provider's model catalog (seeds for Claude, DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai, Antigravity, Copilot, Command Code and Pi; live catalogs from the CLIs, ACP probes and APIs, cached under providerModelCatalogs with dates under providerModelCatalogDates), for slash-command lists per (provider, directory), plan limits, pay-as-you-go credits and banked-reset spending. It resolves each CLI's executable (custom path, PATH via LoginEnvironment.which, then per-provider fallback directories), builds its environment (PATH prefix, COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY, OpenCode MCP env, GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH), and runs the version/auth probes. purpose: ProviderSession.swift is the provider-neutral contract every CLI, ACP and API adapter implements. It defines TurnInput (one turn's request), SessionConfiguration (launch settings, including apiKey, hydra, transcript replay, isHydraHead and antiSlopEnabled), TranscriptMessage, AgentSpawn, the 31-case ProviderEvent stream normalized into a thread, and ToolUpdate. It also defines the @MainActor ProviderSession protocol (onEvent, isRunning, start, send, interrupt, resolveApproval, answerQuestion, compact, stop, stopAgent with a default of false), ProviderError with its user-facing messages, and the ToolTitles helpers (unwrapShell, relativePath, diffStats). At B3 it also hosts two helpers taken out of individual sessions: ToolText.blocks, which reads the text of a string or content-block array, and ApprovalRequest.Kind.grantKey, the key an 'approve for session' grant is stored under.

feature_notes: matches() lowercases the text and returns true on any of: "usage limit", "hit your limit", "usage_limit", "limit reached", "out of extra usage"
Timestamp form: regex \|\s*(\d{9,}) (at least 9 digits after a pipe), as in "usage limit reached|1757865600"; values greater than 1e11 are treated as milliseconds and divided by 1000
Clock form: regex (?i)resets?(?:\s+at)?\s+(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm), matching "resets 3pm" or "resets at 3:30 pm"
12-hour conversion: PM with hour < 12 adds 12; AM with hour == 12 becomes 0; missing minutes default to 0
A timezone in parentheses matching \(([A-Za-z_]+/[A-Za-z_]+)\) (for example "(America/New_York)") overrides Calendar.current.timeZone for the computed reset
The clock time is resolved as the next matching time strictly after `now` using Calendar.nextDate(after:matching:matchingPolicy:.nextTime)
The weekday branch of format() compares against a 6-day horizon computed from Date.now (not from the passed date), so a date more than 6 days out falls through to the abbreviated date form
resetTime returns nil when neither pattern matches, and also when the matched clock digits fail to parse as an hour

purpose: enum ZaiAPI is the lightweight client for Z.ai's GLM Coding Plan (https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4), used for key validation, the model catalog and the Coding Plan usage features; ZaiSession does the chat streaming. It offers only glm-5.3 ids, never GLM-5.3-FlashX, with efforts [low, high, max] defaulting to max, a 1,000,000-token context and 128,000 max output tokens, and treats ids containing 'flash' or ending in 'v' as vision models. Plan limits come from the monitor quota endpoint as CREDIT_LIMIT/TOKENS_LIMIT windows titled from unit codes, plus a 'Monthly · MCP tools' TIME_LIMIT window. It also reads reset cards from customer-package-reset/list and spends one through customer-package-reset/use followed by a two-second wait. Card expiries are parsed as naive Asia/Shanghai 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss', and counts are formatted with en_US grouping. At B3 validate and listModels delegate to OpenAICompatibleAPI, planLimits builds its request with OpenAICompatibleAPI.bearerRequest, and the reset-date DateFormatter is cached in a static.

purpose: Storage.swift is the Services-layer persistence hub. It names the on-disk layout: library.json, threads/<UUID>.json and attachments/ under the store root (now taken from Core's StoragePaths.root), plus worktrees/ and patches/ under the home state directory <home>/<AppInfo.stateDirectoryName>. It also loads the library, reads, decodes and deletes thread documents, and imports attachments: a file copy, HEIC/HEIF to JPEG at quality 0.88, a pasted image stored as 'Pasted image.png', at most 8 files a message. It sweeps orphaned attachment files older than 24 hours. The same file defines DocumentPrefetch, a Mutex-guarded background decoder with a 12-entry / 16 MiB RecentCache, a 24-request queue and an urgent front-of-queue path. It also defines DiskWriter: one serial 'droppycode.storage.write' queue that coalesces saves per URL, writes atomically through JSONEncoder.storage, logs 'Droppy Code could not save %@: %@' on failure and, new in B3, remembers the byte size of each file's last asynchronous write.

purpose: TokenLedger.swift owns the daily AI-token spend behind the Token activity heatmap in Settings, General. TokenSpendTracker turns cumulative provider counters into positive per-event deltas. The @MainActor @Observable TokenLedger singleton merges three sources: legacy v1 per-day totals, live spend saved to token-activity-live-v2.json 2 seconds after the first unsaved record, and a one-time detached scan of Codex rollouts under ~/.codex/sessions and ~/.codex/archived_sessions. The scan tails 131072 bytes of each rollout, subtracts the total inherited on resume by reading up to 8 MiB of the head, and caches per-file fingerprints in token-activity-codex-v3.json, migrating the v2 file and the old 'droppycode.tokenActivity.codexFiles' preference. It reconciles live Codex spend recorded by earlier processes per rollout identity, newest day first. The file also defines TokenActivityMode (Daily/Weekly/Cumulative) and TokenActivityGrid.build, the current-year grid of Sunday-first week columns with fixed English month ticks.

Edge semantics that changed with the JSONValue switch (JSONValue.swift:26-45, :83-90): (a) a total_tokens or last_token_usage.total_tokens given as a JSON string such as "123" now parses through Int(String), where B2 rejected it; (b) a JSON boolean no longer converts (B2's 'as? NSNumber' turned true into 1), so a boolean total now skips the line and a boolean last counts as 0; (c) a finite non-integral number truncates toward zero as before; (d) a finite double outside Int's range now reaches Int(Double) and traps, where B2's NSNumber.intValue did not trap; (e) parse now allows fragments, but a non-object line still yields no payload and is skipped.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: nothing in the pinned source shows whether Codex ever writes total_tokens as a string, boolean, non-integral or out-of-range number. The B3 coercion differences affect only those shapes, and the Int(Double) trap case has no guard in the source.

PR-SETTINGS-137 and UI-SETTINGS-024 cite TokenLedger.swift:626-629 for monthNames. At B2 those lines were a blank line, the build(daily:mode:now:) signature and the first two calendar lines; monthNames was at B2 :623-625 (PR-USAGE-110 cites that correctly). At B3 it is :614-616.

Pre-existing, not a B2->B3 delta: the C# InheritedTotal (TokenLedger.cs:572-597) decodes the head lossily and splits the whole text. The Swift inheritedTotal (:502-533) parses raw line bytes and only examines lines that end in 0x0A, so a final unterminated line in the 8 MiB head is never parsed and invalid UTF-8 makes JSONSerialization fail. The port can therefore accept a line upstream skips. This is worth an adversarial check when the scanner is re-ported.

purpose: New at B3 (status A, 304 lines, added by commit d70cff8fe 'refactor: audit cleanups'): the single AppKit press-tracking strip that now backs every drag handle in the app, replacing three separate B2 NSView classes (SidebarResizeHandleView at B2 WindowChrome.swift:402-571, TerminalResizeHandleView at B2 TerminalPanel.swift:142-256, PanelDragHandleView at B2 SubagentPanel.swift:677-738). DragHandleView (lines 6-267) owns the cursor rect, first-click acceptance, the no-window-move press, an optional slop before a press becomes a drag, a pushed drag cursor, an optional double-click callback, travel reporting per Axis (horizontal x only, vertical y positive up, free with y running down like a panel offset) and, when a Grip is configured, a centred CALayer grip bar that grows on hover plus an optional glow layer below it, both painted in NSColor.labelColor. DragHandle (lines 270-304) is the NSViewRepresentable face that pushes one configuration (axis, grip, cursor, dragCursor, slop, isActive, four callbacks) into the view on make and on every update; its three B3 call sites are SidebarResizeHandle (WindowChrome.swift:379-400: horizontal, Grip 10/22/2.5, glowInset 30, refreshesHoverOnLayout, .columnResize), TerminalResizeHandle (TerminalPanel.swift:114-131: vertical, Grip 12/28/2.5, .resizeUpDown) and PanelDragHandle (SubagentPanel.swift:646-666: free, slop 2, open-hand cursor, closed-hand drag cursor, optional double-click).

feature_notes: SOURCE FACT: the file is new at B3; git diff B2..B3 shows 304 insertions and the only commit touching it is d70cff8fe ('refactor: audit cleanups'), which in the same change reduced SidebarResizeHandle (WindowChrome.swift), TerminalResizeHandle (TerminalPanel.swift) and PanelDragHandle (SubagentPanel.swift) from NSViewRepresentable wrappers over their own NSView classes to SwiftUI Views whose body is a configured DragHandle (B3 WindowChrome.swift:379-400, TerminalPanel.swift:114-131, SubagentPanel.swift:646-666).

SOURCE FACT (sidebar strip, B2 WindowChrome.swift:402-571 vs B3): the configuration reproduces B2 exactly (rest 10, shown 22, thickness 2.5, alpha 0.6, glow 0.05/0.10, glow radius 4, glow inset trafficLightTop + trafficLightDiameter, 0.18 s ease-out, hover re-read on every layout, .columnResize, isActive gating of cursor rect, hover and hitTest). The only differences: mouseUp is now ignored unless a drag is in progress (222-223), a strip removed from its window mid-drag now clears isDragging (130-131), and mouseDown checks clickCount == 2 for an onDoubleClick the sidebar never sets. None is observable in normal use.

SOURCE FACT (terminal strip, B2 TerminalPanel.swift:142-256 vs B3): the grip literals are unchanged (rest 12, shown 28, thickness 2.5, alpha 0.6, 0.18 s ease-out, .resizeUpDown, travel positive upward). Two behaviours are new for the terminal strip: on release it re-reads the real cursor position before animating the grip (230-231), so a drag released off the strip now retracts the grip, where B2 left isHovering at the last enter/exit value; and on entering a window it re-reads hover and snaps the grip (134-137), which B2's terminal view did not override. The grip update at release now runs after onEnd instead of before it (B2: onChange, isDragging = false, updateGrip, onEnd; B3: isDragging = false, onChange, onEnd, refreshHover, updateGrip). The terminal strip also gains an invisible glow layer (glowInset nil, opacity always 0) and an isActive that is always true.

SOURCE FACT (panel drag handles, B2 SubagentPanel.swift:677-738 vs B3): no observable change. slop 2, open-hand cursor, closed-hand drag cursor pushed once the travel passes the slop on either axis, double-click on clickCount 2, y-down travel, pop on release and on removal mid-drag are all kept. The view is now layer-backed with two invisible layers and runs updateGrip/refreshHover with no grip, which draws nothing.

SOURCE FACT: the mouseDownCanMoveWindow comment was generalised from the sidebar-specific B2 text about the strip running through the title bar to 'The drag owns the press, so the window never moves with it.' (185); the behaviour is identical.

SOURCE FACT, latent only: with slop == 0 mouseDown sets isDragging without pushing dragCursor (205-207), yet mouseUp and viewDidMoveToWindow pop whenever dragCursor != nil (132, 226). No B3 call site combines slop 0 with a drag cursor (sidebar and terminal pass no dragCursor; the panel handle passes slop 2), so no unbalanced pop is reachable.

SOURCE FACT: onChange is called with the release travel before onEnd, and onEnd is not called when the view is taken out of its window mid-drag (only isDragging is cleared and the cursor popped, 129-133).
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: the comment at 229 says no exit arrives while the button is held; the port's hover-at-release behaviour for the terminal strip depends on it, and whether Avalonia raises PointerExited while the pointer is captured on Windows has to be established by a test, not assumed.

feature_notes: setFixedContent exists because an NSHostingController publishes preferredContentSize after show(relativeTo:), and AppKit then resizes the shown panel from its top edge, leaving the arrow floating above the anchor; sizingOptions = [] leaves contentSize in charge.

PopoverScroll with a width is 'premeasured': later onGeometryChange heights are ignored (the panel never resizes), so the scroll absorbs any difference; without a width, contentHeight follows onGeometryChange.
PopoverCloseBox compares by reference so the environment value does not invalidate every reader on each update; closePopover is the plain-closure facade that wraps a new box on set.
RowAction.id is its title, so two actions with the same title in one list collide in ForEach.
Checkmark column is kept for every row of a choice list whenever isChecked is non-nil (true or false).

purpose: The pure-value state machine behind a live grip-drag reorder of rows in a vertical stack: it tracks pointer travel, subtracts the slot movement already applied so the grabbed row stays pinned under the pointer, and walks the row across every neighbour whose centre it has passed in a single call.
calls_into: Foundation only; the move closure is supplied by the caller, the list view that owns the order
state_owned: id: the grabbed row's identifier, nil when nothing is being dragged
translation: pointer travel since the grab
settled: accumulated slot compensation, mutated inside settle()
side_effects: None of its own; it calls the caller's move closure, which reorders the caller's model
platform_assumptions: None specific to macOS: pure Swift and Foundation, generic over a Hashable ID. It assumes a vertical stack whose per-row heights the caller can supply.
ui_elements: visualOffset is the y offset the caller applies to the grabbed row
pastCentre defaults to 0; the doc comment records that the follow-up queue passes a quarter so a row held over the middle of a neighbour pairs with it instead of swapping
feature_notes: settle() guards on id being set and present in order, returning false otherwise

Downward branch (offset > 0 and current + 1 < order.count): swaps with order[current + 1] when offset > (own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre and move(next, true) returns true, then settled += slot and current += 1

Upward branch (offset < 0 and current > 0): swaps with order[current - 1] when -offset > (own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre and move(previous, false) returns true, then settled -= slot and current -= 1
The loop repeats so one fast flick crosses several rows in a single call; it breaks as soon as a threshold is not met or move returns false
A row's own height comes from heights[id] with fallbackHeight as the default, and each neighbour's slot height likewise

The doc comment explains that the compensation must be folded into settled here rather than inside move, because settle() mutates a copy of the caller's @State and a write from inside move would be invisible to the loop and clobbered when the copy is written back
move's placeAfter parameter is true when placing after the neighbour (downward) and false when placing before it (upward)
unresolved_questions: The caller that passes pastCentre = 0.25, described in the comment as the follow-up queue, is not in this bundle, so the pairing behaviour it enables is known only from the comment.

purpose: New file in 1.6.2 that REPLACES B1's conversation-only text zoom (B1 DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift, 71 lines, deleted in B2): defines the app-wide zoom, a fixed ladder of eight percentages (75 to 200) with normalisation and step helpers, plus a SwiftUI ViewModifier that applies the zoom to a window's whole content. The zoom is implemented as layout-in-shrunk-space then scale-up: a private custom Layout proposes the window size divided by the scale to the content, reports the content size multiplied by the scale, and the content is drawn with scaleEffect anchored top-leading, so larger zoom shows less content (reflowing, scrollbars stay inside the window) rather than clipping. Callers elsewhere are AppCommands.swift:53-62 (menu items "Zoom In" Command-+, "Zoom Out" Command--, "Actual Size" Command-0, plus a hidden second "Zoom In" on Command-=), AppSettings (persisted appZoom Int, normalised on load), SettingsView's AppZoomCard (stepper buttons disabled at the ladder ends) and WindowManager line 175 which applies .modifier(AppZoomModifier(percent: model.settings.appZoom)).

feature_notes: normalized: any percent not exactly in levels (e.g. 80, 0, 300) returns 100, not the nearest level.

next(increasing: true) returns the first level strictly greater than the normalised current, or the current if already at 200; next(increasing: false) returns the last level strictly less, or the current if already at 75. Because it normalises first, next(80, increasing: true) returns 110 (80 -> 100 -> 110).
AppZoomModifier computes scale = CGFloat(AppZoom.normalized(percent)) / 100, so an invalid percent renders at 1.0.

ZoomLayout.sizeThatFits: returns .zero when there is no subview; otherwise asks the first subview for its size under the proposal divided by scale (nil dimensions stay nil) and returns that size multiplied by scale.
ZoomLayout.placeSubviews: places only subviews.first at bounds.origin with anchor .topLeading and proposal = bounds.size divided by scale. Other subviews (none expected) are ignored.
The doc comments state the intent verbatim: "a bigger zoom shows less at once instead of clipping" and "a bare `scaleEffect` would clip the enlarged content".

Menu commands (AppCommands.swift:53-62, outside this file): Button("Zoom In") sets appZoom = AppZoom.next(appZoom, increasing: true) with `.keyboardShortcut("+", modifiers: .command)`; Button("Zoom Out") next(..., increasing: false) with `("-", modifiers: .command)`; Button("Actual Size") sets `appZoom = 100` directly with `("0", modifiers: .command)`; a second Button("Zoom In") with `.keyboardShortcut("=", modifiers: .command)` and `.hidden()`, commented "US keyboards produce '=' for Command-plus without Shift". Windows port: Ctrl+Plus, Ctrl+=, Ctrl+Minus and Ctrl+0 drive this ladder, and Electron's built-in zoom accelerators (menu roles zoomIn/zoomOut/resetZoom) must not also fire.

(2) ladder: B1 `private static let percentages = [80, 90, 95, 100, 110, 125, 135]` (line 10), `static let defaultIndex = 3` (line 13), `clamped` = `min(stepCount - 1, max(0, index))` (lines 16-18); B2 [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200] with anything off the ladder normalised to 100. feature_notes: B2->B3 diff (git diff 1fbf81e...HEAD -- Components.swift) touches exactly RelativeTime.duration. B2: `let total = max(0, Int(interval.rounded())); if total < 60 { return "\(total)s" }; if total < 3_600 { return "\(total / 60)m \(total % 60)s" }; return "\(total / 3_600)h \((total % 3_600) / 60)m"` (a hand-rolled 3-tier formatter that always clamps negative intervals to 0 and never shows more than two units). B3 replaces the whole body with `Duration.seconds(max(0, Int(interval.rounded()))).formatted(.units(allowed: [.seconds, .minutes, .hours], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down)))` - a call into Swift's system Duration/UnitsFormatStyle machinery instead of a fixed string template. This removes 2 lines net (168 -> 166 total lines) and shifts every line after the function (old line >=42) by -2 versus B2.

This is a genuine algorithm swap, not a pure refactor: the exact narrow-width, ICU-driven unit formatting (locale-specific abbreviations, zero-unit dropping/padding behaviour, rounding of the hidden fractional part) is now delegated to Apple's Duration.FormatStyle rather than being fully specified by the three fixed templates the old code hard-coded. Whether the two produce byte-identical strings for every boundary (0s, 59s/60s, 3599s/3600s, and values with a non-zero seconds remainder above one hour) cannot be determined from source alone.

The already-ported C# RelativeTime.Duration (src/Marrow.UI/Common/Components.cs lines 82-93) still implements the OLD B2 3-tier hand-rolled algorithm verbatim (`{total}s` / `{total/60}m {total%60}s` / `{total/3_600}h {(total%3_600)/60}m`), and the pinned unit test file (tests/Marrow.UI.Tests/Common/ComponentsTests.cs lines 103-141, 5 Duration facts) asserts exactly that old algorithm's outputs (0s, 45s, 1m 30s, 1h 2m, -10s->0s). Both need to be revisited against B3's Duration.FormatStyle-based behaviour.

The C# tests' Req trait for these five Duration facts cites "PR-SIDEBAR-074", but PR-SIDEBAR-074's own source_evidence in porting/spec/SIDEBAR.json actually cites Components.swift:20-35 (RelativeTime.short), not the duration function at :36-41/:37-42; the record that actually documents duration's old three-tier algorithm is CHAT.json's PR-CHAT-116 (and UI-CHAT-035). This mislabeled Req trait should be corrected when the duration behaviour is reclassified.
unresolved_questions: The exact strings `Duration.seconds(_:).formatted(.units(allowed: [.seconds,.minutes,.hours], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down)))` produces on the pinned B3 macOS runtime for the boundary values the old algorithm and the existing C# tests care about (0, 45, 90, 3725 seconds, and negative input after clamping to 0) - needed before PR-CHAT-116/UI-CHAT-035 can be re-specified and before Components.cs's Duration() and ComponentsTests.cs can be rewritten to match.

Whether Apple's narrow Duration.UnitsFormatStyle ever renders all three units (h, m, s) at once for a value like 3725s, given maximumUnitCount: 2 versus the old code's fixed two-unit-above-3600s cap - cannot be confirmed without running the pinned binary or an equivalent Swift snippet.

purpose: The Metal stitchable distortion shader that reproduces the macOS Dock genie effect for archived rows: it maps each destination pixel back into the flying row's frame through a fixed funnel whose sides bend from the row's width down to a narrow neck at the target point.
key_symbols: [[ stitchable ]] float2 genie(float2 position, float progress, float4 source, float2 target)
locals: t, pinch, slide, width, height, flip, x0, y0, targetY, positionY, travel, depth, bend, neck, left, right, u, sourceY
calls_into: Invoked from Swift as ShaderLibrary.genie(.float(progress), .float4(x, y, w, h), .float2(target.x, target.y)) in Genie.swift
platform_assumptions: Metal Shading Language compiled into the app's default shader library
SwiftUI's [[stitchable]] distortionEffect convention: the function receives a destination position and returns the source position to sample
feature_notes: progress is animation progress 0...1, explicitly never a clock; source is the row's frame (x, y, width, height) and target the neck, both in the layer's coordinates
pinch = smoothstep(0.0, 0.45, t) controls how far the sides have bent in; slide = smoothstep(0.2, 1.0, t) controls how far the row has travelled
flip = 1.0 when target.y >= source.y + height * 0.5, else -1.0; the vertical axis is mirrored on the way in and out so a target above the row funnels upwards
travel = max(targetY - y0, height); depth = clamp((positionY - y0) / travel, 0, 1); bend = pinch * smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, depth)
neck = min(24.0, width): the funnel's narrow end is at most 24 points wide
left = mix(x0, target.x - neck * 0.5, bend), right = mix(x0 + width, target.x + neck * 0.5, bend), u = (position.x - left) / max(right - left, 0.0001)

Three discard conditions return 'nothing' (-100000, -100000), sampling nothing: positionY > targetY (past the neck), u outside [0, 1] (outside the funnel), and sourceY outside [y0, y0 + height] (past the row)
sourceY = positionY - slide * (targetY - y0); the returned sample is float2(x0 + u * width, flip * sourceY)

purpose: Owns the single hover popover that appears when the pointer rests on a Hydra head mention (a helper-agent persona name/glyph chip) inside a chat paragraph. It debounces the show by 250 ms, measures a fixed 300 pt wide SwiftUI card (glyph, persona name, task text, status line) and presents it in an application-defined NSPopover with `popover.show(relativeTo: rect, of: view, preferredEdge: .maxY)` against the mention's rect (the source fixes only the edge .maxY; which side of the mention that is on screen depends on the anchor view's coordinate flipping, see unresolved_questions); hide cancels the pending show and closes it. The card's status line tells the user whether the head is working or finished, and that a click opens its chat.

feature_notes: show(): if popover.isShown and shownID == target.threadID, returns immediately (no re-show for the same head). This early return (line 20 `if popover.isShown, shownID == target.threadID { return }`) comes before `pending?.cancel()` (line 21), so it does not cancel a pending show for another head: with A shown, show(B) starts a B task; a show(A) within 250 ms returns early, B's task survives, and when it fires it closes A (`if self.popover.isShown { self.popover.close() }`) and shows B's card anchored to B's rect. In the MarkdownView.swift:1170-1181 hover caller, any hover sample over non-head text between the two mentions calls `HydraHeadHoverPopover.shared.hide()`, which cancels the pending task, so the stale show happens only when the hover samples jump from one mention to the other and back without landing between them.

setFixedContent (UI/Chrome/Popovers.swift:29-40) frames the card to the measured size with alignment .top and .clipped(), and the hosting controller has sizingOptions = [] with contentSize = size, so a card taller than measured loses its bottom (the status line) and never its header; the source comment reads "content that turns out taller than measured loses its tail behind the panel's edge, never its header".
show(): cancels any pending task, then starts a Task that sleeps 250 ms; if self is gone or the task was cancelled, it does nothing.

After the delay: closes an already-shown popover, builds HydraHeadHoverCard, measures NSHostingView(rootView: content.frame(width: 300)).intrinsicContentSize, forces width >= 300 and height 78 when height <= 0, calls popover.setFixedContent(content, size: size), sets shownID = target.threadID, then popover.show(relativeTo: rect, of: view, preferredEdge: .maxY).
Comment explains the width pin: asked for intrinsic size unpinned, the hosting view could answer narrower than the card's fixed frame and the popover wrapped the task a couple of words per line.
hide(): cancels and nils pending, performClose(nil) if shown, sets shownID = nil. popoverDidClose also sets shownID = nil.
Name uses persona.color (SwiftUI Color); task text is limited to 3 lines.

B1->B2: only the three card fonts changed from fixed point sizes to semantic text styles: persona name .system(size: 13, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.body, weight: .semibold); task .system(size: 12) -> .system(.callout); status .system(size: 11) -> .system(.subheadline). On macOS those styles are nominally 13/12/11 pt, so default rendering is expected to match, but the text now follows the system text-style scale. No logic, string or geometry changes.
unresolved_questions: Exact point sizes that .body/.callout/.subheadline resolve to on the owner's macOS (expected 13/12/11) should be confirmed from Apple's macOS text-style table before hard-coding them on Windows.

Whether preferredEdge .maxY places the popover above or below the mention depends on the caller's view flipping (LinkTextView is an NSTextView, which is flipped, so likely below); the caller is outside this file.

purpose: New at B3: a SwiftUI ViewModifier, LinkHoverModifier, that owns the pointer-hover behaviour of a rendered link paragraph. It shows the pointing-hand cursor only while the pointer is over a real link, and shows the shared HydraHeadHoverPopover card while the pointer rests on a head mention whose name, URL and persona all agree. It clears both when the hover ends or the view disappears. The code was lifted verbatim in behaviour from two identical inline copies that B2 kept in InlineText (MarkdownView.swift B2 :1158-1193) and ProseRunView (B2 :27-59). Both call sites now apply `.modifier(LinkHoverModifier(...))` (B3 MarkdownView.swift:1120, ProseRunView.swift:24). The header comment (:4-5) records why the cursor comes from here: LinkTextView keeps no tracking areas, because AppKit rebuilds them every scrolled frame.

feature_notes: Status A, but a pure extraction (refactor): the B2 hover handler existed twice, inline in InlineText.body (B2 MarkdownView.swift:1158-1193) and ProseRunView.body (B2 ProseRunView.swift:27-59). B3 deletes both copies and replaces them with `.modifier(LinkHoverModifier(linkView: linkBox, showsHand: $showsHand, hoveredHeadID: $hoveredHeadID, personas: hydraMentionPersonas, targets: targets))` at MarkdownView.swift:1120 and ProseRunView.swift:24 (git diff 1fbf81e6..HEAD). The sequence of conditions and effects is unchanged. The link check is `overLink != showsHand`, then push or pop. The head check requires `headMentionRect` to hit, `targets[name]` to exist, `target.url == url` and `personasByName[name]` to exist, and it shows the card only when `hoveredHeadID != target.threadID`. The else branch hides the card only when hoveredHeadID is not nil. `.ended` and onDisappear both pop the hand if it was showing, clear the head and hide the card.

Only the mechanics differ, and none of it is observable. B2's closures captured Binding values (`hand`, `hoveredHead`) and a `[weak linkBox]`. B3 uses @Binding properties and holds the WeakView box strongly. The box's own `value` stays weak, so the NSView is still not kept alive, as the :7 comment states. B2 computed personasByName once per InlineText body. B3 computes it once per modifier body. Both keep the first persona when names collide. `} else { if hoveredHead != nil` became `} else if hoveredHeadID != nil`, which is equivalent.

A related B3 change sits outside this file (owned by the MarkdownView.swift reader): InlineText now takes the LinkParagraphView path, and so gets this modifier, when `RichLink.containsLinks(in:streaming:)` is true, not when link hosts are non-empty. That means paragraphs whose only links are hostless local file paths now also get the pointing hand (MarkdownView.swift B3 :1095-1096, comment 'Local file links have no host, but still need the native link opener').

purpose: Declares LinkParagraphView, the NSViewRepresentable that renders a markdown paragraph containing links as a selectable, non-editable NSTextView (LinkTextView) so links show the native pointing hand and prose the I-beam, and its static attributed(source:pointSize:dimmed:streaming:mentions:targets:) builder that turns RichLink.prettyAttributed runs into an NSAttributedString with a per-size font cache (base, bold, font-manager italic, monospaced at max(9, pointSize - 1)), 14x14 favicon attachments from FaviconCache.cached(host:), dimmed labelColor at alpha 0.7 and Hydra head mentions (tinted dragon glyph at (pointSize * 1.25).rounded(), a space, the bold name in the persona colour, carrying the custom key "droppycode.hydraHead" rather than .link). LinkTextView owns its own NSTextStorage/NSLayoutManager/NSTextContainer, drops every tracking area and cursor rect, does its own link and head-mention hit testing, intercepts right-click/control-click to show LinkPopover and left-click on a head to call onOpenHead, measures height once per width and defers re-measurement during live resize. The file also declares MergeRequestTarget and its environment key, the hydraHead attribute key, and (new at B3) MarkdownLinkOpener, which opens scheme-less absolute-path links as local files, stripping a trailing :line suffix when only the file without it exists.

Only the last colon is examined, so "file.swift:12:5" is not stripped; ":0" and negative numbers are not stripped; a path that exists as given is opened as is.

purpose: Declares LinkPopover, the single shared transient NSPopover that a right-click or control-click on a chat link opens in place of the system text menu, anchored below the link's own glyph rect (preferredEdge .minY in the flipped text view), measured from an NSHostingView with a 220x110 fallback, and closed by Escape through a local keyDown monitor on key code 53 that is removed on close and in popoverDidClose. Its private SwiftUI content, LinkPopoverContent, is a 220-point-wide, 6-point-padded column of house PopoverItem rows: an optional "Merge <label>" row (semibold "Merge", the forge favicon or the arrow.triangle.merge symbol) plus a divider when the chat supplied a MergeRequestTarget, then "Open Link" (safari symbol) and "Copy Link" (link symbol, writes url.absoluteString to the general pasteboard). At B3 the Open Link row goes through MarkdownLinkOpener.open(url), so a local absolute-path link opens the file rather than being handed to NSWorkspace as-is.

purpose: Resolves bare YouTube links in chat to the video's own title so a link reads as the title instead of "youtube.com/watch". It extracts a video id from the known YouTube host and path forms, fetches the title once per id from YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint (no key), and keeps answers in a Mutex-guarded store that can be read off the main actor when RichLink builds a paragraph for the cache. Failed or empty answers are remembered as claimed so the same video is never asked twice.

feature_notes: videoID: host lowercased; a leading "www." is stripped; path split on "/" (empty segments dropped). Host "youtu.be": first path segment. Hosts "youtube.com", "m.youtube.com", "music.youtube.com", "youtube-nocookie.com": if segments.count >= 2 and segments[0] is one of "shorts", "embed", "live", "v", the second segment; otherwise the first query item named "v". Any other host: nil. No host: nil. When the path-form condition holds, the function returns `checked(segments[1])` (line 23) with no fallback to the "v" query item, so "youtube.com/embed/x?v=abcdefghijk" gives nil. The segment names (`["shorts", "embed", "live", "v"].contains(segments[0])`) and the query name (`$0.name == "v"`) are case-sensitive; only the host is lowercased (line 14). `checked` applies on all three paths (lines 20, 23, 27).
checked(): id must have count >= 8 and every character a letter, number, "-" or "_"; otherwise nil (rejects bare /watch and playlist links).
cached(for:) returns Store.shared.title(id) or nil if the URL is not a video link.

title(forVideo:): returns a known title immediately; if claim(id) fails (already claimed, in flight or answered-with-none) returns nil; otherwise fetches. Any failure (bad URL, thrown error, status != 200, decode failure) calls finish(id, title: nil) and returns nil. Success: title = payload.title.trimmed; empty -> finish(nil) and nil; else stored and returned.
oembedURL: base "https://www.youtube.com/oembed" with query items url = "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>" and format = "json" (percent-encoded by URLComponents).
Store.finish: when a title is given and titles.count >= 400, removeAll(keepingCapacity: true) first, then stores; always inserts id into claimed. claim returns claimed.insert(id).inserted.
Comment: a streaming row restarts its task on every token, and a claimed id counts as answered so the same video is asked once.

B1->B2: added `import Synchronization`; Store changed from `@unchecked Sendable` with an NSLock and two stored vars (lock/defer pattern) to `Sendable` with `Mutex(State())` holding titles and claimed, each method using state.withLock; finish now does the title insert and claimed insert inside one lock (previously also one locked region via defer). payload.title.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) became payload.title.trimmed (same semantics). Line count stays 112; observable behaviour (400 cap, claim-once, oEmbed URL) unchanged.
unresolved_questions: No timeout is set beyond URLSession.shared defaults; the Windows port must decide an equivalent default.

The 400-entry cap clears all titles but not claimed ids, so an evicted id will never be re-fetched in that process (cached(for:) then returns nil and the host-and-path form shows); this appears intentional per the comments but is not stated explicitly.

purpose: Defines the block-level Markdown model (headings, paragraphs, fenced code, ordered/unordered/task lists, nested quotes, pipe tables, rules) and a hand-written line-based parser for agent output; inline styling is left to AttributedString. It supports incremental re-parsing for streaming replies: a Parse records how many leading blocks are stable and the UTF-8 offset to restart from, so a text that only grew by appending reuses those blocks and parses just the tail. Recursion for quotes and list children is capped at depth 8.

feature_notes: Line splitting: splits UTF-8 on 0x0A keeping empty pieces, drops one trailing 0x0D per line, records each line's UTF-8 start offset.

Stability: after parsing, stable = index of the last top-level block whose start line <= lines.count - 3 (i.e. at least two lines above the last line); restart = UTF-8 offset of that block's start line. If none, stable = 0, restart = 0. Blocks before index `stable` are reusable.

parse(_:extending:): reuses only when previous exists, previous.parse.stable > 0, the new text is strictly longer in UTF-8 and starts with the previous text's UTF-8; then parses from byte offset restart and returns previous.blocks[..<stable] + tail.blocks, stable = previous.stable + tail.stable, restart = restart + tail.restart. Otherwise a full parse.

Main loop precedence per non-blank line (trimmed with the fast trimmed()): blank flushes paragraph; fence (``` or ~~~ prefix, marker = the full run of that character) -> code block until a line whose trimmed form hasPrefix(fence) and consists only of the fence character (unterminated fence runs to end); language = text after the fence trimmed of whitespace, nil if empty; code lines kept untrimmed and joined with \n.

Heading: 1 to 6 leading '#' followed by end of line or a space; content = drop leading '#', trim whitespace, then trim characters '#' and ' ' from both ends (line 125 `content.trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "# "))`). Outcomes: a trailing '#' that belongs to the text is lost ("# Learn C#" gives text "Learn C"); a bare "#" gives .heading(level: 1, text: ""); headingLevel (line 311) accepts only `rest.isEmpty || rest.hasPrefix(" ")`, so "#\tTitle" (tab after the hashes) and "#hashtag" are not headings.

Rule: first byte '-' (0x2D), '*' (0x2A) or '_' (0x5F); every byte is that one or a space (0x20); count >= 3. In the main loop (parse) it is checked before lists, so a top-level "- - -" is a rule. parseList never calls isRule: inside an unordered list, "- - -" at indent <= first.indent matches listMarker and starts a new item with text "- -" ("* * *" likewise gives "* *"); inside an ordered list the unordered marker fails `guard marker.ordered == first.ordered else { break }`, the list ends and the main loop makes the line a rule; indented deeper than the first marker it goes to childLines and becomes a .rule child when the children are parsed. A spaceless "---"/"***"/"___" is not a list marker, so right after a list item with no child lines it is taken as a lazy continuation line and appended to the item text (line 253-254), not a rule.
Quote: trimmed line starts with '>' and depth < 8; consumes consecutive '>' lines, drops the '>' and one following space, parses the inner lines recursively at depth + 1. No lazy continuation.

Table: needs a following line, the current trimmed line contains '|', and the next line is a delimiter (contains '-' and only characters '|', ':', '-', ' '). Header from tableCells; rows continue while trimmed line is non-empty and contains '|'. tableCells strips one leading and one trailing '|', splits on '|' keeping empties, trims whitespace per cell. Column alignment markers are not recorded. isTableDelimiter (lines 325-329) requires only `trimmed.contains("-")` and every character in "|:- ", so a pipe-less "---" or "- - -" counts as a delimiter: a line containing '|' followed by "---" becomes a table header (with no rows or with the following '|' lines as rows), not a paragraph followed by a rule, whenever that '|' line was not already taken by the earlier fence, heading, rule or quote checks. The table check (line 154) runs before the list check (line 170), so "- a | b" followed by "---" is a table with header ["- a", "b"]. Rows (lines 160-165) are `tableCells(candidate)` as split and are not padded or truncated to the header's cell count; the delimiter line's cells are never counted.
List start: depth < 8 and listMarker(line) != nil and (paragraph empty, or unordered, or ordered with start == 1), so an ordered item other than 1 cannot interrupt a paragraph.

listMarker: indent = spaces count 1, tab counts 4; then `let body = line.dropFirst(indent)` (line 274) drops that many Characters, so each leading tab over-drops 3 characters: for "\t- item" indentation is 4, dropFirst(4) removes "\t- i" leaving "tem", and listMarker returns nil, so tab-indented bullets are never list markers (a top-level one is paragraph text). Inside parseList, "- parent\n\t- child" takes the indented branch (indentation 4 > 0) and, with no child lines yet and no marker, appends the trimmed text "- child" to the parent item's text instead of creating a nested list (with child lines already present it would append `line.dropFirst(min(4, contentOffset 2))` = " child" to childLines). A port must reproduce this tab-weighted character drop.unordered markers '-', '*', '+' must be followed by space or tab, content after skipping spaces/tabs, contentOffset = indent + 2, start 1. Ordered: 1 to 9 digits, then '.' or ')', then a space or end of line; content after skipping spaces; start = Int(digits) ?? 1; contentOffset = indent + digits.count + 2.

parseList: blank line continues the list if the next line is indented more than the first marker and non-blank (adds an empty child line), or if the next line is a marker with the same indent and same ordered flag (loose list); else ends. A marker with indent <= first indent starts a new item only if its ordered flag matches, else ends the list. Lines indented more than the first marker: if no child lines yet, not a marker and not a fence, the trimmed line is appended to the item text; otherwise the line (dropping min(indentation, contentOffset) characters) goes to child lines. Unindented lazy continuation lines are appended to the item text when no child lines yet and the line is not a heading, fence or quote; otherwise the list ends.
Task items: item text trimmed of whitespace; prefix "[ ] " -> checked false; lowercased prefix "[x] " -> checked true; the 4 characters are removed. Children are parsed recursively at depth + 1.
parseList fallback: if the start line has no marker, returns .paragraph(line) and start + 1.
trimmed(line) fast path: returns the line unchanged when its first and last UTF-8 bytes are both in 0x21...0x7E; otherwise trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).

Paragraph: consecutive non-block lines are stored untrimmed (line 180 `paragraph.append(line)`, not `trimmed`), joined with \n and only the joined text is trimmed of whitespace and newlines at its two ends (line 87 `.trimmed`), so continuation lines keep their leading indentation (and inner lines their trailing spaces) inside the .paragraph string;empty results are dropped; paragraph start line recorded for stability.

B1->B2: one line changed in flushParagraph: paragraph.joined(separator: "\n").trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) became .trimmed, the project extension that is defined as the same call, so parsing behaviour is unchanged.
unresolved_questions: Setext headings, indented code blocks, HTML blocks and lazy quote continuation are not supported by this parser; a port must reproduce these omissions rather than use a CommonMark library to keep parity.
In parseList the restart offset semantics for nested list children are not tracked (only top-level blockLines), which is by design but worth mirroring exactly.

purpose: MarkdownView.swift is the chat's markdown renderer and most of its inline machinery. MarkdownView parses a message into blocks through a bounded cache (800 finished texts) and 48 streaming slots that re-parse only the block being extended, warms finished messages off the main thread, and draws a finished reply as ProseRunView runs plus standalone blocks and a streaming reply block by block with the settled/streaming flags. MarkdownBlockView draws each block: headings, paragraphs routed between the native link paragraph and veiled text by links, head mentions, list depth and streaming, the lead's `hydra` delegation card, code, list markers, quotes, tables and rules. RichLink builds pretty link titles, bare-domain autolinks and favicon/video asset keys. FaviconCache fetches /favicon.ico only for public hosts and strips white plates. InlineText picks the AppKit link paragraph or a veiled Text. CodeBlock collapses at 120 lines, TableBlock at 30 rows, and CopyButton copies through ProseReflow. At B3 the file stops naming the App-layer HydraDelegationBlock. The card now comes through the MarkdownDelegationCard.render hook that AppDelegate sets at launch. Mention scanning moves to MentionScanner and link hover moves to LinkHoverModifier. InlineText now sends any link, including a host-less local file link, to the native paragraph, and RichLink's streaming slots rise from 4 to 48.

Its one generic function matches(in:candidates:name:) walks the text Character by Character, tries the candidates longest name first (sorted by name(x).count descending, :8), accepts a hit only when the name is a prefix of the remaining text (:15) and the Character before it and the Character after it are each absent or neither isLetter nor isNumber (:17-20), records (range, value) and jumps past the match (:23-26), otherwise advances one Character (:28). The doc comments state the contract: 'The word-bounded mention scan shared by every prose path' (:3) and 'Longest name first, so 'Hank 2' beats 'Hank'; a name inside a longer word or beside a digit doesn't count' (:5-6).

It is a pure extraction: the B3 callers are LinkParagraphView.swift:197 (`for match in MentionScanner.matches(in: string, candidates: mentions, name: \.name)`), MarkdownView.swift:419 (`MentionScanner.matches(in: text, candidates: names, name: { $0 }).map(\.range)`) and MarkdownView.swift:425 (`MentionScanner.matches(in: chars, candidates: hydraMentionPersonas, name: \.name)`), each replacing its own inline loop from B2.

Behaviour is unchanged versus all three B2 copies: same comparator (name count descending) on the same input order, same prefix test, same before/after `!c.isLetter && !c.isNumber` boundary rule, same advance-past-match. The one textual difference, the B2 LinkParagraphView copy computing `after` with `string.index(i, offsetBy: persona.name.count)` without limitedBy, is unobservable because hasPrefix already guarantees the name's characters exist. `for ... where hasPrefix` in B2 became `guard hasPrefix else { continue }` in B3, which is equivalent.

Consequence for the specification: the longest-first word-bounded matching that PR-THEME-143 and UI-THEME-046 attribute to LinkParagraphView.swift:179-244 now lives in MentionScanner.swift:5-32; the rule itself is identical, so only the citations move.

Latent edge case present in B2 and kept in B3: an empty candidate name would hit with a zero-length range when the boundary tests pass, `i = end` would not advance, and the while loop would never end. Real candidates are roster persona names (never empty), so this is not reachable in the source's own use.
unresolved_questions: The existing C# port implements this scan twice, and the two copies disagree: MarkdownBlockView.MentionRanges (src/Marrow.UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.cs:687-714) orders by UTF-16 Length and tests char.IsLetter/char.IsDigit per UTF-16 code unit (the code notes this as an unverified ENGINEERING DECISION under OD-0001), while LinkParagraphView.AppendProse (src/Marrow.UI/Markdown/LinkParagraphView.cs:423-455) is grapheme-aware through SwiftString.Count/Characters and SwiftCharacter.IsLetter/IsNumber. B3's single shared scanner means both paths must behave identically, so the port should settle on one grapheme-correct implementation. Whether char.IsDigit versus Swift Character.isNumber (broader: Unicode Numeric_Type, for example superscripts and vulgar fractions) is observable depends on persona names and the adjacent text, and is not settled by the source.

Both C# copies skip empty names (`name.Length == 0 continue`), where the Swift source would loop forever on an empty candidate. Unreachable with roster names, but it is a difference from the source that the port should record rather than leave implicit.

purpose: Declares ProseRunView, the SwiftUI view a finished reply uses to render a run of consecutive paragraphs, headings, lists and quotes as one selectable LinkTextView (so selection and links span the whole run), reading point size, dimming, Hydra mention personas and targets and openURL from the environment, rounding the size to half points ((pointSize * 2).rounded() / 2), fetching link assets for the run's joined sources in a task keyed by RichLink.linkAssetKey, and (at B3) attaching the shared LinkHoverModifier for the pointing hand and the Hydra head hover card. Its ProseRunRepresentable builds one NSAttributedString from the blocks, reusing LinkParagraphView.attributed for each line: paragraphs with indent and paragraphSpacing, headings at 1.35/1.2/1.08 times the size with non-bold non-mono runs set semibold and spacing before 6 or 2, list items with "☑"/"☐", "n." or "•"/"◦" markers and a tab stop at indent + 18, quotes at indent + 14 forced dimmed, code/table/rule dropped, and a newline between blocks. It shares LinkParagraphView.Coordinator for its rebuild check and keeps onOpenHead and mergeTarget fresh on every update.

The engines differ: B1 matched per UTF-16 unit, B2's Swift Regex literals match per Character (grapheme cluster) by default, so `\S`, `\s`, `[^\[\]]` and `[^<>\s]` classify whole grapheme clusters in B2. purpose: Implements the fade-in of streamed assistant text: every flush is laid out immediately and only a cosmetic opacity veil over the newly arrived characters dissolves, so nothing moves or resizes while a reply streams. The file holds the platform-neutral chunk/cadence model (StreamVeil), a shared display-link frame clock for SwiftUI consumers (VeilClock), the SwiftUI consumer VeiledText (which overwrites the foreground colour of arriving runs of an AttributedString with `base.opacity(span.alpha)`, base being Color.primary or Color.primary.opacity(0.7) when dimmed, so the veil alpha multiplies the base's opacity; it can also interleave non-veiled fixed Text segments such as head-name decorations), the markdownVeiled environment flag, and the AppKit consumer LinkTextVeil that paints the same alphas as NSLayoutManager temporary foreground-colour attributes on an NSTextView, each run's colour given the span alpha as an ABSOLUTE alpha via NSColor.withAlphaComponent (not multiplied into the run's own alpha). Text already on screen when a veil first attaches is adopted as a baseline and never fades; a non-append rewrite keeps fades in the common prefix and re-veils only the changed tail.

ui_elements: No controls or label strings; the file only changes the paint opacity of streamed text.

Fade duration per chunk: clamp(cadence * 3, 0.12 s, 0.40 s), where cadence is an EMA (0.7 old + 0.3 new) of gaps between appends, gap capped at 1.0 s, seed 0.16 s (so the first append after attach uses duration clamp(0.48,0.12,0.40) = 0.40 s when no prior append; with a previous append the EMA updates first).
Easing: alpha (text opacity) = 1 - (1 - progress)^1.6, progress = clamp(elapsed * boost / duration, 0, 1).
Backlog speed-up: boost = 1 + 0.3 * max(0, activeChunks - 2), i.e. 1.0 for up to 2 chunks, 1.3 for 3, 1.6 for 4.

SwiftUI colour: arriving runs get `styled[lower..<upper].foregroundColor = base.opacity(span.alpha)` (line 319) with `let base = dimmed ? Color.primary.opacity(0.7) : Color.primary` (line 311). This REPLACES any existing per-run foreground colour in the veiled range for SwiftUI prose. SwiftUI Color.opacity applied to an already-translucent colour MULTIPLIES: a dimmed veiled run's effective opacity is 0.7 * alpha (at most 0.7), a non-dimmed one is alpha. A port must keep the 0.7 factor on this path (rgba(primary, 0.7*alpha) when dimmed), unlike the AppKit path below.

AppKit colour: for each attribute run in the span, `let color: NSColor = attributes[.link] != nil ? accent : (attributes[.foregroundColor] as? NSColor ?? .labelColor)` then `layout.addTemporaryAttribute(.foregroundColor, value: color.withAlphaComponent(span.alpha), forCharacterRange: runRange)` (lines 423-426). NSColor.withAlphaComponent SETS an absolute alpha and discards the run's own alpha, so the source comment at line 420 ("Each run keeps its own colour, only thinner") holds for the hue only. At B2 a dimmed AppKit paragraph's runs carry `NSColor.labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.7)` (LinkParagraphView.swift line 121, applied as .foregroundColor at lines 143/152): while fading those runs ramp from alpha 0 up toward 1.0 (not 0.7), and when settle/clear removes the temporary attribute they drop back to the storage's 0.7. A port must use rgba(runRGB, alpha), not rgba(runRGB, runAlpha*alpha), to match upstream; the SwiftUI and AppKit paths therefore differ for dimmed text.
Frame rate: VeilClock prefers 30 fps (range 24 to 60); LinkTextVeil's display link has no preferred range set.
Spans with alpha >= 1 are skipped (no attribute written).
feature_notes: advance(text, at:): converts text to [Character]. If previous is nil (first call after attach or after reset) it stores the text as baseline and returns WITHOUT pruning or fading. If text is unchanged it only prunes (idempotent). Otherwise: prefix = common prefix length; every chunk is clipped to upperBound min(upper, prefix) and dropped entirely if the clipped upper <= lowerBound (comment: a range with upper below lower traps, e.g. a delegation block leaving the reply); if the new text is longer than prefix, cadence is updated from the gap since lastAppend (gap capped at gapCeiling 1.0 s; cadence = cadence*0.7 + gap*0.3) only when lastAppend exists, lastAppend = now, and a Chunk(range: prefix..<count, started: now, duration: min(max(cadence*3, 0.12), 0.40)) is appended; previous = characters; then prune.
A pure deletion/rewrite that is not longer than the common prefix clips chunks but adds no new chunk and does not touch cadence or lastAppend.
prune(at:) removes chunks with (now - started) * boost >= duration, where boost is computed from the chunk count BEFORE removal.
spans(at:) prunes first, then computes boost from the remaining chunk count and returns one Span per chunk with alpha = 1 - pow(1 - progress, 1.6).
isFading(at:) prunes and returns !chunks.isEmpty. step(text, active:, at:) calls advance only when active (text is an autoclosure, so it is not evaluated when inactive) and returns isFading.

settlesAt = max over chunks of started + duration / boost, with `let boost = Self.boost(chunks.count)` (lines 110-113) computed from the CURRENT chunk count. Because boost falls as older chunks prune (prune and spans recompute it from the smaller count), the remaining chunks then progress more slowly, so settlesAt can be earlier than the true settle time of the last chunk. Upstream recovers through re-arming: VeilClock.tick sets `now = .now` (line 188), and once `now >= deadline` invalidates the link and sets `link = nil` and `deadline = nil` (lines 189-192); the change to the observed `now` re-renders every VeiledText that read it, and a still-fading one calls fadingText(), which calls `clock.run(until: settlesAt)` again (line 286); `guard link == nil` (line 173) now passes, so a new link is created. Also, since fadingText runs on every tick while fading, the deadline is re-extended each frame via `deadline = max(deadline ?? date, date)` (line 172). A port must keep this re-arm (or re-arm its clock on every fading render); otherwise the last chunk of a backed-up stream freezes mid-fade.
reset() sets previous = nil, chunks = [], lastAppend = nil, cadence = 0.16.

markdownVeiled environment flag defaults to false; doc says it is set once per message on every block, so a paragraph that stops being the last block keeps dissolving instead of snapping. Callers set it to isStreaming (MarkdownView.swift lines 84, 100).

VeilClock.run(until:): deadline = max(existing deadline ?? date, date); if a link already exists or NSScreen.main is nil it returns without creating a link (deadline still extended). tick(): returns immediately while ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling (holds last frame, ramp resumes after scroll); otherwise now = .now, and if deadline is set and now >= deadline, invalidates link and clears link and deadline.
VeilClock design note: the veiled Text is a bare Text (no TimelineView wrapper) so list markers keep first-baseline alignment mid-stream; only paragraphs that read clock.now re-render per tick.
VeiledText.body: if veil.step(source.characters, active: veiled, at: .now) then fadingText() else settledText(). Both return Text.

fadingText(): starts/extends the shared clock to veil.settlesAt, reads clock.now for dependency tracking (`_ = clock.now`), and paints `text(at: .now)` at the real Date.now (not clock.now) so the first frame after a flush is never stale. Timing detail: body calls `veil.step(source.characters, active: veiled, at: .now)` (line 274) and fadingText then calls `text(at: .now)` (line 288), two SEPARATE Date.now reads; text(at:) calls veil.spans(at: now), which prunes again at the second timestamp, so VeiledText can take the fading branch yet render with fewer spans (possibly none) than step saw. settlesAt at line 286 is read before that second prune. LinkTextVeil.update, by contrast, takes `let now = Date.now` once (line 355) and uses it for both step and paint.

settledText(): if !veiled resets the veil (a settled paragraph keeps no copy of its text; while still streaming the baseline stays so a quiet beat between flushes does not make the next flush arrive unveiled). With segments, concatenates starting from Text(verbatim: ""): fixed segments as their Text, prose as Text(a), each via Text("\(out)\(x)") interpolation. Without segments returns source.text (Text(attributed) or Text(verbatim: string)).

text(at:): copies source.styled (plain source becomes AttributedString(string) only here), and for each span with alpha < 1 clamps range to 0..<count, skips empty, and sets foregroundColor = base.opacity(alpha) over those characters. With segments, walks segments: fixed Text appended unchanged (never veiled); each prose segment slices styled from cursor to the character offset proseEnds[prose] of the joined string and appends Text(AttributedString(slice)). Without segments returns Text(styled).

init(segments:) builds the joined AttributedString from prose segments only and records proseEnds as joined.characters.count after each append, so offsets follow the JOINED string's grapheme clustering (a combining mark or ZWJ emoji spanning a join counts once; using per-run counts would trap past endIndex).

Segment doc: fixed runs are head-name glyph + coloured name interleaved with veiled prose; every head named anywhere in a paragraph renders decorated inline in the same flowing Text, and only prose runs veil.
Source doc: code comes as a plain String and is made attributed only for veiled frames, so a finished dump costs a hover nothing new.

LinkTextVeil.update(view, active:): now = Date.now; if veil.step(view.string, active:, at: now) is true, paint, create a display link from the view if none (added to .main, .common), and set tickTarget = view; otherwise settle(view, keepText: active).
LinkTextVeil.detach(view): settle(view, keepText: false) (view leaving its window).

LinkTextVeil.tick(): returns while scrolling; if tickTarget was released, invalidates and nils the link; else if still fading paints, otherwise settle(view, keepText: true) (keeps the baseline text because the tick does not know whether the stream ended).
settle: invalidate link, clear temporary colours, reset veil unless keepText.
clear: no-op if painted.length == 0 or no layoutManager; intersects painted with 0..<textStorage.length, removes temporary .foregroundColor over that range if non-empty, sets painted to empty.

paint: requires layoutManager and textStorage; clears first; for each span with alpha < 1, clamps to 0..<string.count (Swift Characters), converts to String.Index then NSRange(lower..<upper, in: string), enumerates storage attributes in that NSRange and adds a temporary .foregroundColor per run (link -> Chrome.accentNSColor, else existing .foregroundColor as? NSColor ?? .labelColor) set to `color.withAlphaComponent(span.alpha)`, i.e. the span alpha REPLACES the run colour's own alpha (see ui_elements); painted grows as the union of all painted ranges.
Header doc cites the origin: zeron's crates/ui/src/markdown/veil.rs, itself a port of mugen-markdown's FadePainter; only opacity changes, every consumer keeps its layout byte for byte.

purpose: A tiny additive-synthesis engine that renders struck-bell tones to a complete 16-bit mono PCM WAV byte buffer in memory, including hand-written RIFF header emission, so the app's chimes are numbers in source rather than bundled audio assets.
key_symbols: struct ToneSynth.Note { var frequency: Double; var onset: Double; var level: Double }
struct ToneSynth.Partial { var multiple: Double; var level: Double; var decay: Double }
static func wave(notes: [Note], partials: [Partial], duration: Double) -> Data
local generic func append<Value: FixedWidthInteger>(_ value: Value) inside wave
calls_into: cos, sin, exp, abs from the C math library
state_owned: No instance state; only the private static constants sampleRate, attack, release. wave() allocates a local [Double] sample buffer of Int(sampleRate * duration) elements.
side_effects: Pure computation - allocates and returns Data; no I/O, no timers, no notifications
platform_assumptions: Foundation only (import Foundation); no AppKit dependency, so the synthesis itself is portable
Assumes the consumer (NSSound on macOS) can play a raw RIFF/WAVE buffer from memory
Little-endian byte order is written explicitly via .littleEndian, so it is not host-endianness dependent
feature_notes: Sample rate 44_100.0 Hz, mono, 16-bit signed PCM.
Sample count = Int(sampleRate * duration).
Attack: raised-cosine onset of 0.006 s - for time < attack the envelope is 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(.pi * time / attack), else 1. 'quick enough to feel struck, with no click.'
Release: final 0.08 s linear fade, applied as samples[index] *= Double(count - index) / Double(fade) over indices (count - fade)..<count.

Per-note synthesis: start index = Int(note.onset * sampleRate); time = Double(index - start) / sampleRate; tone = sum over partials of partial.level * exp(-time / partial.decay) * sin(2 * .pi * note.frequency * partial.multiple * time); accumulated as samples[index] += note.level * onset * tone.
Partial.decay is documented as 'the seconds it takes to fall by about two thirds' (an exp(-t/decay) time constant).
Normalization: peak = max abs sample; scale = peak > 0 ? 0.9 / peak : 0 - every rendered tone is normalized to 0.9 full scale.

WAV header written by hand, in order: ASCII 'RIFF'; UInt32(36 + count * 2); 'WAVE'; 'fmt '; UInt32(16); UInt16(1) // PCM; UInt16(1) // mono; UInt32(sampleRate); UInt32(sampleRate) * 2 // bytes per second; UInt16(2) // bytes per frame; UInt16(16) // bits per sample; 'data'; UInt32(count * 2); then Int16 samples.
Data is preallocated with capacity 44 + count * 2 (44-byte canonical WAV header).
Sample conversion: Int16((sample * scale * Double(Int16.max)).rounded()).
Shipped and reachable: the only callers are FinishChime and SettleChime in this same bundle.
unresolved_questions: A note whose onset is at or beyond duration would make start >= count and the range start..<count invalid (a crash); no guard exists. Both shipped callers use onsets (0.14 s, 0.075 s) far below their durations, so this is unreachable in practice but unverified as intentional.

Color(hex:): trims whitespace/newlines via .trimmed, drops one leading '#', scans with Scanner.scanHexInt64 into a UInt64 starting at 0; red = (value >> 16) & 0xFF, green = (value >> 8) & 0xFF, blue = value & 0xFF, each divided by 255, opacity 1, color space .sRGB. Error path: the Bool result of scanHexInt64 is ignored and value starts at 0 (line 241 `var value: UInt64 = 0`). Foundation scanHexInt64 scans hex digits up to the first non-hex character and keeps that prefix, so only a string whose first character is not a hex digit (or an empty string) yields 0 (black); "12GG34" gives 0x12 (red 0, green 0, blue 0x12). scanHexInt64 also accepts an optional "0x"/"0X" prefix, and on overflow (more than 16 hex digits) stores UInt64.max, giving white (FFFFFF). A port must reproduce this prefix parse; no shipped palette string exercises it (all are 6-digit literals); an 8-digit string uses only the low 24 bits (last six hex digits); 3-digit forms are not expanded ('FFF' gives red 0, green 0x0F, blue 0xFF).

side_effects: Build steps: `brew install xcodegen`, `xcodegen generate`, `open DroppyCode.xcodeproj`.
scripts/release.sh archives an Apple silicon build, signs it with Developer ID, notarizes and staples both the app and a disk image, and checks Gatekeeper; the disk image lands in build.noindex/.
scripts/package_dmg.sh gives the disk image a styled drag-to-Applications window; its background and baked window layout live in release/dmg and the volume icon is the app's own.
