platform_assumptions: 'A native macOS app for your coding agents. Written entirely in Swift and SwiftUI with Liquid Glass, for Macs with Apple silicon on macOS 26 and later.'
Requirements: a Mac with Apple silicon running macOS 26 or later; at least one provider installed and signed in; Git, plus `gh` or `glab` for pull requests.
Homebrew for xcodegen, an Xcode project, and Swift Package Manager fetching SwiftTerm (Xcode asks once to trust its build plugin).
Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling and Gatekeeper checks are Apple-only release steps; build.noindex/ is a Spotlight-skipped folder name.
persisted_fields: `droppy-code.json` is named as the per-project file carrying project scripts.
Native-API providers are keyed by environment variables: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (DeepSeek), `ZAI_API_KEY` (Z.ai), `MODEL_API_KEY` (Meta, at `api.meta.ai/v1`, Muse Spark).
ui_elements: Projects and threads in a glass sidebar with search, pinning, settling (or archiving), and drag to resize; a settled thread drops to the bottom, small and grey, until you reopen it.
Streaming conversations with reasoning, tool calls, plans, to-do lists and errors; approvals and questions from the agent answered inline.
Plan mode, model and reasoning selection, and four permission modes per thread.
Twenty-six tinted-glass themes, from System to Catppuccin, Dracula, Claude and Codex.
A diff for every turn captured as hidden git checkpoints, with revert; an embedded terminal per thread plus project scripts from droppy-code.json; new threads in their own git worktree.
Commit, push and pull requests with generated commit messages and thread titles; a command palette, keyboard shortcuts and notifications when work finishes.
A welcome tour on first launch, six pages of real captures; the Help menu opens it again.

The usage ring beside the send button opens a popover with the context window, each plan's rolling limits and resets (Codex, Claude, Antigravity, Copilot, Command Code and Z.ai) and the credit left on DeepSeek and Command Code keys; a pair across two providers stacks the lead's over the heads'. A switch in General settings keeps the same in a floating panel beside the chat, and Settings > Providers shows every signed-in account at once. A Codex account that has banked resets can spend one from the same popover to clear its active windows.
feature_notes: Provider table exactly as written: Codex -> `codex` -> app-server JSON-RPC; Claude -> `claude` -> stream-json with permission prompts; Cursor -> `cursor-agent` -> Agent Client Protocol; OpenCode -> `opencode` -> Agent Client Protocol; Grok -> `grok` -> Agent Client Protocol; Antigravity -> `agy` -> stream-json headless; Copilot -> `copilot` -> headless JSON-RPC (the Copilot SDK protocol); Command Code -> `cmd` -> headless print mode (NDJSON events), one run per turn, with a session mod for approvals; Pi -> `pi` -> RPC mode (JSONL over stdio), one process per thread, with a gate extension for approvals; DeepSeek -> `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` -> native API (OpenAI-compatible); Z.ai -> `ZAI_API_KEY` -> native API (OpenAI-compatible, GLM Coding Plan); Meta -> `MODEL_API_KEY` -> native API at `api.meta.ai/v1` (Muse Spark).

Hydra: one chat, many heads. Switch it on and the agent leads a team of helper agents on big jobs: it writes the briefs, sends the heads out in parallel, each in its own copy of the project, and their work lands back in your checkout as one merge. Each head has a floating panel, and a pair sets the lead's model and the heads' model; a pair can cross providers, a strong lead on one and quick heads on another, with one effort slider fused for both.
Explicit non-goals, verbatim: 'Remote access, mobile apps, cloud sync, telemetry and a web client are left out on purpose.'
Login examples given: `codex login`, `claude auth login`, `copilot login`, `cmd login` or `pi` (then `/login`).
SwiftTerm is stated as the only dependency, fetched by Swift Package Manager.

Layout table: DroppyCode/Core holds models and pure support - projects and threads, timelines, providers (`ProviderKind` lives here), Hydra, shortcuts, process I/O, JSON-RPC and the login shell - and depends on nothing else in the app. DroppyCode/Services holds Git, worktrees and diff parsing, the on-disk store, and the Codex, Claude, ACP, Antigravity, Copilot, Command Code, Pi, DeepSeek, Meta and Z.ai adapters behind one event model; depends on Core. DroppyCode/UI holds window chrome, common controls, Markdown rendering, the theme and the chimes; depends on Core only. DroppyCode/App holds the app entry, commands and settings, the project library, the per-thread runtime, windows, captures and every feature view: sidebar, chat, composer, changes, terminal, palette, settings, usage and the tour. `website` is the marketing site, a static page published by Netlify via netlify.toml.

feature_notes: Guidance is ON by default; turning the switch off does not merely omit the block, it sends a matching 'off' block that 'tells the model to disregard the earlier app-provided guidance and to keep following user requests and project requirements'

The guidance asks for: the shortest complete answer, leading with the result, skipping filler and hype, comments only where they explain a non-obvious reason, focused edits instead of unrelated cleanup, product-fitting UI structure, and reusing evidence rather than re-reading it
Delivery timing: 'The setting takes effect on the next message.' A message already in flight is not changed; toggling does not rewrite the current conversation or thread history

Delivery per provider class: providers with system-instruction support receive it when their session starts or resumes; other providers receive it with the first ordinary message of a session and again after explicit compaction; slash commands defer delivery until that ordinary message; automatic history changes inside those providers are not observable by the app
Explicit non-promise: 'Nothing is promised about token savings.' No fixed saving is guaranteed and no such claim is made in the UI

Coverage: the block is attached to the provider request so it reaches every provider Droppy Code runs; Hydra heads are covered because the block itself asks that the guidance apply to delegated work, with the intent that a head answers under the same policy as its lead

Attribution: upstream inspiration is miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop at revision 743735248fbaefd76bb56619615687dfa8b3bc1e, MIT licensed, copyright 2026 Miqdad Badjuber; the upstream LICENSE applies to that work

feature_notes: P0: three unresolved three-way merge hunks sat in ChatView.swift at old lines 160, 206 and 247, left when a head's landing (Git.apply with --3way) could not settle the panel refactor; the 'ours' side referenced origin, panelDrag and layout.panelHeight, none of which exist any more; the 'theirs' side is the PlacedPanel call; fixed by taking the PlacedPanel version

H1 fixed (P0): auto-merge committed every touched path as-is; now it scans the team's files for conflict-marker lines off the main actor and, finding any, leaves a Hydra note naming them instead of merging

H2 (P1): a head's patch lands the moment the head finishes even while the lead is mid-turn; recommendation is to hold a landing whose paths intersect the lead's touchedPaths until phase == .idle and land the rest at once
H3 (P1): after a conflicted landing the only signs are the panel row and a line in the report; add a warning Notice row naming the files and a count on the Hydra button badge

H4 (P2): finishHydraHead releases the head's worktree via releaseHydraCopy before the report is relayed with copyPath, so a stopped or failed head's report points at a just-deleted folder when auto-clear is on
H5 (P2): DiffParser.parse(patch) runs on the main actor inside applyHydraHead and a --binary patch can be large
H6 fixed (P1): the Hydra charge ring and glow now move only while a head is working; otherwise the ring stands still, and reduced motion keeps it still too
H7 (P2): the Hydra panel is a glass surface over a streaming transcript showing a second streaming transcript; swap the glass for the HydraPanelGhost scrim while either streams
H9 (P3): hydraSpawnCount is never reset for a chat, so a long-lived lead's heads drift into second-round names

C1 (P1): the timeline window is a fixed-length suffix, hidden = blocks.count - visibleCount at line 90; sending appends two blocks (the prompt and the working line) and evicts the two oldest rows in the same pass while the bottom anchor tries to hold; track hiddenCount instead while a turn runs

C2 (P1): the turn fold swaps N identities for one 'turn-<uuid>' block at line 818, dropping every measured height at once; armBlankWatch / repairLayout / stackGeneration exist to cover the aftermath; give the running turn the same block id so the fold becomes an in-place content change
C3 (P2): startTurn runs isRepository and captureCheckpoint (four git processes) before ensureSession and send; run the checkpoint with async let so a cold session start of 1-3 s overlaps the snapshot
C4 (P1): finishTurn parses the turn's patch and the provider diff twice on the main actor; settleCommand parses every command's patch in a main-actor Task

purpose: Packages a built 'Droppy Code.app' into the styled installer DMG: stages the app plus an /Applications symlink, the pre-baked window background, .DS_Store and volume icon, builds a UDRW image, sets the volume custom-icon Finder flag, then converts to a compressed ULMO image. Signing and notarization stay with release.sh.
state_owned: VOLNAME="Droppy Code"
APP_BUNDLE_NAME="$VOLNAME.app"
WORK_DIR from mktemp -d /tmp/droppy-code-dmg-XXXX
IFS=$'\n\t'
side_effects: Creates and (via trap cleanup EXIT) removes a /tmp work dir, force-detaching any still-mounted volume
ditto copies the app bundle into the stage; ln -s /Applications creates the drop target; copies .background.tiff and .VolumeIcon.icns
Mounts the RW image at $WORK_DIR/mnt with -nobrowse -noverify, writes .DS_Store onto the live volume, sets the FinderInfo xattr, detaches
rm -f then writes $OUTPUT_PATH; prints 'Styled DMG packaged at $OUTPUT_PATH'
platform_assumptions: Entirely macOS: hdiutil, ditto, xattr, HFS+ filesystem, Finder .DS_Store and FinderInfo semantics, .icns volume icons
ULMO (LZMA) format is noted as supported since macOS 10.15, below Droppy Code's macOS 26 minimum
persisted_fields: Staged names: '/Applications' symlink, '.background.tiff', '.VolumeIcon.icns', '.DS_Store'
FinderInfo bytes written literally: '00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 04 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00' (finderFlags at byte offset 8, kHasCustomIcon = 0x0400)
ui_elements: Error strings go to stderr prefixed 'package_dmg: '; texts include 'Usage: --app <Droppy Code.app> --output <out.dmg>', 'App bundle must be named $APP_BUNDLE_NAME (got ...)', and 'The installer .DS_Store does not point its background at /Volumes/Droppy Code; re-bake it (see release/dmg/README.md)'
feature_notes: Only two flags are accepted, --app and --output; anything else errors with 'Unknown argument: $1'

Refuses to run unless the bundle's basename is exactly 'Droppy Code.app', because the baked .DS_Store keys icon positions and the background alias by that name, by volume 'Droppy Code' and by '/.background.tiff'

The .DS_Store is stored in the repo as base64 text (release/dmg/installer-DS_Store.base64) so git and code review treat it as source; it is decoded first so a bad asset fails in a second, not a minute, then grepped for '/Volumes/Droppy Code'
hdiutil create uses -format UDRW -fs HFS+; final conversion is -format ULMO, measured about 19% smaller than the previous maximum-zlib UDZO image
Detach retries up to 8 times with sleep 1 between tries before falling back to hdiutil detach -force
ditto is used rather than cp specifically to keep the bundle signature, extended attributes and stapled notarization ticket

state_owned: PROJECT="droppyformac1/droppy-code"
ENCODED_PROJECT="${PROJECT//\//%2F}" giving droppyformac1%2Fdroppy-code
VERSION from project.yml MARKETING_VERSION via sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*MARKETING_VERSION:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1
TAG="v$VERSION"
DMG default "build.noindex/Droppy-Code-$VERSION.dmg"
NOTES from mktemp -t droppy-code-notes
ASSET_PATH="/Droppy-Code.dmg"
side_effects: Creates an annotated git tag v<version> on ${RELEASE_REF:-HEAD} with message 'Droppy Code <version>' and pushes it to origin
Creates a GitLab release via glab with asset label 'Droppy Code <version> (Apple silicon)' and --name 'Droppy Code <version>'
PUTs the release asset link with name, direct_asset_path=/Droppy-Code.dmg and link_type=package
Runs scripts/deploy_site.sh, which deploys the website to Netlify
Writes a temp notes file
platform_assumptions: Needs xcrun stapler (macOS notarization) and glab signed in as a maintainer; bash with set -euo pipefail
persisted_fields: GitLab project path and encoded path; release tag format v<MARKETING_VERSION>; asset direct_asset_path '/Droppy-Code.dmg'
ui_elements: step() prints a blank line then '==> <title>' for: 'Checking every contributor is thanked', 'Checking the disk image is notarized', 'Tagging $TAG', 'Creating the release', 'Pointing the latest-download permalink at it', 'Checking the permalink', 'Rebuilding the changelog and deploying the site'

Failure strings: 'No ## [$VERSION] section in CHANGELOG.md. Add one before publishing.', 'No disk image at $DMG. Run scripts/release.sh first.', 'No release notes at $NOTES.', '$NOTES needs at least one of the three headings: ## New features, ## Bug fixes, ## Refinements.', 'Release $TAG already exists on GitLab.'
Final line: 'Published: https://gitlab.com/<project>/-/releases/<tag>'
feature_notes: Accepts one optional positional argument, the DMG path
Notes must contain at least one of '## New features', '## Bug fixes', '## Refinements' (grep -qE '^## (New features|Bug fixes|Refinements)')

Credits gate: python3 scripts/release_credits.py --check "$NOTES" must pass, otherwise it prints 'Add a ### Thanks section to the ## [$VERSION] entry in CHANGELOG.md naming them (python3 scripts/release_credits.py prints it), then publish again.' and exits 1

The permalink is https://gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code/-/releases/permalink/latest/downloads/Droppy-Code.dmg; the link id is found by picking the first asset link whose url lowercases to a .dmg suffix, via an inline python3 -c one-liner
A comment notes GitLab insists on a name or url in every link update, so the name rides along with the direct_asset_path change
RELEASE_REF env var moves the tag off HEAD when the version bump landed on main from elsewhere
The permalink check is curl -sIL ... | grep -i "content-disposition"

purpose: The developer inner loop: builds the Debug configuration as 'Droppy Code Dev', installs it as the single /Applications copy with an atomic swap, preserves the Xcode Development signature so macOS TCC approvals survive, quits the running Dev app (waiting out an in-flight Hydra merge) and relaunches it.
state_owned: APP_NAME="Droppy Code Dev"
DERIVED="build.noindex/dev"
PRODUCT="$DERIVED/Build/Products/Debug/$APP_NAME.app"
TARGET="/Applications/$APP_NAME.app"
side_effects: Builds into build.noindex/dev (xcodebuild output piped through tail -n 5)
Removes $TARGET.old, moves the running bundle aside, ditto-installs the fresh build, removes the .old copy
Strips com.apple.quarantine when the signature verifies, otherwise ad-hoc re-signs
Quits the app via osascript with a 300 second AppleScript timeout, then polls ps for up to 300 seconds
Optionally runs scripts/sync_dev_data.sh, then open "$TARGET", sleep 4 and prints up to 3 matching ps lines
platform_assumptions: macOS only: xcodebuild, ditto, codesign, xattr, osascript, open, plus LaunchServices/Spotlight behaviour
Relies on Xcode's Development signature and Team NARHG44L48 so macOS TCC keeps granted permissions
persisted_fields: Debug bundle id iordv.droppycode.dev; Dev data root ~/.droppy-code-dev; env var DROPPY_DEV_SYNC (default '0', '1' enables the mirror)
ui_elements: step() headers: 'Building $APP_NAME (Debug)', 'Installing the single copy to $TARGET', 'Relaunching', 'Mirroring the release app's data into $APP_NAME'
feature_notes: A Debug build is a separate app 'Droppy Code Dev' with its own library, settings, keychain items and worktrees, never touching the release app's

Builds under build.noindex on purpose: the '.noindex' suffix keeps Spotlight and Launchpad from listing the build folder as a second copy of the app; there must only ever be one dev app at /Applications/Droppy Code Dev.app

The re-sign policy is documented as a fix: ad-hoc re-signing every build gave a new identity with no Team ID and macOS forgot all TCC approvals, so ad-hoc is only a fallback when codesign --verify fails
Explicitly noted as safe to run from an agent inside Droppy Code itself: quitting may interrupt the calling session but the script keeps going and the fresh build picks up the changes on relaunch
The 300-iteration quit wait exists because the app holds its quit while a Hydra merge is going out, up to four minutes

plutil -extract status raw - and -extract id raw -

NOTARY_PROFILE="${NOTARY_PROFILE:-Droppy-Notarize}"
APP_NAME="Droppy Code"
BUILD="$ROOT/build.noindex"
ARCHIVE="$BUILD/DroppyCode.xcarchive"
EXPORT="$BUILD/export"
DMG="$BUILD/Droppy-Code-$VERSION.dmg"
VERSION from project.yml MARKETING_VERSION
side_effects: rm -rf then recreates build.noindex
Writes $BUILD/ExportOptions.plist, $BUILD/archive.log, $BUILD/export.log, $BUILD/DroppyCode.zip
Submits the app zip and the DMG to Apple notarization and staples both
Signs the DMG with the resolved Developer ID Application identity and --timestamp
Removes the archive, export dir, DroppyCode.zip and DerivedData at the end, leaving only the DMG
platform_assumptions: macOS plus Xcode and XcodeGen; Apple notarization service; Gatekeeper (spctl); Apple silicon only build (ARCHS=arm64, EXCLUDED_ARCHS=x86_64, ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO)
persisted_fields: ExportOptions.plist keys: method=developer-id, teamID=NARHG44L48, signingStyle=manual, signingCertificate='Developer ID Application'
DMG filename pattern Droppy-Code-<MARKETING_VERSION>.dmg under build.noindex
ui_elements: step() headers: 'Generating the Xcode project', 'Archiving $APP_NAME $VERSION', 'Exporting with Developer ID', 'Verifying the signature', 'Notarizing the app', 'Building the disk image', 'Notarizing the disk image', 'Checking Gatekeeper', 'Cleaning up'
notarize() prints 'Notarization accepted for <basename>'
Final message: 'Ready: <dmg>' then 'Publish it with scripts/publish_release.sh once CHANGELOG.md has a ## [<version>] section.'
Architecture failure text: 'Expected an Apple silicon binary, got: <archs>'
feature_notes: notarize() parses notarytool JSON with plutil -extract status raw -, and on anything other than 'Accepted' prints the JSON, fetches the log by id and exits 1
Signature gate greps codesign -dv --verbose=4 output for 'Authority=Developer ID Application', 'flags=.*runtime' (hardened runtime) and 'Timestamp='
On archive failure it prints the first 40 'error:' lines from archive.log, otherwise the last 40 lines; export failure prints tail -40 of export.log

Gatekeeper checks: spctl --assess --type execute on the app and --type open --context context:primary-signature on the DMG, both with --ignore-cache --no-cache --verbose, then xcrun stapler validate on the DMG
The signing identity is resolved from security find-identity with sed -nE matching 'Developer ID Application: ... (NARHG44L48)', taking the first match
'.noindex' is chosen so Spotlight and Launchpad never list the build copies of the app, and the cleanup step is justified the same way
The build archives with -skipPackagePluginValidation and -skipMacroValidation

purpose: Lists every outside contributor whose work merged since the previous v* tag, by joining git log authors and Co-authored-by trailers against GitLab merged merge requests, and prints the '### Thanks' block; with --check <notes-file> it is the gate publish_release.sh uses to refuse publishing until each contributor is named.
calls_into: git log / git tag --points-at HEAD / git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match v* / git merge-base --is-ancestor
state_owned: PROJECT = 'droppyformac1/droppy-code'
ENCODED_PROJECT = 'droppyformac1%2Fdroppy-code'
MAINTAINER_USERNAMES = {'droppyformac'}
MAINTAINER_EMAILS = {'jordylegrand@gmail.com', 'droppyformac@gmail.com'}
IGNORED_EMAIL_SUFFIXES = ('@anthropic.com', '@users.noreply.github.com', '@localhost')
by_user / by_email dicts of entries {name, handle, mrs, subjects}
side_effects: Runs git and glab subprocesses in ROOT (read-only)
Prints the '### Thanks' block, a JSON array with --json, or the missing lines with --check; exit codes 0, 1 or 2
platform_assumptions: Needs python3, a git checkout with v* tags, and glab on PATH for MR data (failures fall back to an empty MR list, degrading to commit-only credits)
persisted_fields: --json object keys: name, handle, merge_requests (list of {iid, title}), subjects (list of str), printed with indent=2, ensure_ascii=False
MR fields read from GitLab: iid, title, author.username, author.name, squash_commit_sha, merge_commit_sha, sha
ui_elements: Prints the literal heading '### Thanks'
suggested_line formats: '- {name} (@{handle}): {title} (!{iid}); ...' when the entry has MRs and a handle, '- {name}: {titles}.' without a handle, '- {name}: {subjects}.' when only commit subjects
Warning line on stderr: 'Warning: !{iid} ({title}) is not mentioned in the Thanks section.'
'Missing from the Thanks section:' header followed by one suggested line per missing contributor
'No outside contributors since {tag}.' on stderr, or '[]' with --json
feature_notes: previous_tag(): if project.yml's MARKETING_VERSION tag v<version> already points at HEAD, it describes from HEAD^ instead, so a tagged bump does not credit against itself
commits_in_range uses git log --no-merges with format %H%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%s%x1f%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly), splitting on \x1f and padding to 5 fields
COAUTHOR_RE = (.+?)\s*<([^<>]+)>\s* parses each Co-authored-by trailer into name and email
merged_requests matches MRs by squash_commit_sha, merge_commit_sha or sha against the range's shas, falling back to merged_in() which tests ancestry against HEAD and origin/main but not the tag

MAINTAINER_USERNAMES filtering drops the maintainer's own MRs; ignored_email drops maintainer emails and anything ending in @anthropic.com, @users.noreply.github.com or @localhost, so Claude co-author trailers and GitHub noreply addresses never appear
Commit subjects are only recorded for commits NOT linked to a matched MR, so an MR contributor is credited by title and a direct committer by subject
Email entries are folded into a user entry when the display names match case-insensitively
Entries sort by lowest MR iid (MR-less entries last, float('inf')) then by lowercased name; each entry's mrs sort by iid

check_notes finds the section under a line whose strip() is exactly '## Thanks' or '### Thanks' and stops at the next line starting with '#'; a contributor counts as named if '@handle' or the name appears case-insensitively in it
CLI: --since <tag> / --since=<tag>, --json, --check <file> / --check=<file>; anything else prints 'Unknown argument: {arg}' to stderr and returns 2
--check returns 0 immediately when there are no outside contributors at all
unresolved_questions: check_notes takes a `tag` parameter it never uses.
When glab is missing or the API call fails, merged_requests silently returns [] and credits degrade to commit-based entries with no visible warning.

purpose: One-way mirror of the released Droppy Code's data into Droppy Code Dev: quits Dev, rsyncs the Application Support library, copies the user defaults domain, and re-adds four named API keys into the Dev keychain service, never writing to the release side.
state_owned: RELEASE_NAME="Droppy Code"
DEV_NAME="Droppy Code Dev"
RELEASE_LIB="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Droppy Code"
DEV_LIB="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Droppy Code Dev"
RELEASE_DOMAIN=iordv.droppycode
DEV_DOMAIN=iordv.droppycode.dev
DEV_APP="/Applications/Droppy Code Dev.app"
side_effects: Quits Droppy Code Dev and polls ps for up to 20 seconds
rsync -a --delete from the release library into the Dev library (destructive on the Dev side)
defaults delete on the Dev domain then defaults export <release> - piped into defaults import <dev> -
security add-generic-password -U into service 'Droppy Code Dev' with -T "$DEV_APP" -T /usr/bin/security for each key found
Counts threads with find "$DEV_LIB/threads" -name '*.json'
platform_assumptions: macOS only: ~/Library/Application Support, cfprefsd defaults domains, the login keychain via security, osascript
A comment notes macOS may ask once per key to let `security` read the release item and advises choosing Always Allow
persisted_fields: Keychain service names 'Droppy Code' (read) and 'Droppy Code Dev' (write)
Keychain accounts mirrored, in order: 'DeepSeek API Key', 'Meta API Key', 'Z.ai API Key', 'Command Code API Key'
Defaults domains iordv.droppycode and iordv.droppycode.dev
Library subfolder 'threads' holding *.json thread files
Worktree roots ~/.droppy-code (release) and ~/.droppy-code-dev (Dev)
ui_elements: step() headers: 'Quitting $DEV_NAME', 'Mirroring the library', 'Mirroring settings', 'Mirroring API keys'

Messages: 'No release library at $RELEASE_LIB; nothing to mirror.' (exit 0), '<n> threads mirrored', 'No release settings yet.', two-space-indented '  <account>' per key, '<n> keys mirrored', 'No API keys in the release keychain.', and the closing 'Droppy Code Dev now mirrors Droppy Code. Worktrees stay separate (~/.droppy-code vs ~/.droppy-code-dev).'
feature_notes: Explicitly one-way: nothing is ever written to the release library, defaults domain or keychain items
Dev's own changes since the last mirror are replaced, so Dev opens on the real data as of that moment
Head worktrees and patches under ~/.droppy-code are left alone; Dev keeps its own under ~/.droppy-code-dev
Exits 0 (not an error) when there is no release library to mirror
Invoked by quick_run.sh only when DROPPY_DEV_SYNC=1
unresolved_questions: Only these four API-key accounts are mirrored; whether the app stores other keychain accounts that are deliberately left behind cannot be told from this file.

DroppyCode/App/Captures/TourCaptures.swift and TourCaptures+Hydra.swift (the capture mode this drives)

ui_elements: Every tour picture is exactly 1320x824 (16:10) after fit()
interior() insets 8 points from the window edges so the tour card's own rounded corners do not draw a second, tighter corner inside the window's
theme_mosaic(): 2x2 tiles with a 6 px gap on background (16, 16, 20), tile_w = (1320-6)//2 = 657, tile_h = (824-6)//2 = 409
feature_notes: WINDOW_SIZES in points: tour-welcome and web-hero 1280x800; tour-hydra, tour-pairs, tour-slider, tour-threads, tour-recipes 960x600; tour-panels 1280x800; tour-window 660x600; web-diff, web-palette, web-plans, web-question, web-queue, web-intro 1200x660; every tour-theme-* and web-theme-* 960x600
window_box grows the window by 72 pt per side (w+144, h+144) then widens or heightens to exactly 1.6 aspect

focus_box: pad = max(40, 0.12 * max(fw, fh)); the padded focus is grown about its centre to the 1320/824 aspect; never narrower than min_share 0.55 of the inside width; shifted (never shrunk) to lie inside; returns the whole inside when there is no focus or the inside cannot hold the box

When a focus cannot fit the window (the cookbook's popover is taller than the window it hangs from) frame() re-cuts around the focus within the whole still, so the page shows the popover entire beside the window rather than clipped at its edge
Per-scene log line: '  <name>: focus' or '  <name>: whole window' plus the rounded box tuple
fit() centre-crops to the target aspect only when the aspect differs by more than 1e-9, then resizes with Image.LANCZOS
encode() exits with 'The capture run wrote no <source>.png; see <captures>/run.log' when a scene is missing
Capture-mode budget is 630 seconds; overrun prints '  the run overran its budget and was killed'
--website, --export-only and --upload delegate to website_captures.encode_tour()/upload_tour(); --export-only skips build, capture and encode entirely
The comment records that the old path (cropped WebP into website/assets/app/tour/) was removed so only one uploader writes the R2 tour keys
The welcome page is deliberately its own scene: the whole window with the sidebar open and no popover, so the first page is the overview and not the hero's close-up

SCENES is defined but never referenced; encode() uses its own inline (name, source) pair list instead.
The 'from PIL import Image, ImageDraw' inside fit() and encode() imports ImageDraw without using it.

porting/source_inventory.json flags both files with inclusion_evidence 'may supply runtime content (changelog/update feed) - must be checked'. Checked: porting/spec/UPDATE.json (PR-UPDATE-005/018/019 and neighbors) documents the update feed as one unauthenticated GET to the GitLab releases API (https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/86415974/releases), and on Windows (OD-0008 C6, OD-0012 I1) that feed value is an internal, empty-by-default setting with no network call at all until the owner supplies one; nothing in that flow fetches getdroppycode.app, favicon.ico or og-home.png. The only other appearances of the getdroppycode.app domain in the spec (porting/spec/UPDATE.json and SETTINGS.json) are plain-text attribution strings in the About/Credits card ('Based on Droppy Code by Jordy Spruit (Droppy), https://getdroppycode.app'), not fetches of this asset. So the flag resolves to 'no': this file supplies no app runtime content.

feature_notes: The header comment lists everything deliberately DROPPED from Droppy's original changelog styles because there is nothing to wear them on this page: the frame-sequence hero (.changelog-scrub), the light-paper hero ink override, the nightly/beta/iOS/playground/droppykit channel variants and the .is-nightly/.is-beta/.is-ios rules, the channel note, entry actions, TestFlight, galleries, video, image, lightbox, whatsnew label, and the per-platform float-icon faces. Only the stable channel ships.

Release entries are a two-column grid: the left column (date plus display title) pins with position: sticky at top 108px while the right column's notes scroll past, 'like a product-blog changelog' per the comment.

Stable pill animation: two absolutely positioned overlay layers that only ever change opacity, running on two different periods (5.4s and 7.1s) 'so the pill breathes unevenly rather than pulsing in unison'. channel-breathe-a goes 0.55 at 0%/100% and 1 at 50%; channel-breathe-b goes 1 at 0%/100% and 0.5 at 50%.

Stable droplet streams: ::before background-image is radial-gradient(circle at 7px 4px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.90) 0 0.8px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 2px) plus radial-gradient(circle at 14px 13px, rgba(219, 231, 255, 0.75) 0 0.6px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 1.6px), background-size 20px 20px, animation stable-drizzle-a 4.2s linear infinite. ::after is radial-gradient(circle at 4px 12px, rgba(219, 231, 255, 0.80) 0 0.7px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 1.8px) plus radial-gradient(circle at 16px 5px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.70) 0 1px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 2.3px), background-size 24px 24px, background-position 8px 0, animation stable-drizzle-b 5.4s linear infinite.

Seamlessness rule: each drizzle keyframe scrolls its repeating tile by exactly one tile height downward, in px so a seam is impossible at any rounding. stable-drizzle-a goes from background-position 0 -20px to 0 0; stable-drizzle-b goes from 8px -24px to 8px 0. Comment: 'the loop is seamless and no droplet ever pops or respawns'.

prefers-reduced-motion: reduce kills both pill overlay animations and pins them at opacity 0.9, and flattens .clog-float-icon__face to scale(var(--face-scale, 1)) with filter none and a 320ms opacity-only transition, keeping the dissolve and dropping the movement.
The marker dot takes its channel's colour, #1e40af for stable, 'so the row reads as one thing'.

Comment on .changelog-entry__version: the headline above is the human name for the release, the version is the exact build string kept for support and bug reports, 'the thing you paste into a post', so it stays literal and stays quiet.
Comment: stable is royal blue on purpose because it is the tier the download button gives you.

The single .clog-float-icon carries only one face, the Droppy Code artwork; it cross-dissolves with a little scale and blur on hand-off between entries so the icon reads as gliding down the page rather than being swapped.

The comment for .scrub-frost says Droppy's halo is paper-coloured for its light art, while here it is canvas-coloured (rgba(11, 14, 20, ...) matches --bg-top #0b0e14) for the dark page, and one class on the copy group covers kicker, title and subtitle at once.
unresolved_questions: The markup that pairs with these classes lives in website/changelog.html, which is not in this bundle, so the exact user-visible strings for .changelog-state__title, .changelog-state__text and the .changelog-more toggle label cannot be determined from this file.
--face-scale is consumed with fallback 1 but never declared here; the script that positions .clog-float-icon must set it per face, and that script is not in this bundle.

.changelog-entry.is-stable is the only channel state class kept, but whether the page script can still emit other is-* channel classes (which would then fall through to the :root defaults) cannot be established from CSS alone.

.scrub-frost's exclusion selector references .e2ee and .board-tools; neither class is defined in this file or in site.css, so they look like leftovers from the upstream Droppy page, but that cannot be confirmed from this bundle.
.changelog-hero .hero__kicker-mark sets filter: none to undo a recolor, but the original filter is not in this file (it lived in Droppy's inline block), so what it undid is not recoverable here.

purpose: The single shared design system stylesheet for the whole Droppy Code marketing site. Header comment: 'A dark port of the getdroppy.app design system: the same notch dock, pills, reveal motion, highlight rail, FAQ and footer, re-tokened for a deep code-editor canvas and the blue of the Droppy Code icon. The binary field and the tile system are new and live at the bottom.' Explicitly no build step, one stylesheet, one page.

Status tokens: --color-success #3fd08a, --color-error #ff6b6b, --color-warning #fbbf24
Intentionally invisible: --border-subtle transparent, --border-strong transparent, --shadow-card none
Radii: --radius-sm 8px, --radius-md 12px, --radius-lg 16px, --radius-xl 24px, --radius-2xl 16px, --radius-3xl 24px, --radius-full 999px

Fonts: --font-sans "Inter", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; --font-display "Instrument Sans", "Inter", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; --font-mono ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

Type scale: --text-xs 0.75rem, --text-sm 0.875rem, --text-base 1rem, --text-lg 1.125rem, --text-xl 1.25rem, --text-2xl 1.5rem, --text-3xl 1.875rem, --text-4xl 2.25rem, --text-5xl 3rem, --text-6xl 3.75rem
Layout: --container-width 1120px, --container-pad 24px (18px under 480px), --gap-heading 48px described as 'the one distance between a section's heading block and what follows it'

Nav geometry: --nav-safe-top env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px), --nav-dock-bar-height 8px, --nav-dock-closed-height 56px (54px under 720px), --site-hero-nav-gap 104px (58px under 720px), --site-hero-content-start calc(var(--nav-safe-top) + var(--nav-dock-bar-height) + var(--nav-dock-closed-height) + var(--site-hero-nav-gap))
Motion: --ease-out cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), --ease-out-soft cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), --dur-fast 150ms, --dur-base 300ms, --dur-slow 600ms

Nav dock intro tokens in a second :root block: --nav-dock-duration 640ms, --nav-dock-curve cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1), --nav-dock-intro-delay 120ms, --nav-dock-collapsed-transform translateY(-6px) scaleX(0.78), --nav-dock-collapsed-blur blur(8px), --nav-dock-fade-duration calc(var(--nav-dock-duration) * 0.55), --nav-dock-exit-curve cubic-bezier(0.32, 1, 0.36, 1)

Component-local properties: --notch-bar; --notch-fillet 24px; --notch-fillet-inset 0px (becomes var(--notch-fillet) under the border-shape @supports); --pill-pad-right 7px (10px under 720px); --pill-pad-left 12px (14px under 720px, 12px under 380px)

Morph properties: --morph-dur 340ms, --morph-ease cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), --morph-blur 16px (11px on .footer__cta, .btn--sm and .nav__cta), --morph-tap-dur 620ms, --morph-mark-size default 20px, 26px on .btn--applepill and .btn--darkpill, 17px on footer/sm/nav CTAs
Rail properties: --highlight-card-width min(820px, calc(100vw - 48px)); --highlight-page-gutter max(24px, calc((100vw - 1240px) / 2 + 24px))
--reveal-delay, read with fallback 0ms on .reveal but never set here
side_effects: No JavaScript in this file. It does declare animations that run forever: hero-charge-sheen 3.2s linear infinite and bit-twinkle 4.5s ease-in-out infinite across 12 staggered spans

body background-image embeds an inline data:image/svg+xml grain texture, width 160 height 160, filter id='n' with feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.85' numOctaves='2' stitchTiles='stitch' and feColorMatrix tinting to 0.75 / 0.82 / 0.95 at alpha 0.035, background-repeat repeat. Comment: 'The same whisper of grain as the Droppy site, inverted for the dark canvas so it lifts rather than dirties.'

.hero__charged-sheen embeds a second inline data:image/svg+xml, width 240 height 64 viewBox 0 0 240 64, four copies of the bolt path 'M12 2 4 30h9l-3 22 12-30h-9z' filled %23ffffff at fill-opacity .6, translated to (20 4), (80 4), (140 4), (200 4), each with scale(1.1)
Selection, drag and long-press are suppressed site-wide; the comment says the scripts back this up by swallowing copy, cut, drag and the context menu
platform_assumptions: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) drives --nav-safe-top: an iOS/iPadOS Safari safe-area concept used to push the fixed nav below a device notch

--font-mono is ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace, an Apple-only stack with no Windows fallback; the header comment says 'Code inside the chips uses the Mac's own SF Mono; nothing else is imported', so on Windows the generic monospace would be used
-webkit-backdrop-filter paired with backdrop-filter on .glass and .btn--darkpill targets WebKit/Safari first
-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%, -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased and -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale; the grayscale smoothing hint is macOS-specific
-webkit-touch-callout: none, -webkit-user-drag: none and -webkit-user-select: none are Safari/iOS specifics used for the anti-copy lockdown
-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch on .showcase-highlights__rail is an iOS Safari momentum-scroll hint, alongside a ::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none } rule
border-shape: shape(...) sits behind @supports as progressive enhancement over the two radial-gradient fillet pseudo-elements; it is a very new CSS feature likely only in Safari at the pinned commit
min-height: 100dvh, aspect-ratio, overflow-x: clip, text-wrap: balance / pretty, grid-template-rows 0fr animation and the [inert] attribute selector all require a modern engine
The .hero__apple glyph and the .btn--applepill CTA assume a Mac download is the primary action
ui_elements: .skip-link: fixed at top calc(var(--nav-safe-top) + 12px), left 50%, z-index 101, padding 10px 16px, border-radius var(--radius-md), background var(--text-primary), color var(--ink), font-size var(--text-sm), weight 600; hidden at transform translate(-50%, -160%) and slid to translate(-50%, 0) on :focus-visible with transition var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out)
Global focus ring: outline 3px solid var(--accent) with outline-offset 3px; inside .nav the outline-color becomes #7ab8ff
::selection: background var(--accent-soft-strong), color #fff
.container: max-width var(--container-width), margin-inline auto, padding-inline var(--container-pad); .visually-hidden uses the 1x1 clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0) pattern
section: position relative, padding-block clamp(40px, 6vw, 80px); .section-tight is identical

.section-heading: "Inter Tight" then var(--font-display), weight 600, letter-spacing -0.045em, line-height 1.05, font-size clamp(2.25rem, 5.5vw, 3.25rem), centered, margin-bottom 18px, text-wrap balance
.section-subtitle: font-size clamp(1.05rem, 2.2vw, 1.25rem), color var(--text-tertiary), line-height 1.45, max-width 720px, centered, text-wrap pretty
.surface-well: background var(--bg-well), border-radius var(--radius-3xl)

.reveal: opacity 0 with translateY(24px), transition opacity and transform over var(--dur-slow) var(--ease-out) with transition-delay var(--reveal-delay, 0ms); .is-visible restores opacity 1 and translateY(0); .is-settled sets transform none and transition none; prefers-reduced-motion sets transition-duration 1ms and transform none

.nav: fixed at top var(--nav-safe-top), left/right 0, z-index 100, flex centered, pointer-events none; .nav::before paints a var(--notch-ink) bar at top calc(-1 * var(--nav-safe-top) - 1px) with height calc(var(--nav-safe-top) + var(--notch-bar) + 2px)

.nav__pill: pointer-events auto, flex, gap 10px, width fit-content, height 56px, margin-top var(--notch-bar), padding 6px calc(var(--pill-pad-right) + var(--notch-fillet-inset)) 6px calc(var(--pill-pad-left) + var(--notch-fillet-inset)), border-radius 0 0 var(--radius-xl) var(--radius-xl), background var(--notch-ink), max-width calc(100% - 2 * var(--notch-fillet) + 2 * var(--notch-fillet-inset))

.nav__pill::before/::after fillets: 24px wide, height calc(var(--notch-fillet) + var(--notch-bar)), at top calc(-1 * var(--notch-bar)); ::before is left calc(-1 * fillet + 1px) with radial-gradient(circle var(--notch-fillet) at 0 100%, transparent calc(fillet - 1px), var(--notch-ink) fillet); ::after mirrors it at right with at 100% 100%
.nav__logo: flex gap 8px, var(--font-display), weight 600, font-size var(--text-base), color var(--text-on-dark), margin-right 10px; its img height 24px, width auto, border-radius 6px

.nav__links: flex gap 22px, margin-right 8px; .nav__link font-size var(--text-sm), weight 500, color var(--text-on-dark-soft), white-space nowrap, transition color var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out); :hover and .is-active go to var(--text-on-dark); .nav__links[inert] gets pointer-events none
.btn.nav__cta: border-radius var(--radius-full), background var(--text-primary), color var(--ink); hover background #fff; active background #cdd5e1

.nav__menu hamburger: display none by default, 40x40px, border-radius 12px, transparent background, gap 4px; its three spans are 16x2px with border-radius 2px and background #e8eaed, transition transform 320ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1) and opacity 180ms ease; .nav__pill.is-open rotates span 1 to translateY(6px) rotate(45deg), sets span 2 opacity 0, rotates span 3 to translateY(-6px) rotate(-45deg)

@media (max-width: 720px) nav: pill width and max-width calc(100vw - 2 * fillet + 2 * fillet-inset - 8px), height auto with min-height var(--nav-dock-closed-height), flex-wrap wrap, column-gap 10px, row-gap 0; .nav__logo margin-right auto; .nav__menu display inline-flex; .nav__links order 5, flex-basis 100%, column, align-items stretch, gap 2px, max-height 0, opacity 0, overflow hidden, padding 0 4px, transitions max-height 560ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1), opacity 240ms ease, padding 560ms same curve; open state sets max-height 360px, opacity 1, padding 10px 4px 8px; .nav__link padding 13px 12px, border-radius 12px, font-size 15px, :active background rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)
@media (max-width: 380px): .nav__pill --pill-pad-left 12px, and .nav__logo span display none so only the mark remains

@keyframes navDockExpand: 0% opacity 0 with var(--nav-dock-collapsed-transform) and filter var(--nav-dock-collapsed-blur); 55% opacity 1; 100% opacity 1, transform translateY(0) scaleX(1), filter blur(0). Applied to .nav__pill with transform-origin 50% 0 and animation-fill-mode both

@supports border-shape: .nav__pill sets --notch-fillet-inset to var(--notch-fillet) and draws one path: from 0 0, arc to fillet fillet of fillet cw, vline to calc(100% - var(--radius-xl)), arc to calc(fillet + radius-xl) 100% of radius-xl ccw, hline to calc(100% - fillet - radius-xl), arc to calc(100% - fillet) calc(100% - radius-xl) of radius-xl ccw, vline to fillet, arc to 100% 0 of fillet cw, close; the two fillet pseudo-elements get content: none

.btn: inline-flex centered, gap 8px, height 44px, padding-inline 20px, border-radius var(--radius-lg), font-size var(--text-sm), weight 600, letter-spacing -0.01em, white-space nowrap, transitions background/color/border-color/transform over var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out); :active transform scale(0.97); .btn--sm height 38px with padding-inline 16px

.btn--applepill: gap 11px, background var(--text-primary), color var(--ink), border-radius 20px, padding 17px 28px, font-size 17px, weight 600, line-height 1.4; hover background #fff; active transform scale(0.98); .btn--applepill-logo 16x20px with margin-top -2px

.btn--darkpill: gap 11px, background var(--glass-bg-strong), color var(--text-primary), border-radius 20px, padding 16px 27px, font-size 17px, weight 600, line-height 1.4, backdrop-filter var(--glass-blur-soft); hover background rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); active scale(0.98); its svg is 16x16px

.btn-morph__face: inline-flex centered, gap inherit, transition opacity var(--morph-dur) linear and filter var(--morph-dur) var(--morph-ease); --rest starts opacity 1 blur(0); --hover is absolute inset 0, opacity 0, filter blur(var(--morph-blur)), pointer-events none

.btn-morph__mark inside the hover face: width and height var(--morph-mark-size, 20px), min/max sizing cleared, object-fit contain, flex none, align-self center, margin 0, position static, inset auto, opacity 1, transform none, transition none

@keyframes btn-morph-tap-out: 0% opacity 1 blur(0); 32% opacity 0 blur(var(--morph-blur)); 68% the same; 100% back to opacity 1 blur(0). btn-morph-tap-in is the mirror: 0% opacity 0 blurred, 32% opacity 1 blur(0), 68% the same, 100% opacity 0 blurred. btn-morph-dissolve: 0% blur(0) opacity 1; 45% blur(var(--morph-blur)) opacity 0.3; 100% blur(0) opacity 1
.hero: padding-top var(--site-hero-content-start), padding-bottom clamp(40px, 6vw, 80px), overflow visible; .hero__inner max-width 820px, centered, z-index 1

.hero__kicker: inline-flex gap 10px, "Inter Tight", font-size 20px, weight 500, letter-spacing -0.02em, line-height 1, color var(--text-primary), margin-bottom 30px; hover colour var(--accent-text) with the transition placed on the inner span and the arrow, not the link; .hero__kicker-mark height 22px, width auto, border-radius 6px; .hero__kicker-arrow 14x14px at opacity 0.55

.hero__title: "Inter Tight", weight 600, font-size clamp(2.5rem, 6.4vw, 3.9rem), letter-spacing -0.045em, line-height 1.02em, margin-bottom 26px, text-wrap balance; .hero__apple inline-block 0.72em x 0.88em, vertical-align -0.06em, margin-right 0.08em, fill currentColor; .hero__mac white-space nowrap
.hero__charged: position relative, inline-block, isolation isolate, color var(--accent-text)

.hero__charged-sheen: absolute inset 0, pointer-events none, color transparent, background-size 240px 100%, background-repeat repeat-x, background-clip text, opacity 0 (0.74 once settled). Its gradient layer is linear-gradient(105deg, rgb(255 138 61 / 18%) 0%, rgb(61 139 255 / 55%) 25%, rgb(52 196 106 / 60%) 40%, rgb(255 255 255 / 88%) 50%, rgb(163 91 224 / 60%) 60%, rgb(242 92 154 / 55%) 75%, rgb(43 181 176 / 18%) 100%)

.hero__charge-entry: absolute left calc(50% - 90px), bottom 45%, width 180px, height 100vh, overflow visible, pointer-events none, var(--font-mono), font-size 22px, weight 600, fill #ffb27a, opacity 0; its .dim children get fill #8cc4ff at fill-opacity 0.55
.hero__charged::after: inset -0.08em -0.12em, z-index -1, background radial-gradient(ellipse, rgb(255 138 61 / 30%), transparent 68%), opacity 0

@keyframes hero-charge-entry: 0% opacity 0 with clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0); 5% opacity 0.9; 12% opacity 1 with clip-path inset(0 0 0 0); 26% opacity 0.65; 55% opacity 0.18; 100% opacity 0. Runs 850ms linear with a 340ms delay, fill both
@keyframes hero-charge-arrival: 0% opacity 0 scale(0.65); 32% opacity 0.7; 100% opacity 0 scale(1.08). Runs 900ms ease-out with a 420ms delay, fill both
@keyframes hero-charge-sheen: background-position from 0 0 to 240px 0, running 3.2s linear infinite
.hero__subtitle: clamp(1.05rem, 2.4vw, 1.25rem), weight 400, letter-spacing -0.01em, line-height 1.45, color var(--text-primary) at opacity 0.62, max-width 760px, margin-bottom 34px, text-wrap pretty
.hero__actions: flex centered, gap 12px, flex-wrap wrap; at max-width 480px it becomes a full-width column with children at width 100% and justify-content center

.hero__droppy-link: inline-flex gap 8px, margin-top 26px, font-size var(--text-sm), weight 500, color var(--text-tertiary) going to var(--text-primary) on hover; its img 18x18px with border-radius 5px; its svg 14x14px with stroke currentColor, fill none, stroke-width 1.8, round caps and joins

.hero__field: absolute inset 0, z-index 0, pointer-events none, overflow hidden, mask-image linear-gradient(180deg, #000 0%, #000 55%, transparent 100%); its canvas is display block at 100% width and height

.hero__film aspect-ratio 16 / 10; .hero__video object-fit cover; .media-block position relative, max-width var(--container-width), border-radius var(--radius-3xl), overflow hidden, background var(--bg-well); .hero__media z-index 1, margin-top clamp(48px, 7vw, 84px)

.fcard: flex column, border-radius var(--radius-xl), background var(--bg-well), overflow hidden; .fcard__head padding 32px 32px 24px, gap 16px, flex 1 0 auto (24px 24px 18px under 720px); .fcard__title "Inter Tight" weight 600, letter-spacing -0.035em, clamp(1.5rem, 2.6vw, 1.875rem), margin 0 0 6px; .fcard__sub var(--text-base), color var(--text-secondary), max-width 46ch; .fcard__media aspect-ratio 16 / 10 on background var(--ink); .fcard__media--window also 16 / 10; media video and img are absolute inset 0 with object-fit cover

.showcase-highlights: width 100vw, margin-left calc(50% - 50vw), padding 0, overflow hidden; __head and __controls width min(100%, 1240px), margin-inline auto, padding-inline 24px (18px under 720px); __title "Inter Tight" clamp(2.3rem, 4.8vw, 4rem), weight 600, letter-spacing -0.05em, line-height 0.98; __sub margin 18px 0 0, clamp(1rem, 1.7vw, 1.2rem), line-height 1.5, white-space nowrap (normal under 720px)

.showcase-highlights__rail: grid-auto-flow column, grid-auto-columns var(--highlight-card-width), gap 20px (14px under 720px), margin-top var(--gap-heading), padding 0 var(--highlight-page-gutter) 10px, overflow-x auto with overflow-y hidden, scroll-padding-inline var(--highlight-page-gutter), scroll-snap-type x mandatory, scroll-behavior smooth, overscroll-behavior-inline contain, scrollbar-width none plus ::-webkit-scrollbar display none, cursor grab; .is-dragging sets scroll-snap-type none, scroll-behavior auto, cursor grabbing, user-select none

.highlight-card: min-width 0, scroll-snap-align start, scroll-snap-stop always, border-radius 32px (26px under 720px); its .fcard__head flex 1 0 auto with min-height 150px and padding 32px 36px 28px (min-height 0 and padding 24px 24px 20px under 720px); its title clamp(1.65rem, 2.7vw, 2.25rem); its sub max-width 52ch at clamp(0.98rem, 1.45vw, 1.08rem); its media flex 0 0 auto at 16 / 10

.showcase-highlights__controls: flex justify-content flex-end, gap 12px, margin-top 18px; .showcase-highlights__arrow 44x44px circle (40px under 720px), background rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08), color var(--text-primary), transitions transform/background 180ms var(--ease-out) and opacity 180ms ease; hover (not disabled) scale(1.06) with rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14); active scale(0.96); focus-visible outline 2px solid var(--accent) offset 3px; :disabled opacity 0.28 with cursor default; its svg 20x20px, fill none, stroke currentColor, round caps/joins, stroke-width 2.2

.tiles: grid repeat(6, minmax(0, 1fr)), grid-auto-rows minmax(260px, auto), gap 20px, margin-top var(--gap-heading); .tile position relative, overflow hidden, border-radius 40px, background var(--bg-well), padding 48px; spans are --wide 4 cols, --half 3, --tall 2 cols and 2 rows, --full 6
.tile--center: flex column centered, gap 28px; .tile__caption font-size 17px, color var(--text-secondary), max-width 44ch, text-wrap balance

.tile--trio: grid repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)), gap 24px, centered text; .trio__item flex column gap 18px; its svg 56x56px with fill none, stroke var(--text-primary), stroke-width 2.2, round caps/joins, and a .fill class inside that switches to fill var(--text-primary) with stroke none; .trio__label "Inter Tight" 600 at 22px, line-height 1.12, letter-spacing -0.03em

.tile--visual padding 0; .tile__art absolute inset 0 overflow hidden; .tile__overlay bottom-anchored with padding 120px 32px 32px and background linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(19, 24, 35, 0) 0%, rgba(19, 24, 35, 0.92) 55%, #131823 100%); overlay h3 and .tile__label are "Inter Tight" 600 at 24px, line-height 1.12, letter-spacing -0.03em; overlay p margin-top 8px, 14px, line-height 1.45, color var(--text-secondary), max-width 30ch

.tile--split: grid minmax(0, 0.95fr) minmax(0, 1.05fr), gap 24px, align-items center, min-height 300px; .tile__heading "Inter Tight" 600 at 30px, text-wrap balance, line-height 1.05, letter-spacing -0.035em; .tile__text margin-top 16px, 15px, line-height 1.5, color var(--text-tertiary), max-width 30ch, text-wrap pretty

.tile--film: flex column gap 10px with padding-bottom 0; its caption margin-bottom 22px and max-width 60ch; .tile__film block, width 100%, border-radius 24px 24px 0 0, margin-top auto; .tile--full.tile--film .tile__film border-radius 28px 28px 0 0

.tile__shot width min(520px, 100%) with border-radius 20px; .tile__art-img object-fit cover with object-position top left; .tile--plain flex column justify-center gap 14px with .tile__caption max-width 34ch and text-wrap pretty

.tile--fade: min-height 460px, padding 44px 44px 0, flex column, gap 26px; .tile__copy relative z-index 1 max-width 34ch; .tile__fade relative flex 1 min-height 240px pointer-events none; .tile__fade-img absolute top 0, width 96%, border-radius 18px 18px 0 0, mask-image linear-gradient(to bottom, #000 62%, transparent 100%); .tile--fade-right puts it at right -14%, .tile--fade-left at left -14%; under 720px min-height 0, padding-bottom 0, fade min-height 200px, image width 108%

.tile--agents: grid repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)), gap 40px 20px, margin-top var(--gap-heading), padding 56px 48px; .agent flex column centered gap 16px; .agent__mark 56x56px grid place-items center with color var(--text-primary); its svg 48x48px; .agent__name "Inter Tight" 600 at 22px with letter-spacing -0.03em (18px under 620px); .agents__note margin-top 26px, centered, 15px, color var(--text-tertiary); its code 13px on rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07) with padding 2px 7px and border-radius 6px

.tile--usage: grid minmax(0, 1.05fr) minmax(0, 0.95fr), gap 48px (32px under 960px), align-items center, margin-top var(--gap-heading); .usage__list grid gap 18px, margin 28px 0 0, list-style none; its strong "Inter Tight" 600 at 17px with letter-spacing -0.02em; its span 15px, line-height 1.5, color var(--text-tertiary), max-width 44ch, text-wrap pretty; .usage__shot width min(420px, 100%), border-radius 28px, justify-self center (justify-self start and min(360px, 100%) under 620px)

Tile breakpoints: @media (max-width: 960px) tiles become repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)) with grid-auto-rows auto and gap 16px, tile padding 36px and border-radius 32px, --wide/--half/--full span 2, --tall spans 2 with grid-row auto and min-height 460px, agents keep 5 columns at gap 32px 12px, usage gap 32px; @media (max-width: 620px) tiles become one column, tile padding 28px and border-radius 28px, all span modifiers go to grid-column auto, trio becomes one column at gap 32px, split becomes one column with min-height 0, .tile__rows margin 8px -28px 0 0, agents become repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)) with padding 36px 24px, usage becomes one column

.stats: grid repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)) with gap 14px and margin-top var(--gap-heading); 3 columns under 900px; 2 columns under 560px where .stat:last-child:nth-child(odd) spans 2. .stat padding 22px 12px 20px, centered; .stat__value "Inter Tight" 600 at clamp(1.6rem, 3vw, 2.1rem) with letter-spacing -0.04em and line-height 1; .stat__label margin-top 8px, 13px, color var(--text-tertiary)

.leftout: margin-top clamp(40px, 6vw, 80px) described as 'a second heading block inside the section: the same distance as between sections'; its .section-heading shrinks to clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 2.5rem); .leftout__list flex wrap centered, gap 8px 28px, margin-top var(--gap-heading), font-size clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.15rem), color var(--text-quaternary)

feature_notes: Site-wide anti-copy lockdown: body gets -webkit-user-select and user-select none plus -webkit-touch-callout none, and img and video get -webkit-user-drag none and pointer-events none. Comment: 'Nothing on the page is for taking: no text selection, no dragging a picture or a film off the page, no long-press sheet on a phone. The scripts back this up by swallowing copy, cut, drag and the context menu.' A follow-up comment notes the theme picker's names are buttons and the FAQ questions are buttons, so those keep their pointer events; only the media itself is inert.
html gets overflow-x: clip, -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% and scroll-behavior: smooth globally; body gets min-height 100dvh, line-height 1.6 and the grain background.

The nav dock springs open once per visit: the pill runs navDockExpand for 640ms on cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1) after a 120ms delay, starting collapsed at translateY(-6px) scaleX(0.78) with blur(8px), 'like the Droppy shelf (shelf curve + blur snapping into focus)'. A head-inline gate adds html.nav-intro-done on later loads so it never replays when navigating between pages; prefers-reduced-motion also sets animation: none. The comment states the tokens and keyframes are the getdroppy.app ones, unchanged.

The notch fillets are drawn twice: as radial-gradient pseudo-elements by default, and, where the browser supports border-shape: shape(...), as one border-shape path while ::before and ::after get content: none and --notch-fillet-inset becomes var(--notch-fillet) so the padding compensates.

Morph hover is 'the one hover every button on the site shares'. Two stacked content layers (a REST face and a HOVER face) are built at runtime by site.js so button markup stays plain; on hover the label dissolves through a thick gaussian blur where it stands and a fitting glyph blurs in, centred. The comment is emphatic in capitals: 'NOTHING SLIDES AND NOTHING RESIZES: the silhouette is identical at rest and hovered, only the content changes.'

Hover is gated behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) because 'on iOS Safari a synthesised hover would swallow the first tap'; touch gets the same morph from the .is-tapmorph class, which runs the 620ms tap-out and tap-in animations. .btn-morph--icon swaps faces; .btn-morph--label only runs the 340ms dissolve on its rest face.

Under prefers-reduced-motion the morph system removes the hover face entirely (display: none), cancels the label dissolve and both tap animations, keeps the rest face at opacity 1 with filter none, and falls back to .btn-morph:hover { opacity: 0.85 }.

The hero's charged word replays the choreography of 'Supercharged' on getdroppy.app: once the headline's reveal settles (.is-settled) a strike drops into the word from the top of the viewport over 850ms, an arrival bloom pulses once over 900ms, and a sheen keeps sweeping through the letters at 3.2s linear forever. The comment says Droppy's strike is a lightning bolt while here it is a stream of ones and zeros, and the sheen carries a row of digits instead of a bolt, although the embedded sheen SVG still draws four bolt paths.

Before the headline settles, .hero__title:not(.is-settled) hides the sheen, the charge entry and the ::after bloom with display: none; a will-change: opacity, transform compositing hint is held only while the shared reveal runs and is dropped to auto under reduced motion.

The binary field behind the hero is one canvas fixed to the hero's box, masked with linear-gradient(180deg, #000 0%, #000 55%, transparent 100%) 'so it melts into the page before the promo block'. The outro repeats the idea with radial-gradient(60% 70% at 50% 50%, #000 20%, transparent 100%).

Every tour still is a whole 16:10 frame, so .hero__film, .fcard__media, .fcard__media--window, .highlight-card .fcard__media and .wordscroll__demo-video all use aspect-ratio 16 / 10; the comments say a 16:9 or window-shaped box with cover cropped their edges, and .wordscroll__demo-video therefore uses object-fit contain so no bars and no crop.

The highlight rail is a full-bleed (100vw, margin-left calc(50% - 50vw)) horizontally scrolling, mandatory snap-stopped, drag-scrollable carousel with two round arrow buttons that disable at the ends at opacity 0.28 and cursor default; reduced motion turns off smooth scrolling and the arrow transitions.

The tile system is declared as the one card system: 'Every card on the page is a tile: a big-radius well with generous padding, one bold label, and either a large illustration or a visual that is allowed to bleed off the edge. Nothing else lives in a tile: no small icon chips, no key caps, no paragraphs under paragraphs.'

Picture tiles (.tile--fade) keep copy and capture apart: the copy sits at the top and the capture stands under it, running off the bottom and one side and fading out before the edge. Comment: 'Never under the words: the copy keeps its own band, the picture takes what is left.'

The FAQ list reads as a back-and-forth zig-zag: every question is a content-sized pill drawn by a ::before pseudo-element (so the round button can sit outside it on the page canvas and the row still works when a page ships the question as a bare text node), only every second one is pushed right with margin-left auto, and the answer card mirrors to the opposite side with a 28px accent dot in the side margin. Phones take the full-width pill back for both sides and hide the dots.

The FAQ answer opens with the grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr technique over var(--dur-base) 300ms, and the icon swaps its plus svg (hidden via visibility: hidden, so the circle keeps its size) for a 16x2px minus bar while filling with var(--accent).
The free and open-source card explicitly 'takes the pricing slot' and is centred 'as the pricing card on getdroppy.app is'.

The footer wordmark is a giant clipped word at rgba(232, 237, 245, 0.05) inside a fixed-height overflow-hidden box with will-change: transform and transform translateY(0.06em), implying a script-driven parallax translate.

The theme picker is one big window in the chosen theme plus the names to pick from, and lives inside the second wordscroll's demo slot. Its width is min(1040px, 86vw, calc(60vh * 2080 / 1426)) so that the window, its 26 names and the caption all fit the pinned stage together; the stage is at the same 2080 / 1426 aspect ratio.
The .wordscroll__bits binary twinkles are described as replacing Droppy's sparks.

Comments declare the intentional flat look: --border-subtle and --border-strong are transparent tokens kept only so rules can reference them ('Kept as tokens, intentionally invisible: flat look, no outlines'), and --shadow-card is none ('Disabled: flat look, no shadows, no glow effects').
unresolved_questions: Several classes are styled here but their markup lives in website/*.html and their behavior in website/assets/js/*, none of which are in this bundle: the .wordscroll__* mechanism (only __demo-video and __bits are styled here), the .hero__charge-entry inner SVG content, and the theme picker's 26 theme names.

.tile__rows has only a mobile override (margin 8px -28px 0 0 under 620px) and no base rule anywhere in this file, so its default layout must come from elsewhere or the base rule was dropped in the port.

--nav-dock-fade-duration and --nav-dock-exit-curve are declared in the second :root block but never referenced in this file; they may be consumed by site.js or be dead carry-over from getdroppy.app, and that cannot be decided from CSS alone.

Declared but unused in this file: --radius-2xl, --accent-hover, --accent-active, --accent-glow, --color-error, --color-warning, --surface-dark, --glass-border, --glass-border-strong, --shadow-card, --bg-bottom, --text-3xl, --text-4xl, --text-5xl, --text-6xl. Whether another stylesheet or script reads them is not determinable from this bundle.

.outro__icon-wrap::before is explicitly set to content: none, which suggests it cancels a glow from the upstream Droppy sheet; the original rule is not present here, so the intended appearance it removes cannot be recovered.

The header comment says the fonts are loaded in the page head, so the exact <link> or @font-face declarations are in the HTML, not this file. Notably "Inter Tight" is named first in many rules but is not part of --font-display, so whether it is actually requested cannot be confirmed here.

purpose: Stylesheet for the marketing site's pinned 'wordscroll' section: a 500vh tall dark slab whose sticky stage cross-fades scroll-lit headline copy into a product demo video, driven entirely by CSS custom properties that wordscroll.js writes. console.error('[changelog] failed to load changelog.json:', err) on a failed load

window.setTimeout(..., 680) after each glide to clear the transition and re-check the hand-off

Creates outbound links to https://gitlab.com/<handle> with target=_blank rel=noopener

Error state: title "Couldn't load the changelog", text "Check your connection and try again.", button.btn.btn--sm labelled "Try again" wired to loadChangelog

Group headings normalized through GROUP_LABELS: "new features" -> "New features", "bug fixes" -> "Bug fixes", "refinements" -> "Refinements", "updates" -> "Updates"; any other non-empty title passes through trimmed, an empty title becomes "Updates"

formatDate only rewrites a strict /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/ string, builds a local Date(year, month-1, day) to avoid a timezone day shift, and renders it as en-US { month: 'long', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' } (so "2026-07-06" -> "July 6, 2026"); anything else is passed through unchanged, and a non-string returns ""
Sorting is numeric per dot-separated segment with missing or NaN segments treated as 0, newest first, on a copy of the array (slice) so the fetched data is not mutated
Every entry is drawn as a stable release: the code comments say every entry on this page wears the one blue pill with the droplet glyph and the Stable label; release.platform is never read
Thanks strings are split on /@([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)/g and each captured handle becomes an <a class="changelog-thanks__handle"> with text "@handle" pointing at https://gitlab.com/<handle>

The floating icon picks its host slot by the entry whose rect straddles a line at 42% of the viewport height (vh * 0.42), otherwise the nearest entry by distance to that line

The hand-off is a FLIP glide: measure, reparent, then transform translate3d(dx,dy,0) with transition "transform 640ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1)" back to zero, re-armed after 680ms; under prefers-reduced-motion the icon reparents with no animation
initEntryIcon bails if there are no islots or a .clog-float-icon already exists, so the icon is created exactly once
Entries that are not objects are skipped; if nothing renders, the empty state shows

purpose: Page script for the Droppy Code marketing page: draws the scroll-scrubbed binary (0/1) canvas field behind the hero and outro, runs the horizontal highlight rail carousel (drag, arrows, keyboard, aria-current), and builds the theme picker that swaps one large real-app capture across 26 named themes on a 2600ms auto-cycle. Also keeps a deliberately empty initFilms() stub because the page is stills only now.

Attributes read: data-progress ('pagetop' or 'viewport'), data-scroll-span, data-density
Canvas 2D API, IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver, document.fonts.ready, Element.scrollTo, Pointer Events with setPointerCapture
Mirrors the app's AppTheme.swift theme identifiers
